## 概要

Phase 3 (#129) の safe-gh wrapper body を、P3-04 の配布機構 (#134 merged) の上に載せる **end-to-end 縦切り**。GitHub の Issue/PR/コメントを **untrusted data として安全に読む steering wrapper** を agent-tools body として実装し、`script` artifact kind で build/sync が両 tool home に配る。最初の実 script asset。

**強度ラベル(偽らない)**: これは **steering**。enforcement boundary ではなく、`$(gh ...)` 直実行 / `gh api` / `curl` / MCP github tool で迂回でき、hook も fail-open。hard な防御は床(credential 隔離 + egress)が担う。safe-gh が買うのは「安全な読み方を便利にし、untrusted content を data として扱わせる」こと。

## 設計(設計メモの 8 決定を実装)

- コマンド: `safe-gh [-R OWNER/REPO] <issue|pr> <view|comments> <number>`、出力は **JSON**
- **provenance 3 軸**で author を `self` / `bot` / `other` に分類。**bot を association より先に**評価(決定3、bot は association=NONE に化ける)。**self を確定できなければ全 other**(fail-closed)
- **他人の Issue/PR は metadata のみ**(number/state/author/labels)。**title すら親へ渡さない**(決定4、title は attacker 制御の free-text = injection 面)。本文も渡さない
- **他人コメントは count + 固定理由のみ**。著者名・プレビュー・untrusted 由来の文字列を出力に**一切混ぜない**(決定5)
- **自分の Issue/PR 本文・自分のコメントだけ** trusted として渡す
- self identity = `gh api user` 主体 + 任意 local override(`~/.config/dotfiles/github-trust.local`)。**public repo に numeric id をハードコードしない**

## 検証

- I/O(gh 呼び出し)と純粋な trust/render ロジックを分離。後者を fixture で **deterministic に検証**: self/other/bot 分類、本文除外、コメント count のみ、**untrusted 非漏洩(sentinel 文字列が出力に出ないことを assert)**。`scripts/tests/safe-gh-test.sh`、**10 self-test PASS**
- gh の実挙動は実機手動(docs「検証境界」)。**実機 smoke 済み**: self issue → title/body 含む、他人 issue(cli/cli #1)→ metadata のみ・本文非漏洩、comments、nonexistent → exit 1、`--help`/不正引数
- check-manifests/build/register/status/doctor が script kind を通し **registered**(両 target)。real repo 挙動: generated.total 26→28(safe-gh 2 本)

## スコープ

- 配備(`sync --apply` で実 home へ)は実機手動の別ステップ
- instruction での tool 誘導は body 実在後の follow-up(#129 P3-12)なのでこの PR では行わない(「無い tool 名を instruction に先に書かない」)

## レビュー

author = Claude。相互レビュー規約により reviewer = Codex (author ≠ reviewer)。security-critical な trust gating なので、**untrusted content の非漏洩**・**fail-closed 方向**・**bot/self/other 分類の穴**を重点的に。

author: basecradle-router-ai[bot]
body:
## What

The NOC (fleet "AI mechanic") holds a **wake-lock** while it converges (upgrades) an agent's harness, so the router does not land a wake on a half-installed venv. This adds the router's reader side of that interlock — the counterpart to **basecradle-noc#38**, which builds the writer side.

`WakeLockGuard` is checked in `Pipeline.execute`, **inside the per-agent lock and before the wake-rate breaker**, against the capital-pinned seam:

- **Lock file:** `/run/basecradle-noc/wake-locks/<slug>.lock` — root-owned, `/run` tmpfs (reboot clears stale locks). **Present = locked.**
- **Contents:** `{"agent","reason","acquired_at","expires_at"}` (ISO8601 TTL).

`<slug>` is the agent's `harness_key` (its OS-user slug) — the same key the per-agent lock and the breaker already serialize on.

## Decisions

The fail-direction is set by the asymmetry *corrupting a converge ≫ delaying a recoverable push* (the platform's read API is the source of truth; push is best-effort, so a refused wake only pauses the push):

| State | Outcome | Log |
|---|---|---|
| Absent | wake | — (silent; the common case) |
| Held (`now < expires_at`) | **refuse** | `event=wake_refused reason=wake_lock_held agent=<slug>` |
| Stale (`now >= expires_at`) | wake | `event=wake_lock_stale agent=<slug>` (wedged converge visible) |
| Unparseable (bad JSON / no `expires_at`) | **refuse** | `event=wake_refused reason=wake_lock_unparseable` |
| Unreadable (perms/OS fault) | wake (fail-open) | `event=wake_lock_unreadable` **ERROR** |

All lines ship to BetterStack Live Tail via the `AI` source (journald). Checked **before** the breaker so a NOC-quiesced agent never consumes breaker budget.

## Why it's safe to land first

Harmless with no locks present (no lock file → never refuses), so this deploys before the NOC starts writing locks — the ordering basecradle-noc#38 specifies. It is independent of the harness self-breaker and the wake-rate breaker: defense-in-depth, no shared protocol.

## Tests

`tests/test_wakelock.py` (guard, real temp dir + fake clock) and new pipeline integration tests cover every edge: held/stale/absent/unparseable/unreadable, the exact log shapes, exactly-at-expiry, `Z`-suffix and naive-timestamp tolerance, unsafe/NUL slugs, and that a held lock consumes no breaker budget. Offline, mocked at the boundary. 248 passing; `ruff` clean. Self-reviewed via `/code-review high` (two finder passes, clean; one hardening — `check()` made total against an embedded-NUL slug — applied).

Builds the router leg of #120; the handoff issue is closed by hand after live verification per the handoff procedure.

## What
Loosen watch-registry validation so adding a watch only requires a non-empty **ref** per ref-row. **Dial** and **strap** are now optional.

## Why
The old `_validate` rejected any ref missing dial or strap, forcing users to fill in details they may not know yet. Ref alone is enough to track a watch.

## Changes
- `webapp/flask/app.py` — `_validate` now requires only `ref` (error message updated)
- `webapp/flask/templates/index.html` — form label: "dial + strap optional"
- `webapp/flask/tests/test_app.py` — flipped `test_create_watch_no_valid_ref` to assert empty *ref* fails; added `test_create_watch_ref_without_dial_strap` for the new looser path

## Safety
Downstream `tag_deal` already uses `.get("dial")`/`.get("strap")` (None-tolerant), and the JS form already keeps any row with a ref — no other changes needed.

## Verification
`python3 -m pytest tests/ webapp/flask/tests/ -q` → **80 passed**

author: big-brick
body:
### Motivation

- Provide a way to detect and review XLSX rows whose DGM values differ from the database and allow interactive resolution.  
- Preserve catalog tree expansion/selection when the catalog view is refreshed to improve editor UX.  
- Improve preprocessing to match database letter-casing when appropriate and allow filling the Add dialog with initial DGM values.  

### Description

- Introduced a new module `dgm_gui_xlsx_conflicts.py` implementing `XlsxConflictsMixin` and `XlsxConflictReviewWindow` to collect, display and act on XLSX/database conflicts (clean row, update database, rename in XLSX), and added dependency checks for `openpyxl`.  
- Made `GuiConflictRow.Record` optional in `dgm_gui_common.py` to represent conflicts for names with no matching database record.  
- Extended `AddElementDialog` in `dgm_gui_dialogs.py` with an `InitialValues` parameter and prefill logic so the dialog can be initialized with DGM values.  
- Integrated the new conflicts feature into the main UI by importing `XlsxConflictsMixin` and adding menu buttons in `dgm_gui_main_window.py`, and increased the main window height for the extra buttons.  
- Updated `DgmDatabaseViewer` in `dgm_gui_database_viewer.py` to preserve expanded nodes and selected node across `_PopulateCatalogTree` calls via `_GetCatalogTreeState` and `_RestoreCatalogTreeState`.  
- Adjusted XLSX processing logic in `dgm_gui_xlsx_processor.py` to treat empty/zero sheet DGM cells as non-conflicting and only flag differences when non-zero sheet values differ from the DB.  
- Changed Excel write formatting helper in `dgm_xlsx_common.py` from `DecimalToExcelNumber` to `DecimalToExcelValue` using `dgm_database.DecimalToText`, and updated `WriteEntryToRow` to use it.  
- Improved preprocessing in `dgm_xlsx_preprocessor.py` by applying exact database casing when a database record with DGM exists and added `BuildExactDatabaseText` helper.  

### Testing

- No automated tests were added or executed as part of this change.

author: botoom
body:
## Resumen

Este PR introduce un pipeline completo de ingeniería y validación de features externas para la fase de preparación de datos del Modelo 2 (rendimiento). Integra las fuentes EcoCrop y FAO Calendar en el dataset de modelado EVA, agrega salvaguardas de validación y actualiza documentación y orquestación.

## Novedades

### 1. Ingeniería de Features de Cultivos Externos
- **Features EcoCrop**: emparejamiento jerárquico de cultivos EVA con registros oficiales de EcoCrop, extracción de rangos óptimos de temperatura, lluvia, pH, altitud y duración de ciclo.
- **Features FAO Calendar**: meses de siembra, duración de ciclo y regiones AEZ para cultivos con cobertura FAO.
- **Salida**: `calendar_for_eva.csv` (89 cultivos, 19 columnas) listo para hacer join con `eva_for_modeling.csv`.

### 2. Integración y Filtrado
- `03_integrate_crop_features.ipynb` / `.py` consolidan datos EcoCrop + FAO.
- Lógica de filtrado remueve 5 cultivos con datos externos insuficientes:
  - 4 `not_recommended_limited_data` (sin EcoCrop ni FAO)
  - 1 `recommended_for_validation_only` (solo FAO, sin EcoCrop)
- Genera `crop_features_log.json` y `crop_features_distributions.png`.

### 3. Pipeline de Validación
- `02_validate_crop_features.ipynb` / `.py` validan `calendar_for_eva.csv` contra `eva_for_modeling.csv`:
  - Unicidad de `cultivo_eva_normalizado`
  - Sincronía de universos con EVA (166 cultivos EVA vs 89 cultivos auxiliares finales)
  - Prevención de data leakage (sin columnas de producción/objetivo)
  - Nulos críticos
  - Check condicional de políticas FAO (omitido en dataset final por diseño)
  - Check condicional de confiabilidad (omitido por política Compute, Don't Store)
  - Coherencia de rangos ecológicos EcoCrop
  - Completitud de columnas
- Reporte generado: `crop_features_validation_report.json` con estado `WARNING` esperado.

### 4. Documentación y Orquestación
- Actualizados `README.md`, `02_external_data_integration.md`, `feature_engineering_report.md` y documentos de flujo de ejecución.
- Notebooks de feature engineering renombrados para iniciar desde `01`.
- Actualizadas referencias en `run_all_preparation.py`.
- Despliegue: actualizado a Python 3.12, perfiles de Docker agregados, dependencias modernizadas.

## Arquitectura

### Antes
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[EVA raw data] --> B[Cleaning]
    B --> C[Feature Engineering]
    C --> D[Modeling Dataset]
```

### Después
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[EVA raw data] --> B[Cleaning]
    B --> C[Feature Engineering]
    E[EcoCrop official] --> F[Match & Extract]
    G[FAO Crop Calendar] --> H[Extract sowing & duration]
    F --> I[calendar_for_eva.csv]
    H --> I
    C --> J[eva_for_modeling.csv]
    I --> K[Validation Pipeline]
    J --> K
    K --> L[Validation Report JSON]
    I --> M[LEFT JOIN]
    J --> M
    M --> D[Enhanced Modeling Dataset]
```

## Resultados de Validación

| Check | Estado |
|-------|--------|
| Unicidad | PASS |
| Sincronía de universos | WARNING (EVA tiene 166 cultivos, auxiliar final 89) |
| Data leakage | PASS |
| Nulos críticos | PASS |
| Política FAO | SKIP (columna no está en dataset final) |
| Rangos ecológicos | PASS |
| Confiabilidad | SKIP (columna no está en dataset final) |
| Completitud | WARNING (columnas FAO ~39% cobertura por diseño) |

**Estado global**: `WARNING` (esperado, debido al filtrado deliberado y cobertura parcial de FAO).

## Screenshot

Dashboard generado por el pipeline de integración:

![Crop features distributions](3_data_preparation/docs/modelo_2_rendimiento/03_integration/crop_features_distributions.png)

## Cómo Verificar

1. Ejecutar el script de validación:
   ```bash
   python 3_data_preparation/scripts/modelo_2_rendimiento/04_validation/02_validate_crop_features.py
   ```
2. Revisar el reporte generado:
   ```bash
   cat 3_data_preparation/data/processed/modelo_2_rendimiento/04_validation/crop_features_validation_report.json
   ```

## Notas

- No se sobrescriben archivos existentes en `main`; todos los cambios coexisten agregando nuevos scripts, notebooks y documentación.
- El estado `WARNING` de validación es intencional y documentado.
- El PR está listo para revisión y merge en `main`.

body:
## Summary
- Adds zoom in/out/reset controls to the Full Bracket view so more of the bracket (group stage, knockout, finals) fits in view at once instead of relying on horizontal scrolling.
- Changes the men's knockout round 2 pairing logic: Jorge vs Jason, Eric vs Ben, Bobby vs the Mo/Dylan winner, and Enrique vs the Clay/Keiler winner. Implemented by swapping which round-1 qualifier feeds each pod's seed slots, gated to the men's tournament only (`tournamentId === 'disc-golf-world-cup-2026'`) — the women's bracket is unaffected.

💡 What: Modified `list_runs` in `swarm/api/services/spec_manager.py` to use `os.scandir` instead of `Path.iterdir()`.

author: thad0ctor
body:
Tracking PR for upstream issue [axolotl-ai-cloud#3754](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/issues/3754).

## Problem
Gemma keeps `tokenizer.eos_token = <eos>`, which never appears in the rendered chat (turns end with `<end_of_turn>` on Gemma 1/2/3/3n or `<turn|>` on Gemma 4). The default `eot_tokens = [eos_token]` therefore misses the real terminator, so it's silently masked (`-100`) and never trained — the model never learns to stop. Loss/eval curves look healthy because the only thing not learned (stopping) is never in the loss.

## Fix (config-first, matching the maintainer's preferred approach)
- Set `eot_tokens` on every Gemma `chat_template` example that lacked it: `gemma2`, all `gemma4`, `gemma4-unified`, and the `qat_nvfp4` Math-Gemma3 configs. Existing `gemma3`/`3n` examples already set it.
- Skipped `gemma2/reward-model.yaml` — the Bradley-Terry strategy emits scalar labels, so the terminator is irrelevant there.
- Generalized the "EOS not in chat_template" warning to be actionable and model-agnostic (flags any `eos != terminator` split, not just Gemma).

## Verified against HF tokenizers
| Family | `eos_token` | Terminator | id |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gemma 1 / 2 | `<eos>` | `<end_of_turn>` | 107 |
| Gemma 3 / 3n | `<eos>` | `<end_of_turn>` | 106 |
| Gemma 4 | `<eos>` | `<turn\|>` | 106 |

All terminators confirmed as single special tokens (passes the multi-token `eot_tokens` validation). Gemma 4's tokenizer even declares an explicit `eot_token: <turn|>` field.

body:
## What

First step of a coordinated cross-repo schema change for livespec core's `.livespec-fleet-manifest.jsonc`. dev-tooling's parser + release fan-out read that manifest from livespec **master at run time**, so they must accept the new key **before** core renames it (required-key migration discipline).

- **`fleet/contract.py`** — `parse_manifest` now reads the fleet member array from the new `fleet` key, falling back to the legacy `members` key when `fleet` is absent (accepts BOTH). The `Manifest.members` field name is unchanged (only the JSON read key changed), so `fleet_conformance.py` / `wire_fleet_member.py` need no change.
- **`fleet/_context.py`** — new frozen, keyword-only `Adopter` dataclass (`repo`, `profile`, `posture`), mirroring `FleetMember`.
- **`fleet/contract.py`** — new module constants `PROFILE_LAYERS = ("baseline", "fleet-infra", "orchestrator-plugin", "app")` and `ADOPTER_POSTURES = ("released", "pinned", "none")`; `Manifest` gains an `adopters: tuple[Adopter, ...]` field; an absent `adopters` key parses to `()` (optional), a present-but-non-list value or any malformed adopter entry → `None` (strict, matching the existing member parsing). Member/adopter parsing extracted into `_parse_members` / `_parse_adopters` helpers to keep `parse_manifest` within ruff's branch/return/complexity limits.
- **`.github/workflows/reusable-release-dispatch.yml`** — the sibling-discovery `jq` now reads `(.fleet // .members)[]` so the fan-out works against both the old and new manifest shapes.

## Notes

- Code-only; no dev-tooling spec cycle (`SPECIFICATION/contracts.md` describes the manifest only abstractly and never names the literal `members` key).
- `just check` green locally (46 targets, 100% coverage) at pre-commit and pre-push.

author: mcc-prior-art
body:
## Goal

Extend the governed-agent demo (PR #21) so that, when consensus is required, execution follows the **real** runtime path:

```
Agent proposal → gateway-issued challenge → independently signed evaluator votes
→ N-of-M consensus verification → MCC authority decision → execution gate
→ executor → audit record
```

The agent never calls the executor directly and **never self-authorizes consensus** (it does not issue the challenge and does not sign votes).

## Architecture before → after

- **Before (PR #21):** `Agent → MCC(authority) → Gate → Executor → Audit` — consensus/challenge layer documented as a gap.
- **After:** adds a consensus-required mode using the **existing** `ChallengeService`, `ConsensusVerifier`, and the coordinator's `require_consensus` / `require_challenge`. **No demo-only verifier or second consensus engine.** Consensus is an *additional predicate*, not a replacement: `Agent → Challenge → N-of-M Consensus → MCC(authority) → Gate(nonce) → idempotency/velocity → Audit → Executor`.

## Files changed
- `examples/governed_agent/consensus_support.py` (new) — independent `EvaluatorPool` (separate keys; signs challenge-bound votes)
- `examples/governed_agent/mcc_client.py` — `consensus_required` + `trusted_evaluators` + `consensus_threshold`; `issue_challenge()` (gateway-issued, nonce-bound); `submit(challenge=, votes=)` routes through `require_consensus`+`require_challenge`; fail-closed startup
- `examples/governed_agent/scenarios.py`, `README.md` — consensus scenario + both-paths docs + Mermaid
- `tests/examples/test_governed_agent_consensus.py` (new) — 20 tests

**No existing tests modified.** No prior-art / frozen files touched (root README, CLAUDE.md, doctrine, exhibits, audit.jsonl, VERSION).

## Exact runtime path executed (consensus mode)
`ChallengeService.issue` (gateway) → `EvaluatorPool` signs N votes (real `issue_vote`) → `EnforcementCoordinator.enforce(consensus_votes=…)` → **`ConsensusVerifier.verify`** (signatures, identity uniqueness, trust membership, N-of-M, action/payload/actor/resource/policy_hash/nonce binding, validity window, veto) → single-use **challenge consume** → `ExecutionGate` (one-time nonce) → idempotency → velocity → audit-before-actuation → executor.

## Consensus does **not** bypass the rest of the path (proven)
valid 3-of-3 on a `delete_resource` → still **DENY**; on a no-mandate action → still **ESCALATE**; duplicate idempotency key → still blocked; velocity ceiling → still blocked; replayed challenge/nonce → blocked.

## Test counts & commands
```
$ python -m pytest tests/ -q
457 passed, 1 skipped, 3 warnings            # skip = real-Redis governed-agent test (no MCC_REDIS_URL)

$ python -m pytest tests/examples/ -q
41 passed, 1 skipped                          # 21 basic + 20 consensus

$ MCC_REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6399/0 python -m pytest tests/examples/ -q
42 passed                                     # real-Redis multi-instance runs

$ python examples/governed_agent/scenarios.py     # exit 0; prints the consensus path
$ python evidence/consensus_3of3/harness.py --check          # CHECK PASSED
$ python evidence/consensus_3of3/verify_independent.py        # INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PASSED (11)
$ python scripts/check_version_drift.py                       # DRIFT GUARD OK (1.11.0)
# invariants: no HMAC · no mcc-prior-auth · drift OK
```

## CI status
Will run on push; the existing `nonce-redis-smoke` job runs the example tests against the real Redis 7 service (the governed-agent multi-instance test). Other jobs (tests / smoke / consensus-evidence / consensus-enforcement / consensus-challenge / invariants) unchanged.

## Redis-backed behavior against real Redis
**Yes** — the governed-agent multi-instance test runs against a live Redis locally (42 passed) and in CI. (Consensus state itself is in-memory challenge/verifier; the consensus tests are deterministic and run in the normal suite.)

## Runtime gaps discovered (left explicit, not faked)
- **Consensus + `CONSTRAIN`:** consensus binds to the *proposed* body; if MCC rewrites the payload, the executed body ≠ what evaluators approved → **fails closed** (safe; documented). "Re-consent after constraint" is a follow-up.
- **Consensus + ESCALATE execution:** `execute_with_approval` under `consensus_required` must also carry challenge+votes (else fail-closed for missing consensus). The demo proves valid consensus does **not** turn ESCALATE into ALLOW; it does not wire the combined approval+consensus execution (left for the next PR).

## Residual risks
Verified votes from distinct trusted identities ≠ guaranteed **independence** of evaluators (deployment property). Compromised signing key / evaluator trust set / Redis compromises guarantees. **Not production-certified.**

## Confirmations
- Prior-art files **untouched**; **no** tests removed/skipped/weakened (the one `@skipif` real-Redis test runs in CI); no secrets/keys committed; `.gitignore` not weakened.
- **I did not merge this PR.**

## Summary

Closes the remaining gap in the Phase 2 citation gate. The proxy **enforcement** has been live since 0.22.0 (`gate-proxy` blocks citation-bearing court/third-party egress with a 403), but the **agent-facing contract** that lets agents satisfy the gate was never built — a blocked agent got a raw 403 with no taught remediation, and the citation checker never registered its verification. In live operation the gate was a correct-but-unusable dead-end. This wires the agent-facing half so Phase 2 works end to end.

## What's in here

**Citation-gate contract** (`6dba0e2`, `10ba88b`):
- `citation-verification-checklist` skill — "Gate Registration" section: the checker registers an all-`Yes` table via `POST $GATE_PROXY_URL/quality/citation`, sha-bound to the exact draft text; documents 200 / 422 (`coverage_gap`/`unverified_rows`/`quote_mismatch`) / 400; never trim citations to dodge coverage.
- `legal-citation-checker` agent — Output Format gains the registration step.
- `gate-policy.yaml` — documented `citationGate.boundaries` (default `[COURT_FILING, THIRD_PARTY_EGRESS]`).
- 6 live-egress connector skills (gmail, outlook, google-drive, onedrive, notion, output-delivery-playbook) — the `403 citation_gate_unverified` / `citation_gate_no_document` remediation contract. `share_external` connectors deliberately skipped (v1 write is `not_implemented`).
- `docs/connectors-inventory.md` (tool→field map + 403 contract), `docs/known-limitations.md` (honest scope: curated classes not full Bluebook, no `id.`/`supra`, no good-law; attested floor not source-authority), `docs/operator-walkthrough.md`. CHANGELOG 0.26.0.

**Bundled, unrelated** (`7887863`): a small pre-existing learning-loop fix that was sitting uncommitted in the tree — both scribes now `cd` into `$POSSIBLAW_REPO_ROOT/learning-loop` so their CLI invocations resolve `tsx` in the agent sandbox (launcher injects `POSSIBLAW_REPO_ROOT`). CHANGELOG 0.25.1. Independent of the citation gate; included per the commit-it-separately-first request.

## Validation

- `gate-proxy` **215/215** tests + typecheck clean (no proxy code changed here — this PR is package/docs + the launcher env fix).
- Launcher dry-run regression: `agents=177 skills=172 projects=3 issues=3 warnings=0 errors=0`.

body:
## The final bug — `Client.Query` dropped every daemon row

The daemon's `query` op returns rows as **objects keyed by column name** (`[{"node_id":…,"hover_text":…}]`) with a separate ordered `columns` array. mache's `Client.Query` parsed rows as **arrays of values** and silently `continue`d past any non-array — so **every daemon query returned zero rows**.

That's the root cause of `get_type_info` surfacing no hover despite enrichment working: the enrich populated `_lsp_hover` with real rust-analyzer data (489 items / 22 hovers), and the query **threw all the rows away**. Never caught before because the LSP path never got past the old `unknown op: tool` (#452) to reach the query.

**Fix:** `Client.Query` flattens object-shaped rows in `columns` order (legacy array shape still accepted; absent `rows` → nil; present-but-wrong-type → error preserved). `TestQuery_ParsesObjectRows` pins the real wire shape.

## Also: leyline v0.5.4 → v0.5.5

v0.5.5 (LLO #121) adds **active-probe rust-analyzer readiness + per-language per-file timeout** — making cold-start LSP enrichment **reliable** (verified: 3/3 fresh daemons → 22 hovers / ~22 defs / ~420 refs, consistent, ~8s each). v0.5.5 carries a wire/schema change, so the binary pin and `go.mod` `leyline-schema` move together.

## ✅ Verified end-to-end (cold start)

`mache get_type_info(symbol=config, file=crates/memory-core/src/lib.rs)` on a freshly-cleared `~/.mache`:
```json
{ "node_id": "symbols/config",
  "hover_text": "```rust pub mod config``` --- Shared configuration for the CLI and the daemon (bead:lectio-016d7d)..." }
```

That's rust-analyzer's real type signature + doc comment, through mache's MCP tool, cold. **The "Rust find_callers weak / LSP never works" problem is solved.**

author: aaronbamblett
body:
## What this does

Adds iOS to the release pipeline so every `v*` tag also produces an **unsigned `…-ios.ipa`**, attached to the release alongside the existing platforms. No Apple Developer account or signing certs required.

- New `ios` matrix target on a macOS runner; builds with `flutter build ios --release --no-codesign` and packages the `.app` into a `Payload/` zip → `.ipa`.
- Isolated from the other jobs (`fail-fast: false`), so an iOS hiccup never blocks an Android/desktop release.

## Why unsigned

Apple won't install an arbitrary downloaded app — it must be re-signed to the user's own account. So the IPA serves sideloaders who use **SideStore** (on-device, recommended), **AltStore** (needs a computer on the same Wi-Fi), or **TrollStore** (older iOS, permanent). There is no App Store build.

## Docs

Adds `.github/RELEASE_NOTES_TEMPLATE.md` carrying the full install section, including an iOS sideload how-to, so the instructions are owned by the repo and copied into each release body instead of hand-retyped.

## Verification

Ran the workflow manually on this branch (non-tag, so nothing was published). All six platform jobs went green, and the downloaded iOS artifact was a well-formed `Payload/Runner.app` bundle (executable + Info.plist present). The temporary artifact-upload step used for that check has been removed.

author: nitrobass24
body:
## Tracker-intelligence hardening: failing-tracker circuit breaker + cache observability

Phase 11 follow-through on the "kind to trackers" thesis. Two of the four tracker-intelligence backlog items were already shipped in substance and are now marked DONE with cited evidence; this PR builds the two genuine residuals and defers the other two with documented rationale.

### What's already shipped (marked DONE in `docs/plan.md`)
- **Shared RSS-feed caching** — the #60 search cache keys on `(instanceID, canonical query)` with no consumer identity, caches RSS polls, and uses SWR + singleflight so a tracker sees ≤1 fetch per TTL across all consumers.
- **Fabric-wide tracker pacing** — a process-wide per-host `rate.Limiter` (strictest-wins) fronts every Cardigann + native driver + `/dl` request.

### What's new in this PR
1. **Negative-result circuit breaker** (`searchcache_breaker.go`) — after a live search to a tracker fails, further cache **misses** for that instance short-circuit to the recorded error for a short window instead of re-driving the tracker (anti-thundering-herd). Rate-limit responses honor `Retry-After`. A still-fresh positive cache entry is never affected — only misses consult the breaker. Caller-cancelled contexts never trip it. New runtime-tunable `negative_ttl` knob (default `1m`; `0s` disables) threaded through the same DB-backed app-settings path as the other cache knobs.
2. **Per-indexer observability** — `GET /api/cache/stats` now reports `trackerHitsSaved` (the headline "tracker requests served from cache" metric), `breakerSuppressed`, and a `byIndexer[]` breakdown (hit ratio, hits saved, breaker open-state). Durable store `StatsByInstance` + an engine merge of durable rows ∪ in-memory counters ∪ live breaker state.

### Deliberately deferred (documented)
- **Cross-category superset dedup** — categories flow into the real tracker request via `{{ .Categories }}` and the thin-clamp measures raw result count, so a superset-fetch-then-slice would change the outbound request shape and break thin-clamp/parity semantics for a narrow win.
- **User-configurable per-host request rate** — `ClientParams.RateInterval` is captured at adapter-build time with per-host strictest-wins limiters, so a live global floor is a real plumb-through, not a settings-only change. The new `negative_ttl` knob still demonstrates the runtime-tunable pattern.

### Notes
- **No DB migration** — uses existing `instance_id`/`hit_count` columns + the existing `app_settings` table. `db_test.go wantMigrations` stays at 6.
- `go.mod`/`go.sum` untouched; stdlib + existing deps only.
- Secret-safe: the breaker stores the same typed, redaction-safe error the live path returns and never logs it; the stats join exposes only slug/name + counts, never the cached payload.

### Testing
- `make precommit` (`-race -count=1`) + `make build` green; `make test-openapi` green (OpenAPI updated for the new fields + `CacheIndexerStats` schema).
- New tests cover: breaker trip/short-circuit/Retry-After/self-heal/caller-cancel/bypass/runtime-disable, fresh-cache-served-while-open, per-instance counter isolation, the store `StatsByInstance` GROUP BY, the engine merge (incl. flushed-instance + breaker-open), and the API surface (`byIndexer`, `negativeTtl`, disabled-path `byIndexer:[]`).
- Each leaf went through a parallel adversarial review panel (correctness / secret-redaction / Go-shape); a whole-feature review + `scripts/check-no-secrets.sh` sweep ran before opening.

Built leaf-by-leaf, test-first, as 4 focused commits.

---

### Update — also folded in: HTTP cache validators on the feed (conditional GET)

Following a design thread with the autobrr team (ze0s asked for "ETags/cache tags so clients can get some knowledge, and force new queries manually"), this PR now also adds standards-based conditional GET to the Torznab/Newznab feed — something Prowlarr and Jackett don't do:

- A cache-backed results feed emits a strong **`ETag`** (a content hash of the cached result set) + **`Cache-Control: private, max-age=<remaining TTL>`**.
- A request **`If-None-Match`** that matches is answered **`304 Not Modified`** — no body, no tracker hit.
- A request **`Cache-Control` / `Pragma: no-cache`** forces a live fetch (the header sibling of `nocache=1`) and suppresses the 304.

Design notes:
- The ETag hashes the **pre-`/dl` payload**, not the rendered body — `/dl` tokens reseal per request with a random nonce, so the body is never byte-stable, but the underlying release set is. The tokens carry no expiry, so a client reusing its prior body on a 304 still grabs fine.
- The registry cache surfaces validators to the handler via a `CacheInfo` context sink, filled only on the synchronous `serveHit`/`liveAndStore` paths — never the detached SWR refresh (no sink race). `Cache-Control` is `private` because the feed URL carries the caller's apikey.
- **Standards-only, zero coupling**: autobrr (or any HTTP client) can adopt `If-None-Match` to poll harbrr almost for free; clients that don't simply get the normal cached feed.

Tests cover the validator emission, the 304 match / non-match, the no-cache-header force-fresh path, the uncached (no-validator) path, and the registry recording the sink on both miss-store and hit. OpenAPI + the cache feature page document it.

author: bobbyzhouzijian
body:
## What

Changes how a migrating agent's **notes** are handled when it moves to another island:

1. **Carry forward** — the agent's own notes are now **copied to the destination island** as live notes, so its research follows it.
2. **Archive on source** — the source-island originals are flagged `legacy: true` and moved into that island's `notes/_legacy/`, so the island keeps a record and readers can tell the author has moved on.

Skills still stay island-local (unchanged).

## Why

Previously notes were island-local only: after migrating, an agent's default `coral notes` view scopes to the *new* island (via the `.coral_island` breadcrumb), so it effectively lost convenient access to its own accumulated research. Carrying a copy forward keeps the agent's research with it, while the legacy archive on the source preserves island history.

## How

- **`copy_notes_to_island(coral_dir, agent_id, src_island, dst_island)`** (new) copies each note the agent authored (by `creator`) into the destination's `notes/`:
  - preserves the path relative to `notes/` (`research/idea.md` → `research/idea.md` on dst),
  - keeps the original `creator` attribution so `notes_by(dst, agent)` finds them,
  - leaves the copy **live** (no `legacy` flag),
  - skips notes already archived as legacy on the source (no re-carrying across repeated hops),
  - `-N`-suffixes same-named destination notes instead of clobbering (shared `_dedupe_path` helper, also used by the legacy-archive path).
- **`mark_notes_legacy`** (from the first commit) stamps `legacy: true` and moves the source originals into `notes/_legacy/`, idempotently.
- In `_apply_migration` the **copy runs first** (against pre-stamp content) and the **legacy archive second**, so the destination gets clean live notes and the source keeps the archived snapshot.
- Migration docstrings, the arrival announcement note, and the agent-facing arrival prompt are updated to say notes are carried; skills stay island-local.

## Net effect of a migration

| Location | Result |
|---|---|
| **Destination** `notes/` | live copies of the agent's notes (attributed, not legacy) + the arrival announcement |
| **Source** `notes/_legacy/` | the originals, flagged `legacy: true` + `legacy_reason` |
| Teammates' notes | untouched on both sides |

## Testing

- New unit tests (`tests/test_hub.py`): copy carries authored notes (structure + attribution preserved, not legacy), skips already-legacy notes, and avoids destination collisions; plus the existing legacy-archive tests.
- New end-to-end test (`tests/test_migration.py`): drives the real `AgentManager._apply_migration` with seeded notes and asserts the copy lands live on dst **and** the originals are archived under `_legacy/` on src, teammate notes untouched.
- Full suite: **546 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Also verified by driving the production `_apply_migration` against an on-disk worktree (real symlinks/attempts/notes): the agent's notes appear live on island 1 with `notes_by(island 1, agent)` returning them, while island 0 holds the legacy archive.

together. **Pure console** — `web` (no memory consumer) and `ops-console` (no
memory GRANT) are not touched. Minimal adapter change, **no UI refactor**.

> **Do not tag / release / deploy.** This PR is built + (operator-gated) merged but

## Changes (only `console`)
- **Adapter (`id ← logicalId`):** new `RawEntryView` wire type (`logicalId` + the
  additive `updatedBy`/`updatedSource`) mirroring `AdminDtos.EntryView`;

body:
Captures the two additive SS contract decisions for the promo decision engine, ahead of the build sync. Both are additive; neither reopens anything already agreed.

## 1. Per-link attribution (`cta_id`)
`promo_events` already has a `cta_id` column — this surfaces it on the **authoring** side. Each native CTA may carry an optional `cta_id`; the client echoes it back on `promo_click`, so multi-CTA cards get per-link CTR.

- **Native** cards return it as a field.
- **HTML** cards: GP appends a `promo_cta_id` query param to the href; SS reads it off the intercepted tap (no JS bridge).

`appstore | storekit_offer | paywall | url | deeplink | none` — now **enforced server-side** in the campaign CRUD (was documented-only, open JSON). 
- Adds **`paywall`** (the design doc previously had only `storekit_offer`).
- Each native CTA must declare a valid `action.type`; unknown types → 400, so a payload can't ship a target the client won't render.
- Purchases (`storekit_offer`/`paywall`) resolve through StoreKit on device — no prices or tokens in the payload.

## Scope / safety
- Only touches admin CRUD validation + the design doc + the variant authoring schema. The promo feature isn't live yet (event ingestion, decision engine, dashboard analytics are later slices), so no runtime/traffic impact.

Send the **deeplink route allowlist** so GP only authors routes the client accepts.

author: raistlin7447
body:
# Description

I'm not sure there's an appetite for this, but I'm hoping there is.

A large share of the bugs reported against OrcaSlicer are regressions, or the kind of breakage that basic tests would have caught. The slicing core has very little coverage today, and what exists has no consistent organizing structure, so it is hard for a contributor to know where a test belongs or to trust that adding one is worth the effort.

When a test suite is not well defined, organized, or maintainable, there is little incentive for anyone to add or maintain tests. This PR demonstrates what a clear, maintainable testing framework for `fff_print` could look like, in the hope that the approach, once agreed to, can extend to other parts of the codebase.

This matters most for a large codebase with many contributors. Tests let a contributor pin down and prove the behavior they intend, so when someone later changes that area they immediately know whether they made an intentional change or broke something. And, over time, testing tends to accelerate development rather than slow it, because far less time goes into reproducing and chasing regressions.

**Start with [`tests/fff_print/README.md`](https://github.com/raistlin7447/OrcaSlicer/blob/26ecc08888/tests/fff_print/README.md) for the shape of what I am proposing**.

## What this PR does

- Adds a written testing contract (`tests/fff_print/README.md`): one file per subsystem, each owning both its in-memory and emitted-G-code assertions; flat, behaviorally-named tests with a single `[Subsystem]` tag; helper and style guidance.
- Reorganizes the existing tests so every subsystem has one home: skirt/brim consolidated; multi-filament split into its own file; the catch-all `test_printgcode` and the sprawling end-to-end smoke scenario decomposed into focused tests; the 22-line `test_gcode` folded into `test_gcodewriter`; the misnamed `test_data` harness renamed to `test_helpers`.
- Standardizes names and tags across the whole suite, aligns simple-cube tests on the `cube()` helper, and removes redundant `Slic3r::` qualifiers in the new files.
- Adds coverage in the proposed style: multi-filament per-feature and per-object filament routing; a skirt/brim behavior matrix covering the behaviors reworked in #14333 (including brim ears), with regression coverage for the sequential/by-object skirt bugs #14319 and #14366; resolved extrusion-width and config comments; custom-G-code placeholder substitution; and a new `test_cooling` subsystem file (fan-off, speed-marker consumption).
- Fixes a latent production bug the tests surfaced: `Print::m_isBBLPrinter` was uninitialized, which non-deterministically dropped per-feature filament assignments.
- Re-enables three slice tests previously tagged `[NotWorking]`: the clipper "Coordinate outside allowed range" error that disabled them was specific to a past CI runner environment and no longer reproduces.

## Related work

This builds on an active community effort to make the test suite trustworthy and cross-platform:

- #10308 (need instructions on how to run and author tests): `tests/fff_print/README.md` answers this for fff_print, documenting where each subsystem's tests live, how to name them, and how to run them.
- Fixes #11273 (get unit tests working on non-Linux): this suite is verified green on Windows (MSVC) and Linux (clang-18).
- The appetite for better tests is current:
  - #13466 adds a regression guard against a preset-key crash class
  - #13467 refactors ironing routing to be unit-testable
  - #11269 is fixing long-failing libslic3r tests.

## Notes

- The only production change is initializing one bool member to the value every real flow already assigns; everything else is tests and docs. No change to slicing output, profiles, project files, or the GUI.
- The conventions are a starting point scoped to `fff_print`, open to whatever is preferred.
- Consider this a Phase 1 pass on `fff_print`.  Additional phases would:
  - Replace remaining BDD constructs
  - Remove redundant `Slic3r::` qualifiers
  - Improve consistent use of helpers
  - Migrate legacy `Approx` / exact-float assertions to `WithinAbs` / `WithinRel`
  - Improve test coverage of high-regression-risk areas (prime/wipe tower, supports variants, ironing, seam placement, multi-material/AMS)
  - Extend the contract to the other test suites (`libslic3r`, `sla_print`)
  - Move the large inline meshes in `test_helpers` out to data files
  - Optionally, a CI expectation that new `fff_print` code ships with tests, plus coverage reporting

# Screenshots/Recordings/Graphs

N/A - tests, one bug-fix line, and docs; no UI impact.

## Tests

Full `build_all` CI on the branch is green (run [28212179171](https://github.com/raistlin7447/OrcaSlicer/actions/runs/28212179171)): every platform builds (Linux x64/arm, Windows x64/arm, macOS x64/arm/universal, Flatpak x64/arm), and the ARM `unit_tests` job passes 100% (204/204 across all suites, with every new fff_print case included and green).

Locally, `fff_print_tests --order rand` reports **565 assertions in 47 test cases, 0 failures** on Linux (clang-18); the suite also builds and passes on Windows (MSVC).

author: usernode-bot
body:
When you create an election and the backend has a hiccup, the app no longer tells you it's done when it isn't. Instead, your new election is saved locally on your device and quietly retries in the background until the server confirms it's real—at which point you'll see the success message and can access it. If you close and reopen the app, it picks up where it left off. No more stuck "Loading election…" pages.

Fixes false-success toast when backend returns 502/500 during election creation.

- Implement browser localStorage queue (`election-queue.js`) to persist pending elections across reloads
- Replace optimistic success toast with "Saved locally — retrying…" status pill until server confirms creation
- Add automatic exponential-backoff retry when backend is reachable; classify errors as recoverable vs. terminal
- Show real "Election published ✓" and navigate only after server confirms election exists
- Queue survives page reload and resumes automatically; per-account isolation

## How to test

1. Open the Elections tab on the staging preview. A blue **"Saved locally — retrying…"** pill appears near the top of the screen — this is the staging demo seed proving the new local-first queue indicator renders.
2. To see the real flow: connect an active organization wallet, press **+ New election**, fill in a name + candidates, and press **Create & publish**. The form collapses and the "Saved locally — retrying…" pill tracks the creation.
3. Append `?bridgefault=timeout` to the URL before creating to force the first attempt to fail — confirm the pill stays, then the election auto-recovers and you get the real green **"Election published ✓"** toast only once it lands, navigating to a workspace that actually loads (not stuck on "Loading election…").
4. Reload the page mid-retry: the pill reappears and retrying resumes — nothing is lost.

author: benjithompson
body:
Closes #3.

## What

The shared **Platform Credentials** resolver that any shared script or skill uses to call the BlazeMeter REST API directly. It reuses the *exact* environment variables the BlazeMeter MCP already defines (ADR-0008), so a user who already has the MCP working needs no extra setup.

Resolution precedence:
1. `API_KEY_ID` + `API_KEY_SECRET` (both required), else
2. `BLAZEMETER_API_KEY` — a path to a JSON key file `{ "id": "...", "secret": "..." }`.

No repo-specific config, no hardcoded default key path.

## Safety contract

Isolating this as one small, tested component is what makes the safety guarantees enforceable:

- `Credentials` is a frozen dataclass whose `repr`/`str` **redact** id and secret, so an accidental `print(creds)` or log call cannot leak them. The real values are only handed out via `.as_dict()`.
- `CredentialError` messages name only *sources* (env-var names, key-file path) — never a credential value or the key-file contents. Tests pin this even for the invalid-JSON path (whose raw bytes contain the secret) and a valid-JSON-but-wrong-shape file.

## Changes

- `shared/scripts/resolve_credentials.py` — stdlib-only resolver + `--help`-able `check` CLI (prints a redacted confirmation: source + masked id, never the secret).
- `tests/test_resolve_credentials.py` — 18 fixture tests over the precedence: both env vars, file-only, partial/missing, malformed key file (missing file, invalid JSON, non-object, missing/empty fields), plus redaction / no-leak assertions and the CLI surface.
- `.gitignore` — exclude `api-key*.json` / `api-keys*.json` (`.env` already covered).
- `README.md` — document the key-file JSON shape.

## CI

No `ci.yml` change needed, by design (ADR-0010 thin CI): the existing workflow already runs `pytest` (auto-picks up the new tests) and loops `--help` over every `shared/scripts/*.py` (auto-covers the new script). This is the "script `--help` smoke harness that later utilities plug into" the issue called for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Component returns `{id, secret}` by precedence, or fails clearly when neither source is configured
- [x] Fixture tests cover: both env vars set; only `BLAZEMETER_API_KEY` file; partial/missing; malformed key file
- [x] Credentials never appear in logs or error output
- [x] `.gitignore` excludes `api-key*.json`, `api-keys*.json`, `.env`; README documents the env vars
- [x] CI runs the credential tests and a script `--help` smoke check

body:
## Summary
Migrates ``magi_agent/runtime/deadline.deadline_note`` from ``source.get(\"MAGI_EVAL_DEADLINE_SECONDS\")`` to ``flag_str``.

**New ``FlagSpec``**:
- ``MAGI_EVAL_DEADLINE_SECONDS`` (``scope=\"public\", kind=\"str\", default=\"\"``)

Stored as ``str`` because the callsite parses to ``float`` and treats empty / invalid / non-positive as \"no deadline\"; a typed ``int`` / ``float`` ``FlagSpec`` would collapse those three cases together with the registered default and break the strict opt-in shape.

**Byte-identity**: ``flag_str`` returns ``\"\"`` on unset; the surrounding ``(value or \"\").strip()`` collapses both ``None`` and ``\"\"`` to ``\"\"``. Non-numeric / non-positive values still collapse through the existing ``ValueError`` and ``budget <= 0`` guards.

**Ratchet**: not counted (prior shape was a ``Mapping`` parameter).

Refs: ``docs/plans/2026-06-18-magi-agent-oss-main-remediation-plan-unified.md`` I-1.

Downloaded+extracted onedir builds crash on launch (`Failed to resolve Python.Runtime.Loader.Initialize`): the extracted .NET DLLs carry the **Mark-of-the-Web**, so the CLR refuses to load the managed `Python.Runtime.dll` (pywebview → WinForms → pythonnet).

## Fix
- `bootstrap.unblock_bundle()` strips the `Zone.Identifier` stream from `sys._MEIPASS` at startup (frozen builds only) — like `Unblock-File` — before the GUI loads .NET. Graceful on read-only dirs.
- Bump to **1.0.2**; INSTALL documents the self-unblock + manual fallback.

## Verified

Closes #41.

author: realmeylisdev
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #3628 (Area K): localizes the **below-UI-layer** video-publish error strings that #4889/#4890/#4891 deferred because they're produced without a `BuildContext`.

**Live + persisted path (the real work).** `PublishError(String userMessage)` becomes `PublishError(PublishErrorKind kind, {serverName, rawFallback})`. `VideoPublishService` classifies a failure into a stable `PublishErrorKind` (the substring taxonomy is preserved byte-for-byte — only the return type changed), and `upload_failure_sheet` maps the kind to `context.l10n` via a new `PublishErrorKindL10n` extension (mirrors #4891's `ShareSheetCopiedKind`). This also fixes the standing per-layer violation of carrying an English string in BLoC state.

**Persistence (no Drift migration).** The kind is encoded under a `pek1:` sentinel into the existing `publishError` `String?` column. On interrupted-draft resume it re-localizes in the reader's current locale. As a correctness bonus, the service no longer writes raw `e.toString()`, so the kill-window that could surface a **raw exception dump** to the user is closed. Legacy drafts (plain sentences) decode to `rawFallback` and still render verbatim.

**Notifications (dead code).** Deleted the `AppNotification` publish factories (`videoPublished`/`uploadComplete`/`uploadFailed`/`processingStarted`), their `show*` wrappers, and the orphaned `show()`/`_showPlatformNotification` chain — they had **zero production callers**. Real push copy is server-owned (generated by `divine-push-service`, rendered verbatim by `sendLocal`), so there is nothing client-localizable here.

**l10n.** 18 new `publishError*` keys (3 with a `{serverName}` placeholder), translated into **all 17 locales**.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4892

## Out of Scope

- Client-side localization of OS push-notification copy — it's server-rendered by `divine-push-service`; would require a backend `type`+params contract change (the payload already carries `type`/`senderName`/`eventKind` alongside the rendered strings). Tracked separately.
- Pre-existing dead code adjacent to this change, left untouched to keep the diff focused: `VideoPublishProviderState.errorMessage` (write-only), the `'Video rendering failed'` `setError`, `VideoPublishService.retryUpload`, and the wider `AppNotification` in-app-list machinery.

author: ebconsult-apps
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #63. With the timeout fixed (the full phase now reuses the persisted teaser instead of regenerating it), the full report runs as a single model call — but it now fails with:

> `Model output hit the 6000-token limit and was truncated before returning complete JSON.`

That message is the `max_tokens` guard added in #63 doing its job: the run completes in ~95s (well within limits) but the report is larger than the 6000-token output cap, so the JSON is cut off.

## Diagnosis (from prod logs + Supabase limits)

- Post-#63, every `full` POST completes at **~92–100s** (no longer killed) and returns the truncation error — i.e. the model is generating the full 6000 tokens and getting cut off mid-JSON.
- The full report is the largest output in the engine: 5–10 leverage points + behaviors + behaviorPriorities + keyActors + causeEffect + loops + the six COM-B components (each naming a mechanism) + strongestBarriers + barrierNarratives + gapLog + discoveryActivities + an ≤800-word systems map.
- **Supabase edge limits** (this project is on the **free** plan): wall-clock **150s**, idle timeout **150s**. At the observed ~63 tok/s, 6000 tokens ≈ 95s, so there's room to raise the cap — but only to ~8000 tokens (~130s) before approaching the 150s ceiling.

## Fix

- **`live-engine.ts`** — raise `runLeverageFull` `max_tokens` from **6000 → 8000** (the largest value that stays safely under the free-plan 150s wall clock).
- **`prompts.ts`** — nudge the LEVERAGE full pass to keep prose economical and prioritise the strongest leverage points, so the complete report returns in one response without padding.
- **`pricing.ts`** — align `PHASE_MAX_OUTPUT.full` (pre-run cost estimate) with the new 8000 cap.

The `max_tokens` truncation guard from #63 stays in place, so if a report ever still exceeds 8000 it fails with a clear message rather than corrupt JSON.

## Heads-up: free-plan ceiling

8000 tokens (~130s) is near the free plan's hard 150s wall-clock limit. If reports need to be larger/richer, the durable options are a **paid Supabase plan** (400s wall clock → much higher cap) or **chunked generation**. Noted in a code comment.

## Testing

- `npm test` → 108 passing
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` → clean
- `npm run lint` → 0 errors

Edge functions auto-deploy on merge to `main` (`supabase-deploy.yml`).

author: aiden-wei
body:
Title: dl: reuse static worker tasks in dual-core module runtime

## Summary

This PR fixes long-run performance drift in `module_forward_dual_core()` by replacing per-inference task/semaphore creation with two static worker tasks and static synchronization objects.

## Root cause

The current dual-core runtime creates and deletes:

- two pinned FreeRTOS tasks
- one counting semaphore

for every `module_forward_dual_core()` call.

Under a sustained high-frequency inference workload on ESP32-P4, this causes runtime degradation over time. In our downstream product workload, the degradation shows up as a clear increase in model inference latency, followed by a watchdog reset.

## Fix

`module_forward_dual_core()` now:

- initializes two static pinned worker tasks once
- reuses a static mutex to serialize dispatch
- reuses a static counting semaphore for completion
- updates task priority to match the caller before each dispatch
- wakes workers with `xTaskNotifyGive()` instead of creating/deleting tasks every call

This keeps the original dual-core execution model, but removes the per-inference task lifecycle overhead.

## Validation

Validated in a downstream ESP32-P4 firmware project that exercises `esp-dl` face detection + face feature inference continuously in multi-core mode.

Before this change:

- long-run latency drift appeared after about 70-110 seconds
- face detect latency increased from about 40 ms to about 130+ ms
- face feature latency increased from about 120 ms to about 200+ ms
- the system eventually hit WDT reset

After this change:

- 125 s run: stable
- 195 s run: stable
- 5 min run: stable
- no WDT resets
- no recurring latency drift

Representative downstream 5 min result:

- host result interval count: 1749
- min: 27 ms
- max: 227 ms
- avg: 171.0 ms
- >300 ms: 0

Representative downstream device-side tail latency:

- detect: about 34-52 ms
- feature: about 115-129 ms
- total: about 150-173 ms

## Notes

- This issue was reproduced and verified in a downstream project workload, not with a standalone `esp-dl` sample.
- I have intentionally kept the fix scoped to the common dual-core runtime path.

author: olafkfreund
body:
## What

Clears the **55 medium CodeQL `py/stack-trace-exposure` alerts** in TFactory — route handlers were returning raw exception/stack-trace text (`str(e)`, `f"...{e}"`) to the HTTP client. Exposing internal exception detail to external users is the vulnerability.

## How

Every site now **logs the full exception server-side** (`logger.exception(...)`) and returns a **generic, non-sensitive message**. Response shapes, keys, and status codes are unchanged.

**Two commits:**
1. The 55 CodeQL-flagged sites across the 7 route files + 3 shared helpers where the exception text actually originated (`routes/git.py::run_git_command`, `routes/github.py::run_gh_command`, `services/pr_data_service.py::_run_gh` + file readers) — fixing at source clears the delegated downstream alerts.
2. **Same-class sites CodeQL did not track** but that still leak exception text: `github_auth` (`_gh_auth_status`), `tasks_worktree` (`failed_files` entries + worktree branch/push/discard returns), and the rest of `github.py` / `git.py` (issue ops, Ollama/fnm/Node/Claude-Code install steps, project-load, worktree-dir creation, MCP health, release creation). This leaves **no exception-text-in-response in any file the PR touches**.

Deliberately left untouched: `raise ... from e` (re-raise doesn't expose text) and subprocess `result.stderr` branches (CLI process output, not a Python traceback — not this vulnerability class).

## Verification

- No `str(e)`/`{e}` reaches any response across all 10 touched files (grep-verified).
- Full web-server suite: **36 pre-existing failures unchanged** (git/network/profile e2e; verified by stash-compare), **0 new failures**.
- Compile + import clean; new lines `ruff`-clean (the 9 bare-ruff findings are pre-existing default-rule noise — unused imports / ambiguous `l` — not enabled in the repo's CI ruff config).

## Scope note

A handful of route files elsewhere in the codebase likely share this `return {"error": str(e)}` pattern; a fleet-wide sweep can follow. This PR fully covers the 55 flagged alerts + every same-class site in the files it touches.

Cierra el hueco **workers-1** (el bridge del reviewer sin caller productivo) que prod-06 difirió a un plan dedicado (ADR 0084 Opción B). Apilado sobre la rama de prod-06 (PR #55) porque usa su transición a `in_review` (dag_01).

**Corrección clave (ADR 0084):** NO depende de ADR 0063 (ése es el contenedor review-runtime de preview *humano*); el AI reviewer es una ejecución de agente normal.

## Entregado (Fases A–B) — el bucle autónomo de revisión YA es funcional
- **Fase A (bridge_01)** — `apply_reviewer_verdict` reconciliado con la state machine: `approve` → `in_review→done` (antes no-op que colgaba la tarea); `reject` → `backlog`+`retry_count++`; al `max_retries` → **`blocked`** (escalado DB-legal; `awaiting_human_approval` no es alcanzable desde `in_review`); `unknown` → no-op; guard de idempotencia + predicado `tenant_id`.
- **Fase B (loop_01/02/03)** — trigger `in_review` en el orchestrator → despacha la ejecución del reviewer (routing por `agent_type`: humano = peer-review existente; sin reviewer = no-op); builder del request de review (reusa herencia de modelo + tools/skills + budget de budget_02) marcado `review=True` con `review_context`; el worker, al terminar la ejecución de review, parsea la salida y aplica el veredicto (en vez de la transición de dag_01).

## Pendiente (en este plan, sin empezar)
- **Fase C** — inyección del `<test-report>`: cableo productivo de `run_test_runtime` → `reviewer_input_block` en el prompt del reviewer (bucle completo ADR 0027). Subsistema Docker-pesado.
- **Fase D** — e2e del bucle + ratificación de ADR 0084.

## Tests (TDD)
`test_reviewer_bridge_wiring.py` (6, el que dag_03 pedía y nunca existió) + `test_in_review_dispatch.py` (3) + `test_review_execution_applies_verdict.py` (5). Regresión del dispatch (17) y de ExecutionRequest (capture 6) en verde. mypy limpio.

author: adriendacunha
body:
**Problème signalé** : en créant une campagne, si le cabinet ne répond à aucune question, « on ne demande presque rien au client ». En effet, sans réponses, la liste de documents est vide (0 doc) tant que le client n'a pas qualifié. La mécanique d'auto-qualification existait déjà (le client répond dans son espace → la liste se génère), mais ce n'était **pas explicite**.

## Changements (rendre le mécanisme visible des deux côtés)
- **Client (espace)** : le bloc de questions « Quelques questions pour générer votre liste de documents » devient **prioritaire** (encadré marque) et affiche **en direct le nombre de documents** générés au fil des réponses.
- **Cabinet (page campagne + aperçu)** : **bandeau** listant les questions qui seront posées au client pour générer sa liste, quand le cabinet ne les a pas remplies. Fini l'aperçu « vide » trompeur.
- Helper `pendingClientQuestions` (questions visibles, non verrouillées par le cabinet, sans réponse) + tests.

## Comportement
- Cabinet remplit tout → pas de bandeau, liste complète.
- Cabinet remplit partiellement / rien → le client est clairement invité à répondre, et le cabinet voit quelles questions lui seront posées.

tsc ✓ · **140 tests** (2 nouveaux) ✓ · build ✓.

author: jrandallsexton
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #468 closing the second half of the same bug. \`EventCompetitionDocumentProcessorBase\` had the **same anti-pattern on \`Links\`** as it did on \`Notes\` — \`CurrentValues.SetValues\` in \`ProcessUpdate\` copies scalar properties only, so any link ESPN added to the document after first sourcing (boxscore, gamecast, recap, etc. landing post-game) was silently dropped.

## Fix
New \`ProcessLinksOnUpdate\` mirroring the \`ProcessNotesOnUpdate\` pattern from #468. Reads existing \`SourceUrlHash\` values for the competition WITHOUT loading the Links nav onto the tracked entity (same no-Include rule that applies to Notes / Competitors per the \`ProcessInternal\` comment). Adds only links whose URL hash isn't already present.

## Natural identity
\`(CompetitionId, SourceUrlHash)\`. The URL itself uniquely identifies a link's target. Text changes on the same URL (\`""Box Score""\` → \`""Box Score (Final)""\`) wouldn't be reflected — same trade-off documented in #468 for notes (a stale-text row beats a missing link).

## Tests
- New \`WhenReprocessed_WithNewLink_PersistsTheLinkOnUpdatePath\` in \`BaseballEventCompetitionDocumentProcessorTests\`:
  - Seed via fixture (fixture has multiple existing links — captured as baseline).
  - Mutate to inject a Recap link with a unique URL.
  - Reprocess via update path → assert exactly one new row persisted with the expected text.
  - Replay → assert count unchanged (dedupe works).
- Full Baseball/Football event-competition processor suite: **14/14** (was 13; +1 new).

author: kidcarmi
body:
## Summary

This closes the core P0 from the release-catalog review: the signature/trust **verification primitives existed but were inert** in production. Wiring hardcoded `VerifyPermissive` with no baked roots, so an unsigned catalog seeded on disk was loaded and trusted — violating the "unsigned catalogs are never accepted" invariant.

After this change, **production wiring actually reaches `VerifyEnforce`**, unsigned catalogs are not silently trusted, and `permissive`/`disabled` are explicit break-glass only.

### Central rule (`release_wiring.go::resolveCatalogVerifyMode`)
- **Trust roots present** (baked `bakedReleaseTrustKeysJSON` ∪ `CULVERT_RELEASE_CATALOG_TRUST_KEYS`) ⇒ `VerifyEnforce`, automatically.
- **No roots, no override** ⇒ enforce with an empty ring ⇒ `NewTrustStore` fails closed ⇒ Release Management disabled. An unsigned catalog is **never** auto-trusted.
- **`CULVERT_RELEASE_CATALOG_VERIFY=permissive|disabled`** is the only path to a non-enforce mode — explicit, read-once at startup, always logged loudly. Mirrors the existing `CULVERT_C2_ENFORCE` convention.

### Freshness + rollback (new `release_catalog_freshness.go`, enforce-mode only)
- `expires_at` required and not past (5-min skew; future-dated `generated_at` rejected).
- `catalog_version` required (≥1) and ≥ a monotonic floor persisted at `<dataDir>/release_catalog_state.json`; lower version refused; corrupt floor fails closed (never silently resets to 0).
- Wired via an **opt-in** holder option `WithFreshnessEnforcement`; `NewCatalogHolder` is now variadic so all existing 2-arg callers compile unchanged and the signature-only unit tests stay green.

### Schema + API
- `expires_at` / `catalog_version` added to the index — structurally tolerant at load, enforced in the enforce-mode holder.
- `/api/releases` now surfaces `verify_mode`, `expires_at`, `catalog_version`.

## Scope guardrails (please read before reviewing)

- **The legacy Docker updater was NOT removed.** It remains as compatibility/fallback until a production catalog-driven update succeeds.
- **No official catalog auto-download was added.** This PR does not add any network/download behavior. `CULVERT_RELEASE_CATALOG_URL` verified auto-seed is a deliberately separate next slice (network + atomic-write surface warrants its own review).
- **No private keys are baked.** None in repo, image, installer, docs, or compose.
- **`bakedReleaseTrustKeysJSON` is a public-key / linker seam only** (`-ldflags "-X main.bakedReleaseTrustKeysJSON=..."`), empty in the open-source tree. Public keys only — never private signing material.
- **Official builds still need actual baked public roots** injected at build time (or operators must set `CULVERT_RELEASE_CATALOG_TRUST_KEYS`); otherwise Release Management is disabled by design.
- **Clean install is still not fully no-manual-step** until the `CULVERT_RELEASE_CATALOG_URL` verified auto-seed lands. With no trusted catalog present, `/api/releases` reports `available:false`.

## Next PR (do not start in this branch)

Installer auto-seed: `CULVERT_RELEASE_CATALOG_URL` → download to temp → verify (enforce) → freshness/rollback check → atomic rename → `available:true`, otherwise fail closed. Separated intentionally because it adds network/download/atomic-write behavior that should be reviewed on its own.

## CI fail-closed wall

`release_catalog_phase1_ci_test.go` (`TestPhase1CI_*`): through the production enforce-mode holder, **unsigned / sig-stripped / wrong-key / expired / missing-`expires_at` / missing-`catalog_version` / rollback-replay** catalogs each fail closed and publish nothing. Plus wiring-mode tests (`TestResolveCatalogVerifyMode`, `TestCombinedReleaseTrustKeys_*`, `TestLoadReleaseManagement_UnsignedNotAutoTrusted`) and freshness/rollback unit tests.

## Docs/config
- Plan Phase 1 rewritten with the central rule + delivered/remaining status.
- README demotes "preferred" (legacy updater stays fallback until a production catalog update succeeds) and documents enforce-by-default + break-glass.
- CLAUDE.md env vars + architecture note.
- `docker-compose.yml` forwards the break-glass env; install contract test updated.

## Verification

- `go build ./...` — clean
- `go vet .` — clean

author: timotheegrollier
body:
## Problème

À chaque création de ticket de signalement, **deux runs Actions « skipped »** polluaient l'historique (constaté sur l'issue #124, 25/06) :

| Run | Workflow | Déclencheur | Pourquoi skip |
|---|---|---|---|
| 28175195837 | `claude-fix` | `labeled` (label `à-valider` posé à la création) | label ≠ `claude:fix` |
| 28175194986 | `claude` | `issues: opened` | pas de `@claude` dans le titre/corps |

GitHub enregistre un run pour **tout** événement qui matche le `on:` d'un workflow, même si le job est skippé par son `if:` — un `if:` ne masque pas le run, il ne fait qu'éviter d'exécuter le job. Pour atteindre **zéro**, il faut empêcher les événements de matcher.

## Changements

- **`claude.yml`** — retrait du déclencheur `issues: [opened, assigned]`. Il ne servait qu'à invoquer `@claude` en **ouvrant** une issue (cas jamais utilisé : les issues sont créées par le bot in-app). On invoque toujours `@claude` via un **commentaire** (`issue_comment`). → supprime le run `claude`.
- **`server/src/github.js`** — l'issue est créée **sans aucun label** (plus de `à-valider`). Le **gate humain devient implicite** : une issue ouverte **sans** `claude:fix` est en attente de validation. Domaine + sévérité restent écrits **dans le corps**. → supprime le run `claude-fix`.

Décision validée avec le mainteneur : on accepte de perdre la pastille visuelle `à-valider` en échange de zéro bruit.

## Suivi

- Commentaires (`claude-fix.yml`, `support.js`, `bugReports.js`) et **README** mis à jour (le label `à-valider` n'est plus à créer ; gate implicite documenté).
- Tests ajustés (`github.test.js`, `support.test.js`) : `labels` attendu `[]`. **20/20 verts en local.**

author: dkyncu
body:
Pressing "Apply Radio Settings" crashed and restarted the controller on every Apply (NULL em_cmd dereference in submit_commands).

Root cause: the anticipated channel preference is carried at Network scope in the subdoc, but it was parsed from Device scope. Parsing always failed and returned a negative error code, which the handler cast to a huge unsigned command count and passed to submit_commands over an all NULL array. This also meant the preference set from the UI was never applied.

Fix:
- Parse anticipated preference from Network scope so Apply applies it.
- Treat a negative analyze_* result as no-submit (== 0 -> <= 0).
- Harden submit_commands to clamp to EM_MAX_CMD and skip NULL slots.
- Replace a strict op class count assert with a graceful no op.

Issue: RDKBWIFI-480
Signed-off-by: Durmus Koyuncu <durmus.kyncu.kd@gmail.com>

author: ayushjhanwar-png
body:
## Summary

Fixes a 500 error on funnel and conversion charts that mix a `profile.*` filter with an event-level `properties.*` filter on different steps.

## Reproducer (from prod)

Funnel with 4 steps:
- Step 1: `$identify` filtered by `profile.properties.quotaPlan = 'FRAMEO_BASIC'`
- Step 2: `homePageViewed` (no filter)
- Step 3: `pricingModalViewed` filtered by `properties.$current_url contains 'canvas'`
- Step 4: `paymentSuccess`

```
JOIN ... ambiguous identifier 'properties'. In scope funnel AS (SELECT ... 
windowFunnel(...)(..., 
  ((profile.properties['quotaPlan']) = 'FRAMEO_BASIC') AND (name = '$identify'), 
  name = 'homePageViewed', 
  ((properties['$current_url']) LIKE '%canvas%') AND (name = 'pricingModalViewed'),  ← unqualified `properties`
  name = 'paymentSuccess') AS level 
FROM events 
LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, properties FROM profiles FINAL WHERE project_id = 'frameo') AS profile
  ON profile.id = events.profile_id ...)
```

Removing the `$current_url` filter (or the `profile.*` filter) makes the query work.

## Root cause

The profile JOIN selected the whole `properties` Map column from profiles whenever there was an unmaterialized `profile.properties.X` filter. ClickHouse then had TWO columns named `properties` in scope — `events.properties` and `profile.properties` — and any unqualified `properties['key']` reference (from an event-level filter) became ambiguous.

## Fix

Extract specific keys as aliased columns instead of pulling the whole Map. The profile JOIN now produces columns like `` `properties.quotaPlan` `` (backticked, no Map at all):

```sql
-- Before (broken when mixed filters)
LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, properties FROM profiles FINAL ...) AS profile
       --             ^^^^^^^^^^ pulls whole Map → collision

-- After (no collision possible)
LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, properties['quotaPlan'] AS `properties.quotaPlan`
           FROM profiles FINAL ...) AS profile
```

`getSelectPropertyKey` now returns `` profile.`properties.X` `` for unmaterialized `profile.properties.X` paths (matching the alias form the JOIN creates).

By construction the profile JOIN never has a `properties` column → no ambiguity is possible.

## Why not a quick qualify-with-`events.` band-aid?

Considered, but it requires future contributors to remember the constraint anytime they add a new filter type. The extract-as-aliased-column approach eliminates the bug at the structural level — if someone tried to reintroduce the bug, the JOIN literally wouldn't have a `properties` Map to collide with.

Also slightly more efficient: one key extracted vs the whole `properties` Map pulled into the JOIN.

## Where the change lives

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `chart.service.ts` (`getSelectPropertyKey`) | Emit aliased column ref for unmaterialized `profile.properties.X` (was Map lookup) |
| `funnel.service.ts` | Profile JOIN SELECT extracts specific keys (both filter + breakdown paths) |
| `conversion.service.ts:buildSingleEventCte` | Profile JOIN SELECT now matCols-aware + extracts specific keys (was always pulling whole Map regardless of materialization) |
| `conversion.service.ts` breakdown profile JOIN | Same extract-key pattern as filter path |

Materialized-column path is unchanged — it already returned a column reference (`profile.\`<col>\``), so no collision was possible there.

## Test plan

- [x] Verified locally — the prod-failing funnel now runs correctly
- [ ] Funnel with `profile.*` filter only — unchanged behavior, correct numbers
- [ ] Funnel with event-level `properties.*` filter only — unchanged behavior  
- [ ] Funnel mixing both (the bug case) — runs without "ambiguous identifier" error
- [ ] Funnel with `profile.email` filter (non-properties profile field) — unchanged
- [ ] Funnel with materialized profile.properties.X filter — unchanged (matCols path)
- [ ] Same matrix for conversion charts
- [ ] Same matrix for breakdowns (profile.properties.X as breakdown dimension)

author: mynameyi
body:
## Bug

When `AgentConfigWatcher` triggers a zero-downtime reload while `_consume_queue` is processing a batch (e.g. file upload), the `CancelledError` causes the already-dequeued batch to be silently lost. The new Consumer starts with an empty queue and the message is gone forever.

## Root Cause

In `_consume_queue` (`manager.py`), when `CancelledError` is raised during `_process_batch()`, the batch has already been taken out of the queue via `queue.get()` but has not been processed. The current handler simply `break`s out of the loop, discarding the batch.

## Reproduce

1. User sends a file via WeChat Work to an agent
2. Consumer dequeues the batch and starts `_process_batch()`
3. During processing, `AgentConfigWatcher` detects an `agent.json` change (e.g. `last_dispatch` update) and triggers hot-reload
4. `stop_all()` → `CancelledError` thrown inside `_process_batch()`
5. Consumer catches the error and `break`s, batch is discarded
6. New Consumer starts with empty queue → file message is permanently lost

## Fix

Re-enqueue the in-flight batch items (in reverse order to preserve FIFO) before breaking out of the consumer loop so the new Consumer can pick them up.

```python
except asyncio.CancelledError:
    logger.debug(...)
+   # Re-enqueue in-flight batch so messages are not lost
+   # during hot-reload (zero-downtime agent restart).
+   if batch:
+       for item in reversed(batch):
+           await queue.put(item)
    break
```

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Channels (UnifiedQueueManager / ChannelManager)
- [ ] Other

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature

author: kshitijk4poor
body:
## Summary
When the first assistant response never completes (stall, client disconnect, crash), the user's prompt is now persisted to state.db on receipt, and the user is offered a retry/discard choice on their next message instead of silently losing the turn.

## Root cause (#45110)
`_persist_session` only runs on successful turn-exit paths. If the first assistant response never completes, nothing from the turn is persisted — the prompt vanishes. Follow-up turns hit an agent with a hole in its history, causing confabulation.

## Changes
- `run_agent.py`: new `_persist_inbound_user_message(user_msg)` method — writes the user message directly to SQLite via `append_message` on receipt, before any model call. Registers `id(user_msg)` in `_flushed_db_message_ids` + advances the flush cursor so `_persist_session` does NOT write a duplicate row.
- `agent/turn_context.py`: calls `_persist_inbound_user_message` immediately after `messages.append(user_msg)`, wrapped in try/except.
- `gateway/run.py`: stale-turn detection after `load_transcript` — if history ends with a user message (no assistant response), the previous turn was abandoned. Uses the clarify system to ask the user "Retry or Discard?" with button UI on supported platforms. Retry: re-injects the stored content as the current turn's input after soft-deleting the stale copy. Discard: `rewind_session(n=1)` soft-deletes it. Both paths keep conversation history clean.

## Validation
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Turn completes normally | prompt persisted | prompt persisted (unchanged) |
| Client disconnect before first response | prompt lost silently | prompt persisted on receipt |
| User retries after stall | double-user-message (merged by repair_sequence) | user is asked Retry/Discard |
| User discards stale turn | n/a | stale message soft-deleted, history clean |

- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_turn_context.py tests/gateway/test_compress_command.py` — all pass.
- E2E: real SessionDB — verified early persist (no duplicate), stale detection, discard via rewind_session, and retry re-persist. All pass.

Closes #45110

author: nicolaslardinois
body:
## Was

Behebt den Bug, dass eine **laufende Cockpit-Analyse abbricht**, sobald man während des Laufs auf eine andere Seite wechselt — z. B. ins Portfolio (#5) oder auf den Buffett-Indikator / Big-Mac-Index (#7). Beides war **dieselbe Ursache**.

## Warum

Der Lauf-Zustand — der WebSocket plus `phase`/`events`/`overview` — lebte **im `useCockpit`-Hook der `CockpitPage`**. `CockpitPage` ist aber eine eigene Route. Navigiert man weg, hängt React die Seite aus, der Unmount-Effekt schließt den WebSocket (`useCockpit.ts:69`), und die Live-Ansicht ist verloren. Der Backend-Lauf (Singleton-RunManager) lief zwar im Hintergrund weiter, aber das Frontend hatte die Verbindung gekappt und zeigte beim Zurückkommen wieder „leer/lädt".

## Wie

Neuer **`CockpitProvider`** (`frontend/src/hooks/CockpitProvider.tsx`) hebt den Lauf-Zustand per React-Context **oberhalb der `<Routes>`** (in `routes.tsx`). Die `CockpitPage` liest ihn jetzt über `useCockpitContext()`, statt selbst `useCockpit` zu halten.

author: luisguzman-adfa
body:
xz was shipping **dynamically linked** (`interp /system/bin/linker64`) because it links liblzma via **libtool**, which swallows a plain `-static` (statically links only libtool libs, not libc).

Fix: inject **`-all-static` at link time only**, via a `termux_step_make`. It can't go in configure-time `LDFLAGS` — configure's raw-clang test rejects `-all-static` ("C compiler cannot create executables"). Compile steps ignore `LDFLAGS`, so this affects only the link.

Result (validated on switnet + a clean arm64 node): xz is now **STATIC** + round-trip OK, like tar/gzip/rsync.

`aria2c` is intentionally left **dynamic**: a static aria2c can't resolve DNS off-device (bionic resolver needs Android `netd`); it works correctly dynamic on-device. See the native-binaries standard.

Refs ADFA-4468.

author: davidzakaria
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `startsWith` check in the `protectedFileAccess` middleware was vulnerable to a partial folder match bypass. An attacker could potentially bypass the directory traversal protection by accessing a sibling directory that shares the same string prefix as the intended upload directory (e.g., escaping `/uploads/avatars` to access `/uploads/avatars-secret`).
🎯 Impact: This could allow unauthorized access to sensitive files residing in directories that start with the same name as the protected directories.
🔧 Fix: Added a path separator (`path.sep`) to the target directory before performing the `startsWith` check, ensuring that only actual subdirectories are considered valid, and safely allowed the base directory itself.
✅ Verification: Tested path resolution locally to ensure paths outside the intended directory boundary are correctly blocked while valid subdirectories and the base directory remain accessible.

## What this is (and what it isn't)

A **fail-soft guard** for the area of bug **#33** (slidedeck preview self-heal). Honest scope, confirmed in review against the fix diff:

- **It does NOT reproduce the original #33 symptom** (the Drive `/preview` iframe showing Google's "you need access" until a manual reload). That symptom lives inside the cross-origin Google iframe, which the test aborts, and is unobservable in a harness with no Drive. This test would have passed on pre-fix code.

This test exercises the half of that contract the harness *can* reach — the new view-time Drive call must **never 500 the page** when Drive is unavailable, leaving the "Open in new tab" fallback + embed iframe intact. It's a forward guard against a future change that makes the self-heal throw.

The grant/idempotency/host logic is covered by the `gdrive-link-access` + `drive-embed` unit tests; the Drive **happy path** stays on manual verification (the harness intentionally has no Drive). See the note in `docs/TESTING.md`.
