Drives the real admin submission detail page for a submission whose pitch-deck field is a Drive file URL, with Drive requests aborted, and asserts: **200** (not 500), the **"Open in new tab"** fallback at the original Drive URL, and the embed iframe at the Drive `/preview` URL.

author: consentirdev
body:
## What
The AI session synthesis already existed — but buried as plain text behind the super-admin passcode, and only **after** End/Archive wiped the room. F1 turns it into a **facilitator-facing, branded, exportable handover** the facilitator can produce **while the session is live**.

- **`buildReport(slug)`** composes the report from the LIVE room and persists it to the durable archive overlay **without wiping** — preview + export mid-session. Serialised under the room lock with a **read-merge-write**, so a concurrent build/archive never clobbers.
- **`archiveRoom` refactored to REUSE** an already-built report instead of regenerating (no double Opus spend, no clobber) — a shared `composeArchive()` does both.
- **`buildFallbackReport`**: a structural, AI-free report (counts + curated pattern names) so the handover is never empty without an API key.
- **`ReportDocument`**: a pure, branded, light-surface render of the **synthesis only** — never raw submission text or handles (**privacy by construction**). `reportToMarkdown` mirrors it.
- **`HandoverPanel`** (Session tab): *Build handover report* → branded preview → **Print / Save as PDF** (`window.print` + a print stylesheet that shows only the report) + **Copy as Markdown**. Posts to the host route **directly**, not the shared `cmd()` (which only applies a rev'd state and would drop the returned archive). Replaces the old raw "Download export" JSON dump.

The export is the **synthesis, not the raw room** — individual responses are never reproduced (asserted by test). Building persists only the report onto the existing `rooms:archive:<slug>` record; no new always-on data, no accounts, no external destinations.

body:
Adds `ssh: ${{ secrets.DOCUMENTER_KEY }}` to the TagBot step.

## Why
GitHub blocks the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` (a GitHub App) from pushing any
ref that touches `.github/workflows/`. That's why the automated v0.2.0
tag failed (`remote rejected … without 'workflows' permission`) and had
to be pushed manually. Pushing over an SSH deploy key is treated as a
user push, not an App, so it bypasses the guard.

## Setup (already done on the repo)
- A write-enabled ed25519 deploy key registered on the repo.
- Its private half stored as the `DOCUMENTER_KEY` Actions secret.
- The same key already referenced by `docs.yml`, so one key serves both.

## Result
TagBot becomes fully autonomous — future releases self-tag even when the
release commit changes a workflow file.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: unidel2035
body:
Закрывает #3742.

## Проблема
В тайминге резки (`download/atex/js/production-planning.js`) намотка **фольги** считалась пропорционально метражу. Для прохода 122 м при норме `WIND_FOIL_305 = 4 мин` выходило `4 × 122/305 = 1.6 мин/проход`, т.е. «Итого резка: 1.6 × 20 = 32 мин» — хотя норма намотки фольги 4 мин. Должно быть `4 × 20 = 80`.

## Решение
Намотка фольги считается **блоками** (модель подтверждена в тикете): время прохода = `ceil(метраж / норма-метры) × норма-мин`. Короткий проход всё равно стоит полную норму.

| Метраж | Было (пропорция) | Стало (блоки) |
|---|---|---|
| 122 м | 1.6 мин | **4 мин** (1 блок) |
| 305 м | 4 мин | 4 мин (1 блок) |
| 400 м | 5.24 мин | **8 мин** (2 блока) |
| 610 м | 8 мин | 8 мин (2 блока) |

Модалка тайминга для примера из тикета:
```
Намотка 1 прохода: 4 мин
Итого резка: 4 * 20 = 80 мин
Норма намотки: WIND_FOIL_305=4 мин
```

### Изменения
- `foilWindingMinutes(runMeters, foilPoints)` — новая чистая функция блочной модели (экспортирована).
- `windingMinutes` диспетчеризует точки с флагом `foil` в неё — **одна точка истины**: модалка тайминга, `plannedCutDurationMinutes` и расписание (`scheduleDurationMinutes`/`buildCutTimingCtx`) согласованы автоматически.
- `foilWindingPointsFromTimes` больше не добавляет опорную `(0,0)` — она была нужна только пропорциональной модели.
- Обычная (не фольга) намотка `WIND_<метры>` не изменилась.

## Тесты
- `experiments/atex-production-planning.test.js`: foil 122 м → 4 (было 1.6), +блочные проверки `foilWindingMinutes` (305/400/610/0/нет нормы), `plannedCutDuration 122 × 20 = 80`.
- Предсуществующие FAIL (`rowsToGenPositions #3340`, `isCutVisible #3249`, `#3619`) — не относятся к правке (есть и на `main`).

## Прочее
- `docs/atex_production_planning_algorithm.md` — пример пересчитан (источник истины по алгоритму).
- `index.php`: `VERSION` 61→62 (cache-bust ассетов atex).

author: graemef
body:
Ticket: [PAE-1590](https://eaflood.atlassian.net/browse/PAE-1590)
## What

Registered-only registrations (those with no accreditation) submit summary logs, but no `SUMMARY_LOG_SUBMITTED` event was being written to their waste-balance stream. The read model resolves which submissions belong to a registration from those events, so registered-only row states were being written but could not be read back.

This change writes a balance-neutral zero-delta summary-log submitted event (`creditTotal: 0`) for these registrations so their row states become readable.

## How

Behind a dedicated `FEATURE_FLAG_REGISTERED_ONLY_SUBMITTED_EVENTS` flag (default off), independent of the row-state write flag:

- **Forward path** — when the flag is on, a registered-only submission writes its summary-log submitted event as part of committing its state.
- **Historical migration** — the backfill sweep writes one summary-log submitted event per existing registered-only submission. It is idempotent: it never writes a second event for a submission that already has one, so the sweep is safe to re-run.

A registered-only registration has no accreditation and therefore no waste balance, so the event carries `creditTotal: 0` and leaves all balances unchanged. Balance calculations only consider accredited registrations, so this never surfaces a balance for a registered-only registration.

## Notes

- The sweep is wired at `onPostStart` under the server lock (the standard startup-sweep pattern), so it runs automatically on every deploy — a read-only dry-run when the flag is off, executing the historical backfill when it is on. It is idempotent, so it is safe on every restart.
- The flag defaults off, but off is not inert: on each startup the dry-run logs, per registration, the event it would emit, giving the reviewable production evidence the pre-flip review gates on. No stream events are written in any environment until the flag is flipped on — only dry-run log lines appear before then.
- Related row-state rollout work is tracked separately under PAE-1590.


[PAE-1590]: https://eaflood.atlassian.net/browse/PAE-1590?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

author: mergify[bot]
body:
# 🦟 Bug fix

Probably fixes #760 

## Summary
There is potential race condition in the  `PeerTracker` around the `this->peers`  member variable (which is a  `std::map<std::string, PeerState>`).

In C++,  `std::map`  is not thread-safe for concurrent read and write operations. If one thread writes to the map while another is reading it without synchronization, it leads to undefined behavior.

1. Heartbeat Thread (`heartbeatThread`): This thread is spawned by `PeerTracker` and continuously runs `PeerTracker::HeartbeatLoop()` in the background to publish heartbeats and clean up stale peers.
2. Transport Callback Threads: gz-transport  runs internal thread pools to handle incoming messages. When a  heartbeat  or  announce  message is received, callbacks like  `OnPeerHeartbeat`  or  `OnPeerAnnounce`  are invoked on these background threads.

- Unsynchronized Read: In  `PeerTracker::HeartbeatLoop()` , the heartbeat thread iterated over  `this->peers`  to calculate the age of each peer and check if they had gone stale: 
```
for (auto peer : this->peers) { ... }
```
This read operation was performed without holding the  peersMutex  lock.
- Concurrent Write: At the same time, when a new heartbeat message was received from another peer, a transport callback thread would invoke  `PeerTracker::OnPeerHeartbeat()`, which inserts or updates entries in the same `this->peers`  map. This write operation was protected by  peersMutex , but since the read in  HeartbeatLoop  did not acquire the lock, the synchronization was incomplete.

Im guessing this could be a reason for potential flakes.

## B-17 — surface a salary the employer stated only in the description

**User finding:** offer `4430229490` says **"Salary: Up to 60K€ + 20% variable"** in the description, but LinkedIn left the structured `salary_*` fields empty, so the console showed nothing. This is **distinct from B-15** (which *estimates* when no salary is disclosed) — here the salary **is disclosed**, just not parsed into the structured fields.

## Fix — parse-on-display, no schema change

- **`salaryparse.salary_text_from_description`** — conservative regex: needs a salary keyword **and** a monetary figure in the same segment; doesn't split European thousands (`45.000`) on the dot; ignores revenue (`facturación de 100M`) and benefit lines (`Retribución Flexible: Seguro…`).
- **API** job detail returns `salary_listing` **only** when there's no structured band.
- **web** shows it as a normal disclosed chip (hover: "Stated in the job description"). Precedence: **structured > listing (description) > estimate (B-15)**.

## Verification

- `test_salaryparse.py`: extracts the real cases (incl. `Banda salarial: 45.000 - 55.000 €`, `$90,000-$120,000 USD`) and rejects false positives (revenue, benefits, "competitivo"). API tests: listing surfaced; structured band wins over it.

author: yewman
body:
Four independent primitives the `sol_compat_shred_parse_v1` conformance harness needs out of `Receiver`. Each is self-contained — review per commit.

No behavioural change to existing callers: new feature gates default to inactive, `Receiver.reset()` is opt-in, and the hoisted parse-time bound was already enforced one stage later.

### Commits

1. **`feat(v2:shred): split debug-skip flags into sig-verify and version-check`** — replaces the single `-Ddebug-skip-shred-checks` meta-flag with two orthogonal options (`-Ddebug-skip-shred-sig-verify`, `-Ddebug-skip-shred-version-check`). The harness needs to skip sig verify (synthetic shreds, no known leader) but keep version-check on.

2. **`feat(v2:shred): add Receiver.reset() for state-free reuse`** — in-place reset of `Receiver`, `InProgressSets`, `DoneSets`, and a new `Pool.reset()` that rebuilds the free list without touching the backing buffer. Lets the harness reuse a single `Receiver` across fixtures (a fresh one per call is too expensive — the ctx pool alone holds 4096 in-flight sets).

3. **`feat(v2:shred): reject shred-indices past max_shreds_per_slot`** — hoists the `slot_idx < 32768` bound into `Shred.fromPacketChecked` so the parse-level verdict (`reportShredParseResult`) matches Agave/FD. Previously the bound was enforced one frame too late — after the harness had already observed `parses_as_chained = true`. The `32768` literal is promoted to a single named `pub const max_shreds_per_slot`. Closes the last shred-fixture mismatch in `test-vectors/shred/fixtures` (1001/1001).

4. **`feat(v2:shred): discard unexpected data-complete shreds under feature gate`** — adds `Receiver.Features` with the `discard_unexpected_data_complete_shreds` activation slot (default `maxInt(Slot)` = inactive). When active for a slot, a data shred with `DATA_COMPLETE` set is only accepted when `slot_idx == fec_set_idx + FEC_SHRED_COUNT - 1`. Enforced in `processPacketInner` because it needs the runtime activation slot. Mirrors agave's [`ledger/src/shred/filter.rs`](https://github.com/anza-xyz/agave/blob/v4.1.0-rc.1/ledger/src/shred/filter.rs#L327-L342).

author: westey-m
body:
### Motivation & Context

The OpenAI Responses shell tool was unusable in two ways:

1. **Hard failure when a shell tool was attached.** Invoking an agent that had a
   shell tool raised `ChatClientException: 'FunctionShellTool' object is not
   subscriptable`. The client constructed the OpenAI **pydantic model**
   `FunctionShellTool` for the request `tools` payload, but the Responses request
   path expects the corresponding **TypedDict** param (`FunctionShellToolParam`)
   and indexes it like a dict, so a model instance blew up. This made every shell
   tool call fail (e.g. "value MSFT for me" in the `build_your_own_claw` sample).

2. **Empty command on streaming shell calls.** When streaming, a shell call
   surfaced with an **empty `command`** — the run failed and the UI printed the
   tool/parameter name with no value. The streaming parser read shell items off
   the `response.output_item.added` event, whose `action` is an in-progress
   skeleton with no `commands` yet. The command (and output) are only populated on
   the completed `response.output_item.done` item, and there are no shell-specific
   streaming delta events to fill the gap.

### Description & Review Guide

- **What are the major changes?**
  - Use the TypedDict param type `FunctionShellToolParam` (instead of the pydantic
    model `FunctionShellTool`) when building the Responses `tools` payload — two
    call sites and the import in `_chat_client.py`. This resolves the
    `not subscriptable` throw.
  - Move streaming shell-item parsing from `response.output_item.added` to
    `response.output_item.done`, where the item carries the fully-populated
    `action`/`output`. The `.added` case is now a no-op (`pass`) with an
    explanatory comment. This mirrors how the client already defers `mcp_call`
    results to `.done`.
  - Extract a shared `_shell_item_to_contents()` helper that converts
    `shell_call` / `local_shell_call` / `shell_call_output` items into framework
    `Content`. Both the non-streaming parser and the new streaming `.done` handler
    call it, removing three near-duplicate parsing blocks.
  - Tests: added `test_prepared_local_shell_tool_survives_make_tools`,
    `test_parse_chunk_from_openai_shell_call_added_defers_command`, and
    `test_parse_chunk_from_openai_shell_call_done_emits_command`; updated the two
    `get_shell_tool` tests for dict (param) access.

- **What is the impact of these changes?**
  - Shell tools no longer throw when attached, and streaming shell calls carry the
    actual command and output. Hosted shell, local shell, and shell output items
    are all handled. Non-streaming behavior is unchanged (it now goes through the
    shared helper). No public API changes.

- **What do you want reviewers to focus on?**
  - That deferring shell parsing to `response.output_item.done` is correct for
    both hosted (`shell_call`/`shell_call_output`) and local (`local_shell_call`)
    items, and that the shared helper preserves the previous non-streaming output.

### Related Issue

Fixes #6761

body:
Closes #59.

## Problem

The overworld builder threaded feature flags as **trailing positional bools** through `build()` / `write_overworld()` / `assign_pool()` and as **bare `PickupFlags` literals**. Adding a single flag (e.g. `shuffle_hammer_bros` in #20) forced edits at ~40 unrelated test call sites, and left opaque call sites like `build(&rom, &data, &mut rng, true, false, true)`.

## Change

- New `BuildFlags { shuffle_toad_houses, eights_are_wild, shuffle_hammer_bros }` and `WriteFlags { cross_world, shuffle_hammer_bros }` structs; `build()`/`write_overworld()`/`assign_pool()` take them.
- `#[derive(Default)]` on all three flag structs (`PickupFlags`, `BuildFlags`, `WriteFlags`). `WriteFlags::default()` keeps `cross_world` on (the standard mode); feature flags default off.
- **Production** call sites construct the structs **exhaustively** — so adding a flag still breaks the one place that must wire it to `Options` (a deliberate nudge).
- **Test** call sites use `{ ..Default::default() }` — so future flags leave them untouched.

This is the pattern `Options` / `test_options()` already use; the builder flags just hadn't adopted it.

## Verification

- Pure refactor, **no behavior change**.
- **Byte-identical** generated ROM vs `main` (`--no-palettes`, seed 12345).
- `cargo build` / `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` / full suite (**226 pass**).

author: tonite31
body:
The **behavior-changing** P2-medium batch from the audit — kept opt-in / config-gated (defaults preserve current behavior, with one fail-faster default flagged). Full report: `artifacts/security-perf-review-core-auth-2026-06-26.md`.

## P-M2 — unbounded `_findMany`

`_findMany` applied `.limit()` only if one was passed, so a missing/wrong `where` could load a whole large table into memory. Added a **`DB_MAX_ROWS` safety ceiling** (default `0` = unlimited, **unchanged**): when set, an unbounded findMany is capped and an explicit limit is clamped to it.

The bulk-mutation `.returning()` hydration (the other half of P-M2) is **left as-is** — changing the return contract of `_updateMany`/`_deleteMany` would be breaking — and documented as a caveat to bound with a tighter `where`.

## P-M10 — unbounded cache offline queue + 20 retries

ioredis defaults to an unbounded offline command queue and 20 retries/request, so a post-startup cache outage buffers every command and hangs awaits. Resilience options are now applied to every client (single / sentinel / cluster):

- `maxRetriesPerRequest` = `CACHE_MAX_RETRIES_PER_REQUEST` (**default 3** — fail faster than ioredis's 20 so commands reject instead of hanging; this is the one default that changes).
- `enableOfflineQueue` = `CACHE_ENABLE_OFFLINE_QUEUE` (default `true`; set `false` for strict fail-fast that rejects immediately while disconnected).

## Verification

type-check + madge circular + build clean; config/env unit suites green. 

> Note: the `src/db` and `src/cache` **integration** suites have pre-existing failures in this environment (cross-file `test_users` pollution; valkey test config) — confirmed identical on a clean `main` checkout, unrelated to this change.

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Problem

In the robotsix-chat chat UI, answering a **Pending Question** auto-closes/removes it immediately, severing the assistant's link to the original question before it has read the answer.

Concretely, in `src/robotsix_chat/ui/index.html` the `submitPendingAnswer(questionId, answer)` function does three things when the user clicks **Answer**:
1. Pushes the answer into the conversation queue as a chat turn (`[pending question <id>]: <answer>`).
2. Immediately calls `DELETE /pending-questions/<id>` — which on the server runs `PendingQuestionsStore.remove(...)` and deletes the entry from the per-session store.
3. Optimistically removes the panel row from the DOM.

Because the entry is deleted from `PendingQuestionsStore`, the assistant can no longer fetch the question (or its answer) by id. There is also **no agent-facing tool to read a question by id** — `build_pending_questions_tools` only exposes `add`/`update`/`remove`. This breaks follow-up acknowledgement and context recall: the assistant cannot confirm what it asked or relate the answer to the question.

The lifecycle should change so that **the human answering does not close the question** — answering moves it to an *answered-but-open* state, and the **assistant** is responsible for explicitly closing it (by id) once it has read and acted on the answer.

## Scope

Grounded in the actual `robotsix-chat` checkout. Make all of the following changes; keep the existing **dismiss** path (empty answer) closing the question as it does today.

### 1. Store — `src/robotsix_chat/pending_questions/store.py`
- Add two fields to the `PendingQuestion` dataclass: `answer: str = ""` and `answered_at: float = 0.0`.
- Add a method `answer(self, question_id, answer_text, *, wall_clock=None) -> PendingQuestion | None`:
  - Looks up via `self._find(question_id)`; returns `None` for an unknown id (mirroring `update`/`remove`).
  - Sets `entry.answer = answer_text.strip()`, `entry.status = "answered"`, `entry.answered_at = wall_clock if wall_clock is not None else time.time()`.
  - **Does NOT delete the entry** — it stays in `self._questions`.
  - Publishes a new `pending_question_answered` frame via `self._publish(...)` and returns the entry.
- Add a frame builder `_answered_frame(entry)` returning a dict with `type="pending_question_answered"` plus `question_id`, `session_id`, `text`, `detail`, `status`, `answer`, `answered_at`, `created_at`.
- Add `answer` and `answered_at` to the existing `_added_frame` and `_updated_frame` payloads so reload/update paths carry them.
- Leave `remove(...)` unchanged — it remains the explicit-close path (publishes `pending_question_removed`). `get(...)` / `list_for_session(...)` are unchanged but now expose the new fields.

### 2. Agent tools — `src/robotsix_chat/pending_questions/__init__.py`
- Add a new tool `get_pending_question(question_id: str) -> str` returned from `build_pending_questions_tools`. It calls `store.get(question_id)` and returns a readable summary including `text`, `detail`, `status`, `answer`, and `created_at`; returns `f"Unknown question id: {question_id!r}"` when not found. This is the mechanism by which the assistant **reads the question + answer by id** after the human answers.
- Update the `remove_pending_question` docstring to state explicitly that this is how the assistant **closes** a question after it has read and acted on the answer; behaviour (calls `store.remove`) is unchanged.
- The returned tool list becomes `[add_pending_question, update_pending_question, get_pending_question, remove_pending_question]`. When `settings.enabled` is `False`, still return `[]`.

### 3. HTTP server — `src/robotsix_chat/chat/server.py`
- Add an endpoint `pending_questions_answer_endpoint` bound to `POST /pending-questions/{question_id}/answer`:
  - Reads the JSON body and extracts `answer` (string; default `""`).
  - Calls `store.answer(question_id, answer)` on `request.app.state.pq_store`.
  - Returns `404` JSON `{"error": "unknown question", "question_id": ...}` when it returns `None`; otherwise `200` JSON `{"question_id": ..., "status": "answered", "answer": ...}`.
- Register the new `Route("/pending-questions/{question_id}/answer", pending_questions_answer_endpoint, methods=["POST"])` alongside the existing pending-questions routes.
- Keep the existing `DELETE /pending-questions/{question_id}` endpoint (`pending_questions_delete_endpoint` → `store.remove`) — it remains the dismiss/close path.
- Extend the `pending_questions_list_endpoint` JSON projection to include `answer` and `answered_at` for each entry.

### 4. Frontend — `src/robotsix_chat/ui/index.html`
- In `submitPendingAnswer(questionId, answer)`:
  - **Non-empty answer:** still push the message into the conversation queue (`[pending question <id>]: <answer>`), but call `POST /pending-questions/<id>/answer` with body `{"answer": <answer>}` **instead of** `DELETE`. Do **not** optimistically remove the row from the panel. Mark the local entry as answered (set `status="answered"`, `answer=<answer>`) and re-render it in the answered state.
  - **Empty answer (dismiss button):** keep the current behaviour — call `DELETE /pending-questions/<id>` and remove the row.
- In the SSE frame handler (where `pending_question_added` / `pending_question_updated` / `pending_question_removed` are dispatched to `updatePendingPanel`), also handle `pending_question_answered` and route it to `updatePendingPanel`.
- In `updatePendingPanel` / `renderPendingEntry`: when an entry is answered (`status === "answered"` or `entry.answer` is non-empty), render the submitted answer (e.g. in the meta/detail area), reflect `status` as answered, and disable/hide the answer input + button so it cannot be re-submitted. The row stays visible until a `pending_question_removed` frame arrives (i.e. the assistant explicitly closed it).
- In `loadPendingQuestions()`: pass through `answer`, `answered_at`, and `status` from the GET snapshot so answered-but-open questions restore in the answered state across reloads/session switches.

### 5. Tests
- `tests/pending_questions/test_store.py`: `answer()` sets `status="answered"`, stores the answer, sets `answered_at`, leaves the entry retrievable via `get()`/`list_for_session()`; `answer()` on an unknown id returns `None`; with an event bus wired, a `pending_question_answered` frame is published.
- `tests/pending_questions/test_tools.py`: `get_pending_question` returns the text/detail/answer/status for a known id and an error string for an unknown id; after `answer`, `remove_pending_question` still closes the question.
- `tests/chat/test_server.py`: `POST /pending-questions/{id}/answer` returns `200` and the question remains listable via `GET /pending-questions` with `status="answered"` and the stored `answer`; `POST` to an unknown id returns `404`; `DELETE` still removes.

## Acceptance criteria

- Submitting a (non-empty) answer in the UI transitions the question to an **answered-but-open** state: `PendingQuestionsStore` still contains the entry with `status="answered"` and the stored `answer`/`answered_at`; the panel row remains visible (input disabled) instead of disappearing.
- After an answer is submitted, the assistant can fetch the question **and its answer** by id via the new `get_pending_question` tool, and the entry is still returned by `GET /pending-questions`.
- `POST /pending-questions/{question_id}/answer` exists, sets the answered-but-open state, returns `200` with the answer on success and `404` for an unknown id.
- The assistant has an explicit close mechanism (`remove_pending_question` tool → `store.remove`, surfaced as `DELETE /pending-questions/{id}`); the panel reflects closure only after a `pending_question_removed` frame is received.
- The dismiss button (empty answer) still closes/removes the question immediately, unchanged.
- Follow-up acknowledgement works end-to-end: after the human answers, the assistant can read the original question text + answer by id, reference it,

author: loning
body:
## Problem

The G10 saga-handler ratchet flagged **every** non-saga-shaped department not on the shrink-only `migration/saga-handler.allowlist`, with no path for a one-shot **stateless build-time generator**. fkst-website's FKST-generate feature added a `site-gen` package whose `generate` department builds in-memory artifacts and writes generated Eleventy source files one-shot (via `fkst-framework run`) — `consumes={}`, `produces={}`, no `raise`/marker/CAS, no lifecycle state, no state transitions. The saga doctrine ("every **state transition** is a bounded saga step") does not apply to it, yet G10 rejected it and the allowlist cannot grow. The website's autonomous fix loop hit this 22 times and dropped to `blocked`.

## Fix

Add a first-class, **fail-closed** stateless-generator exemption to G10. A department source is exempt **only if**:
1. it positively declares `kind = "stateless_generator"` in its spec (opt-in — not accidentally inferred from empty edges), **and**
2. `consumes = {}` **and** `produces = {}` (empty), **and**
3. it makes **none** of the lifecycle/event/state calls `raise / emit / enqueue / publish / ack / nack / retry / compensate / with_lock / once / cache_* / *marker* / *CAS*`.

The positive `kind` declaration makes the exemption opt-in; the forbidden-effect check **fail-closes against smuggling** a real lifecycle handler behind empty edge declarations (a lifecycle handler must consume/produce/raise/persist — it cannot satisfy the predicate). Any uncertainty ⇒ not exempt ⇒ must be saga-shaped.

This is **not** a vacuous zero-step saga and **not** allowlist growth — it is a distinct, statically-verified `stateless_generator` department kind, sitting alongside `lifecycle department → workflow.saga.department` in the G10 model.

## Cross-model design validation

ChatGPT Pro (independent cross-model oracle) validated the design: **option (c)** — "Do not call it a saga. Do not grow the allowlist. Add a first-class, explicitly declared, statically verified `stateless_generator` department kind to G10." It flagged that an inferred `consumes=={}/produces=={}` predicate is **necessary but insufficient** (could hide a lifecycle handler); this PR's positive-kind + fail-closed forbidden-effect predicate is the hardened answer.

## Tests

- `scripts/check_repo_stateless_generator_test.py` (4 tests): a declared generator is exempt; a source with empty edges but **no kind declaration** is NOT exempt (proves opt-in); a declared generator containing a `raise(`/marker/CAS call is NOT exempt (proves fail-closed against smuggling); a normal lifecycle department is NOT exempt.
- `python3 scripts/check_repo.py` passes (repository checks passed).

## Follow-up (separate website-repo change)

author: jayking40
body:
Title: feat: introduce shared Dialog primitive and standardize modal infrastructure

Description
This PR introduces a reusable <Dialog> primitive and migrates all existing custom modals to use it, standardizing behavior and resolving multiple edge-cases related to focus trapping and scroll-locks.

Fixes #653

Changes Made
Primitive Added: Introduced src/components/ui/Dialog.tsx, which abstracts away createPortal, scroll-locking, and focus trapping via inert.
Modals Migrated: Stripped out custom background wrappers and bespoke event listeners from CommitmentCreatedModal, CommitmentDetailsModal, SettlementModal, CommitmentEarlyExitModal, and ExportCommitmentsModal in favor of the new primitive.
Documentation: Added docs/MODAL_SYSTEM.md to outline best practices for future developers adding modals to the codebase.
Test Suite Updates: Wrote exhaustive unit tests for Dialog.test.tsx (handling focus wrapping and Escape keys). Refactored migrating components' tests to align with the new structural DOM nodes.
Motivation and Context
Previously, each modal in the repository implemented its own version of a focus trap, background wrapper, and useEffect logic for escape keys and scroll locking. This led to bug regressions and a lack of standardized accessibility (missing aria-modal, inert backgrounds, etc). This PR centralizes this infrastructure into a single heavily-tested primitive.

How to Test
Fire up the development server npm run dev.
Open any of the modals (e.g. from the marketplace or dashboard commitments).
Verify that the background scroll is completely locked.
Try to click anywhere outside the modal boundary to ensure it safely closes.
While open, hit Tab and Shift+Tab to verify the focus trap wraps smoothly.
Verify the test suite npm run test passes without errors.
Notes for Reviewers
Note: During this branch, you may observe unrelated test errors originating from duplicate declarations in src/lib/backend/services/contracts.ts and src/lib/backend/validation.ts. These exist upstream and have been decoupled from this branch. This PR strictly targets the modal infrastructure standardization.

closes #653

body:
Part of **D-BA-RETURN-SIMULATOR-FIRST** (CEO-approved 2026-06-26): build + test ALL BA-return functionality pre-licence-day against a SIMULATED outside world. Phase 2b completes the derivative book and drives **BA 350 (Derivatives Instruments)** + **CVA**.

## Premise confirm / challenge

- **BA 350** premise CONFIRMED: a notional + fair-value inventory grid over the derivative book (1410 cells, 6 asset classes × trading/banking, ETD/OTC × instrument-type × maturity-band). No fold existed (all cells `licence-day-data`, no driver). Built the fold + cell-assembly + simulated book.
- **CVA** premise CORRECTED: the brief's "CVA contract-only" premise is **superseded** — a real standardised CVA engine ALREADY EXISTS (`platform/market-risk/cva-engine.ts`, `computeCva`), landed under D-MODEL-REGISTRY-SCOPE-CLOSURE-V1 Slice 5. It is the **standardised BA-CVA reduced approach** (Σ LGD × EAD × PD × discount), V1-free. **No new engine built.** I extended its exposure derivation to read the born-V2 derivative book and validated against a hand-computed BCBS d424 MAR50 golden case. This is bounded (closed-form), NOT an FRTB-scale build — no gap-register deferral needed for the engine.

## Simulated derivative-book shape

Born-V2 `DerivativeTradingPositionOpened`/`Closed` (v2-parallel, registered). 10-position book (`seed-derivative-book-sim-v1.ts`, `provenance: simulated`, scenario `derivative-book-sim-v1`): every instrument type (futures bought/sold, forwards/FRAs, swaps, options written/purchased, CDS), asset class (IR/FX/equity/commodity/credit), ETD vs OTC venue, maturity band (<1y/1-5y/>5y), trading + banking book. OTC positions carry counterparties (CP_BANK, CP_CORP) for CVA reuse. FRTB-desk-allocated.

## BA 350 cell→fold map

`ba-350-derivatives-fold.ts` folds the book into a grid keyed by (assetClass, venue, instrumentType, maturityBand, book) → {notional, positive/negative/net fair value}. `ba-350-derivatives.ts` assembles the backbone: per-asset-class × book notional + fair value, ETD/OTC venue split, credit-derivative Section 2, grand-total hash-totals.

**BA 350 golden (recon + 6 golden tests):** grand notional **R820m**; net fair value **+R3.22m** (positive R5.27m / negative −R2.05m); IR-trading R440m, IR-banking R150m, FX-trading R90m, equity-trading R70m, commodity-trading R20m, credit-trading R50m; ETD R220m / OTC R600m.

## CVA approach + golden values

Standardised BA-CVA reduced (existing engine). EAD = max(0, Σ positive fair value) + Σ PFE add-on (documented per-asset-class fractions — SA-CCR-supervisory-factor analogue, loud `requireWeight`). ETD (no-counterparty) excluded. PD via fallback weights by counterparty class (bank 0.5%, corporate 2%); LGD 0.6; discount 0.97.

**CVA golden (recon + 4 golden tests, hand-computed BCBS):**
- CP_BANK (bank): EAD **R9.07m**, PD 0.005 → CVA **R26,393.70**
- CP_CORP (corporate): EAD **R3.3m**, PD 0.02 → CVA **R38,412.00**
- **Total CVA = R64,805.70**; CVA RWA = **R810,071.25** (capital × 12.5)

## BA 700 CVA-leg wiring

`cva-rwa-leg.ts` converts CVA capital → RWA (× 12.5) → `cvaRwaMinor`, wired into `computeRwaFromPositions`'s `computeRwa` call — the BA 700 totalRWA CVA leg now **sources the real charge** instead of the historical zero placeholder. Provenance-filtered → production stays 0.

## Production-read=0 vs simulated-read=values proof

Both BA 350 + CVA are provenance-filtered. **Production-only lens** of the simulated book:
- BA 350: empty inventory; grand-notional line `absent` (zero by absence, never fabricated).
- CVA: `no-otc-exposure` (loud zero); CVA RWA leg 0.

**Simulated/combined lens:** drives the golden figures above. Guards the `includeSimulated`-into-Prod trap (D-V2-UI-VISIBILITY-REMEDIATION). Root-cause fix: threaded a `ProvenanceFilter` through `deriveCounterpartyExposures` for the derivative-book leg (the legacy IRS/FX loops still rely on store separation — tracked, see below).

## statusReason reclassification

Idempotent script noted **1410 BA 350 + 53 CVA cells**: "engine/fold proven end-to-end against the simulated derivative book; production folds to 0 until real positions at licence-day". Status stays `licence-day-data` (correct — the licence-day gate on REAL data is unchanged).

## Recon assertions

Two ENFORCING, self-contained (always-assert) recons: `recon:ba350-derivatives-sim-drive` (18 asserts — oracle reconciliation, fair-value sign split, ETD/OTC split, credit Section 2, provenance boundary, gap tracked) + `recon:cva-derivatives-sim-drive` (10 asserts — BCBS golden, ETD exclusion, RWA leg = capital × 12.5, provenance boundary).

## Tracked gaps (gap-register, no silent deferral)

- `ba350-maturity-ladder-cell-mapping` — the ~1000-leaf maturity-ladder detail-row mapping (data IS folded; only the leaf-cell row enumeration is deferred). Surfaced on the assembled output's `gaps[]`.
- **`cohort-var-provenance-filter`** (the brief's VaR-provenance finding) — the cohort VaR engine (`computeCohortVar`) is not provenance-filtered; it relies on store separation, so a production canonical store that ever held a simulated FIL instrument would compute VaR over it. **Tracked, NOT fixed** (separate FX-V2-simulator hardening).

## Engineering integrity

`bun run ci` GREEN on a fresh self-seeded store (the 2 local failures — `rms-document-blob-integrity` home-store IAS-21 blobs + `event-store-append-only` local-baseline-vs-rebuilt-store — are environmental, not reproducible on CI's clean store, and untouched by this diff). Full `tsc` clean; biome clean; citation-gate clean. **Decimal-native money arithmetic** (no float-money debt added; the 3 pre-existing IRS/FX float lines re-keyed to shifted line numbers — count held at 223). No `any`/`!`/`@ts-ignore`. V1-free (born-V2, imports from v2-core canonical homes). Replay-safe + idempotent seed.

**Cited:** D-BA-RETURN-SIMULATOR-FIRST; D-FX-V2-SIMULATOR-FIRST; D-FRTB-TRADING-DESK-STRUCTURE; D-OPERATING-BOOK-PROVENANCE-ARCHITECTURE; D-ENGINEERING-INTEGRITY-CHARTER; D-MODEL-REGISTRY-SCOPE-CLOSURE-V1 Slice 5; BCBS CVA framework (MAR50 / d424); Reg 28 / Reg 30.

- 引入全新的 `BorderGlow` 边缘发光卡片组件，实现动态渐变光效。
- 将原有平铺式问答列表重构为可交替左右对齐的独立发光卡片布局。

- 将场景卡背景从 `ink-900/80` 调整为 `ink-950`。

### 2. BorderGlow 组件实现
- **`BorderGlow.tsx`**: 新增 React 组件，通过监听指针移动实时计算边缘接近度与光标角度。

  - 支持 `animated` 模式下自动扫描动画，通过 `requestAnimationFrame` 驱动光晕沿边缘旋转并淡入淡出。
- **`BorderGlow.css`**: 新增样式文件，定义边缘渐变光效、网格渐变边框与外发光层。
  - 通过 CSS 变量（`edge-proximity`、`cursor-angle`、`cone-spread` 等）驱动发光强度、角度与锥形扩散范围。
  - 使用 `conic-gradient` 蒙版实现随光标方向旋转的局部发光，并支持 `hover` 与动画扫描状态。

### 3. QA 页面背景与模糊调整
- 将背景遮罩的透明度从 `opacity-30` 降低为 `opacity-25`。
- 将模糊强度从 `blur-2xl` 调整为 `blur-md`。

### 4. 新增 Playwright 截图脚本
- 新增 `.trae/qa_screenshot.py` 脚本，用于捕获 QA 页面静态截图及鼠标沿卡片边缘移动时的发光效果。

## 💡 Technical Highlights

- **动态光效**: `BorderGlow` 组件通过实时追踪鼠标位置，利用 CSS 变量和 `conic-gradient` 实现边缘动态渐变发光效果，提升用户交互体验。
- **组件化设计**: 将问答项解耦为独立的 `BorderGlow` 卡片，提高了组件的复用性和页面的可维护性。
- **动画性能优化**: `requestAnimationFrame` 用于驱动动画，确保动画流畅性并优化浏览器渲染性能。
- **自动化测试**: 新增 Playwright 脚本，能够自动化捕获动态光效的视觉效果，便于回归测试和效果验证。

author: tdraier
body:
## Issue

Fixes dust-tt/tasks#8846 — SharePoint files silently skipped within an accessible folder.

## Root cause

In `syncFiles()`, a Graph `404` raised while listing a folder/drive's `/children` was treated as "the node was deleted upstream": it returned `{ count: 0, childNodes: [], nextLink: undefined }`, the full-sync workflow then called `markNodeAsSeen()`, and **the entire subtree below the node was silently dropped and never retried** — no connector error surfaced.

This skip was introduced in #27024 (Jun 8); the customer hit transient `itemNotFound` 404s the next day. Microsoft Graph is known to return transient `itemNotFound` on `/children` enumeration, so a momentary blip was converted into permanent, invisible data loss. It also explains the "re-sync ran with no errors but no new docs indexed" report: the silent skip is logged at `warn` (not `error`) and returns gracefully, so the connector reports success while subtrees are dropped again.

## Fix

A bare `404` on enumeration is now disambiguated instead of assumed-deleted:

1. `isSiteNotFoundError` (the SharePoint host is gone) → skip as before (genuinely unrecoverable).
2. A bare `404` → lightweight direct `GET ...?$select=id` on the parent node (new `microsoftNodeStillExists` helper, mirroring the existing existence-check at `activities.ts:1177`):
   - parent **gone** → skip gracefully (preserves the original anti-infinite-retry intent),
   - parent **still exists** → the 404 was transient → **rethrow** so Temporal retries the page rather than dropping the subtree.

This also restores admin-facing visibility: a persistent anomaly now surfaces as a retried/failed sync instead of a silent success.

## Scope notes

- `reconcileSensitivityLabelsForParent()` has the same silent-skip shape but only runs for sensitivity-label reconciliation (not the indexing path in this issue), so it's left untouched to keep the change focused.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsgo --noEmit` passes
- No existing test harness for `syncFiles` (heavily DB/Graph-coupled); no new mock infra added.

author: umwelt
body:
## Summary

Two related changes on the executor/sled consolidation path:

1. **#2641 Phase 4** — consolidate post-executor hooks into `finish_block_processing`, remove per-block seed-sled token reconciliation, gate in-memory SOV mint behind `!has_executor()`.
2. **Replay determinism fix (g4 @ h=74010)** — fresh wipe-and-catch-up failed with `Insufficient token balance` (50 SOV short) because executor-only `ChainSync` replay never seeded genesis SOV to sled and skipped `finish_block_processing` side effects.

## Root cause (g4)

After sled wipe, `ChainSync::import_blocks` replayed blocks 0→74009 via `BlockExecutor::apply_block` only. Live validators built state incrementally with:

- Genesis `[allocations.sov_balances]` written to sled (not via block txs)
- Domain registration fees applied in `finish_block_processing` (executor treats `DomainRegistration` as no-op)

Replay-from-genesis on the new binary produced sled balances ~50 SOV short of what block 74010 expected. Not the same bug as #2723 (quorum verify).

## Fix

- Credit embedded genesis `sov_balances` during executor block-0 apply
- Route `expected_start == 0` imports through genesis bootstrap (block 0 via executor) + canonical `Blockchain` runtime for blocks 1+
- Mirror domain registration SOV fees to sled alongside in-memory debits
- Re-apply genesis metadata on `load_from_store`; persist genesis SOV before fresh-node verified import
- Treat `DomainRegistration` / `DomainUpdate` as canonical-runtime import triggers

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p lib-blockchain --lib` — 1946 passed
- [x] `test_genesis_persists_sov_allocations_to_sled`
- [x] `test_genesis_bootstrap_import_seeds_sov_balances`
- [ ] Deploy to g4, wipe sled, verify catch-up passes h=74010+

## g4 recovery

Rebuild with this branch, wipe sled, re-sync from peers. Should replay 0→tip without balance divergence.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
# 🦟 Bug fix

Probably fixes #760 

## Summary
There is potential race condition in the  `PeerTracker` around the `this->peers`  member variable (which is a  `std::map<std::string, PeerState>`).

In C++,  `std::map`  is not thread-safe for concurrent read and write operations. If one thread writes to the map while another is reading it without synchronization, it leads to undefined behavior.

1. Heartbeat Thread (`heartbeatThread`): This thread is spawned by `PeerTracker` and continuously runs `PeerTracker::HeartbeatLoop()` in the background to publish heartbeats and clean up stale peers.
2. Transport Callback Threads: gz-transport  runs internal thread pools to handle incoming messages. When a  heartbeat  or  announce  message is received, callbacks like  `OnPeerHeartbeat`  or  `OnPeerAnnounce`  are invoked on these background threads.

- Unsynchronized Read: In  `PeerTracker::HeartbeatLoop()` , the heartbeat thread iterated over  `this->peers`  to calculate the age of each peer and check if they had gone stale: 
```
for (auto peer : this->peers) { ... }
```
This read operation was performed without holding the  peersMutex  lock.
- Concurrent Write: At the same time, when a new heartbeat message was received from another peer, a transport callback thread would invoke  `PeerTracker::OnPeerHeartbeat()`, which inserts or updates entries in the same `this->peers`  map. This write operation was protected by  peersMutex , but since the read in  HeartbeatLoop  did not acquire the lock, the synchronization was incomplete.

Im guessing this could be a reason for potential flakes.

body:
## Three verified accuracy issues in `getting-started.md`

### 1. OpenAI key is **not** read from `OPENAI_API_KEY` (major)

The "Pick an embedding path" table told users the OpenAI path is set up
with the standard `OPENAI_API_KEY` env var. memtomem never reads that
variable (`grep -rn OPENAI_API_KEY src/` → 0 hits). The OpenAI embedder
builds its auth header from `embedding.api_key` only
(`embedding/openai.py:40-41`), which is set via `mm init` (`--api-key`
flag or interactive prompt) or the `MEMTOMEM_EMBEDDING__API_KEY` env var
(prefix `MEMTOMEM_`, nested delimiter `__`). A user who exports only
`OPENAI_API_KEY` sends unauthenticated requests — a silent failure on the
documented happy path. Reworded the Setup cell.

### 2. Extras table omitted `langfuse` (minor)

`pyproject.toml:51` defines a 7th extra `langfuse`, and `all` pulls it in
(`:52`). The Option C extras table listed only onnx/ollama/openai/korean/
code/web, so `all` = "All of the above" was literally inaccurate and a
reader couldn't discover the extra. Added the `langfuse` row.

### 3. `localhost` vs `127.0.0.1` (nit)

The CLI-reference block printed `http://localhost:8080` while the rest of
the guide (and the source default, `web.py` `--host` default `127.0.0.1`)
uses `http://127.0.0.1:8080`. Unified to the canonical form.

author: davmont
body:
## Problem

The `ext2` server never released an inode's extended-attribute block (`i_file_acl`) when the inode was deleted — it only cleared the field for *newly allocated* inodes. So every `unlink` of a file carrying an xattr block **leaked that block**: it stayed marked in-use in the block bitmap while referenced by nothing. `e2fsck` reports it as a block-bitmap difference.

This bites in practice because Linux attaches an xattr block to most files by default (e.g. the `security.selinux` label), so deleting such files on a real ext4/ext3/ext2 volume steadily leaks blocks. It surfaced while validating ext4 extent write (#271) and is independent of the block-mapping scheme.

## Fix

`put_inode()` now calls `free_xattr_block()` on the inode it is about to free. ext2/3/4 xattr blocks may be **shared** between inodes with identical attributes via a reference count in the block header, so this:
- decrements the header `h_refcount` and keeps the block when it is still shared;
- frees the block only when the last reference is gone;
- adjusts `i_blocks` for the released reference;
- leaves a missing/out-of-range/wrong-magic block untouched rather than risk freeing something unrelated.

This mirrors what Linux does and removes the only known source of `e2fsck` differences when round-tripping a default-feature Linux ext4 volume through the server.

## Validation (QEMU vs e2fsprogs 1.47.3)

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| delete file with **unshared** xattr block | block freed |
| delete one of two inodes **sharing** a block | `h_refcount` 2 → 1, block kept for survivor, its attrs intact |
| kept file | retains xattr block + contents (`security.selinux`, `user.*`) |
| `e2fsck -fn` after each | **clean (RC=0)** |
| real default-features ext4 (`ext_attr`/`extra_isize`/`huge_file`/`dir_nlink`, `mke2fs -d`) | mounts RW, create/append/truncate/unlink, **e2fsck RC=0** |

Independent of #271 (branches off `devel`); together they make a real Linux-made ext4 volume round-trip fully clean.

author: eeee2345
body:
This adds an additive, opt-in rule pack that maps the open-source Agent Threat Rules (ATR, MIT) detection signatures onto the A2A protocol threat surface: agent cards, inter-agent messages, capability declarations, tool descriptions, and registry entries. It mirrors the ATR pack already merged into cisco-ai-defense/skill-scanner (#79 and #99), applied here to a2a-scanner.

The pack is auto-discovered by the existing PackLoader and enabled with --rule-packs atr. No core rules, registry, loader, or unrelated code are changed; the diff is limited to a2ascanner/data/packs/atr/ and one test file.

Contents

- 24 signatures, 182 regex patterns, across 6 categories: agent_impersonation, message_injection, multi_agent_attack, capability_abuse, data_leakage, agent_card_spoofing.
- Every pattern is sourced from an ATR rule (MIT). Patterns are pinned to ATR commit 9f0991c34f359894e79afe2a7657b4c314b34f83, recorded in pack.yaml and the pack README.

False-positive discipline

- A realistic benign corpus (tests/benign_corpus/: devops/CI runner, db-admin, customer-support, billing-reporter, marketing/link, data-analytics) is the zero-false-positive gate. test_atr_pack.py asserts zero ATR findings on each benign card and across the corpus, and asserts the malicious control card is still detected.
- Conversational-tone rules that fired on benign self-description were dropped; several others were anchored to a structured malicious signal so they no longer match normal cards. The URL-shortener check is off by default. The zero-FP result is measured on the included corpus, not a universal guarantee.

Validation

- uv run pytest: full suite passes (adds 14 pack tests).
- uv run a2a-scanner validate-rules: pack manifest and all signatures load.

Disclosure: I maintain the upstream ATR project this pack draws from, and authored the merged skill-scanner ATR pack (#79, #99). Happy to adjust scope, severities, or category mapping to fit a2a-scanner's conventions.

author: antonioventilii
body:
# Motivation

oisy-trade's user-facing endpoints share one error envelope — `{ kind: variant { RequestError | TemporaryError | InternalError }; message }` — that says **whose fault a failure is and whether a retry can help**. The frontend was throwing that away (`new Error(Object.keys(kind)[0])`), so callers couldn't tell a transient hiccup (retry) from a client error (fix the input) from a canister bug (report).

# Changes

- `oisy-trade.errors.ts`: a shared mapper + typed errors (mirrors the Onramper pattern on `CanisterInternalError`):
  - `OisyTradeRequestError` — client/request fault, `retryable: false`.
  - `OisyTradeTemporaryError` — transient, `retryable: true`.
  - `OisyTradeUnexpectedError` — canister internal fault, `retryable: false`.
  Each carries `retryable` + the canister `reason` discriminant; prefers the canister's human `message`.
- `oisy-trade.canister.ts`: `getBalances` now throws via `mapOisyTradeError`.

The write methods (`deposit`/`withdraw`/`addLimitOrder`/`cancel`) live on the open feature branches; they adopt this mapper — and branch on `err instanceof OisyTradeTemporaryError` for retry UX — as those branches are finalized.

# Tests

Splits the styling-related props out of the base hook so `useTagPickerBase_unstable` produces a presentation-agnostic state, matching the base/styled convention used by the other `react-tag-picker` sub-components.

## Resumen

Diagnóstico y corrección completa del glitch visual en el Motorola G05 (ruido estático en el tablero AAC) + auditoría de toda la codebase. 18 bugs corregidos en 3 commits.

---

## Commit 1 — Fix Motorola G05 GPU rendering corruption

El teléfono mostraba ruido estático (textura GPU sin inicializar) en lugar de las tarjetas AAC.

| Causa raíz | Fix |
|---|---|
| Faltaba `-webkit-backdrop-filter` en 10 declaraciones CSS | Prefijo `-webkit-` añadido en todas |
| `height: 100dvh` sin fallback (WebView < Chrome 108 lo ignora) | Añadido `height: 100vh` como fallback previo |
| Sin `isolation: isolate` en `.app-container` | Las compositing layers del header/navbar ya no contaminan el grid AAC |
| Orden incorrecto del prefijo en onboarding overlay | Corregido (webkit siempre antes del estándar) |
| Service Worker con logs inconsistentes (v9 + "SW v6") | Bumpeado a v10, logs consistentes |

## Commit 2 — 9 runtime bugs (canvas, timers, storage)

| Severidad | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| CRÍTICO | `canvas.getContext('2d')` sin null check en `drawSensoryCanvas` | Guard `if (!ctx) return` |
| CRÍTICO | 5× `getContext('2d')` sin null check en notebook (draw/endDraw/resize/clear/export) | Guard individual en cada punto |
| CRÍTICO | `resizeCanvas` encadenaba `.getContext().drawImage()` | Dividido con guard |
| ALTO | `stopBreathingGuide` accedía `breathingRingText` sin null check | Guards individuales |
| ALTO | 5 labels de sliders sin null check | Optional access pattern |
| ALTO | Error de quota de localStorage silenciado | Muestra toast al usuario |
| MEDIO | Countdown del breathing no se limpiaba al detener | Nuevo `state.breathingCountdown` + cleanup |
| MEDIO | `JSON.parse` de journal logs sin try-catch | Wrapped con reset a `[]` |

## Commit 3 — Accessibility, audio, speech, i18n

| Área | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **WCAG 2.1** | `user-scalable=no` bloquea el zoom para baja visión | Eliminado del viewport meta |
| **ARIA** | `.aac-categories[role=tablist]` sin `aria-label` | Añadido `aria-label` |
| **i18n** | `journal.save_error` referenciado en código pero faltaba en dict (8 idiomas) | Añadido en es/en/it/fr/de/zh/pt/ja |

| **Speech** | `SpeechRecognition` nueva instancia sin abortar la anterior | `recognition.abort()` antes de crear nueva |
| **Speech** | `onerror` silencioso — usuario no sabe si el micrófono fue denegado | Toast en `not-allowed` + reset `aria-label` |
| **Toast** | DOM accumulation si se llama rápido | Remove existing antes de append |

author: mergify[bot]
body:
# 🦟 Bug fix

Probably fixes #760 

## Summary
There is potential race condition in the  `PeerTracker` around the `this->peers`  member variable (which is a  `std::map<std::string, PeerState>`).

In C++,  `std::map`  is not thread-safe for concurrent read and write operations. If one thread writes to the map while another is reading it without synchronization, it leads to undefined behavior.

1. Heartbeat Thread (`heartbeatThread`): This thread is spawned by `PeerTracker` and continuously runs `PeerTracker::HeartbeatLoop()` in the background to publish heartbeats and clean up stale peers.
2. Transport Callback Threads: gz-transport  runs internal thread pools to handle incoming messages. When a  heartbeat  or  announce  message is received, callbacks like  `OnPeerHeartbeat`  or  `OnPeerAnnounce`  are invoked on these background threads.

- Unsynchronized Read: In  `PeerTracker::HeartbeatLoop()` , the heartbeat thread iterated over  `this->peers`  to calculate the age of each peer and check if they had gone stale: 
```
for (auto peer : this->peers) { ... }
```
This read operation was performed without holding the  peersMutex  lock.
- Concurrent Write: At the same time, when a new heartbeat message was received from another peer, a transport callback thread would invoke  `PeerTracker::OnPeerHeartbeat()`, which inserts or updates entries in the same `this->peers`  map. This write operation was protected by  peersMutex , but since the read in  HeartbeatLoop  did not acquire the lock, the synchronization was incomplete.

Im guessing this could be a reason for potential flakes.

### Motivation

- Make the chapter revision cockpit more reliable and deterministic by improving attention states, recommended actions, and refresh behavior after relevant learning events. 
- Ensure the cockpit remains read-only, compact and does not require a full page reload to reflect changes. 
- Surface partial loader failures without breaking the whole cockpit and avoid rendering stale overview data for the wrong chapter. 

### Description

- Add a canonical list of supported warning ids as `CHAPTER_LEARNING_WARNING_IDS` and introduce new attention states and mapping for extraction-related and partial errors in `services/project-chapter-learning-overview.js`. 
- Emit deterministic recommended actions tied to existing layouts (e.g. `cours`, `connaissances`, `cartes`, `quiz`, `exercices`) and change upload-related actions to target the `exercices` layout rather than introducing direct upload behavior. 
- Harden partial-failure handling by collecting `sectionErrors` and pushing a `partial_overview_error` plus specialized `exercise_extraction_error` / `correction_extraction_error` warnings while still returning available section data.

- Add a stale-data guard in `views/project-situations/project-situations-view.js` so the cockpit renders overview data only when `overview.projectId` and `overview.chapterId` match the current project and selected chapter. 
- Keep the cockpit UI compact and read-only; avoid duplicating full tab content or adding scoring/student-progress UI. 
- Add tests: `apps/web/js/services/project-chapter-learning-overview.test.mjs` (extended) and a new `apps/web/js/views/project-chapter-learning-cockpit-refresh-source.test.mjs` to assert warning ids, deterministic actions, layout targets, event-driven refresh, stale-data guard and forbidden integrations.

author: jeffmhopkins
body:
## The "Couldn't start the session" 502, root-caused

On-box debugging (jcode enabled, all three containers up) showed `POST /api/jcode/sessions → 502` with **no request ever reaching the jcode control server**. Cause: the api proxies to `http://jcode:9100`, but that service lives **only on the isolated `jcode` network** — and the **api was on `[edge, internal]` only**, never joined to `jcode`. So it couldn't resolve/reach the control server, and every create 502'd. (It could reach `local-llm` only because that's also on `internal`.)

Wave J2's design says "the api joins the jcode network to proxy the control surface" — the compose just never reflected it.

## Fix
Add `jcode` to the api's networks: `[edge, internal, jcode]`.

- **Stock deploy unaffected:** the `jcode` network is empty (no jcode profile up) and the api's jcode client stays fail-closed.
- **Sandbox isolation preserved:** `jcode` + `claude-shim` stay on the `jcode` network *only* (off `internal`), so the arbitrary-code sandbox still can't reach db/worker/blobs. The api being reachable *from* the sandbox is the inherent, **auth-gated** tradeoff of proxying its control surface (no owner data without a session).

## Test
`test_jcode_compose.py` regression-guards the api↔jcode wiring **and** the sandbox's network isolation (jcode/shim on `jcode` only, profile-gated).

## To apply on the box
`sudo jbrain update` (pulls the compose + recreates the api on the jcode network) → "Start session" should reach the control server.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
## Why I'm doing this

Fix: https://github.com/StarRocks/StarRocksTest/issues/11482

## Why I'm doing this

A heap-use-after-free (caught by ASAN) can crash the BE when a window function with a skew hint on `PARTITION BY` runs at DOP>1:

```
heap-use-after-free in Cow<Column>::ImmutPtr::operator->()
  READ  : Chunk::num_rows()      <- OrderedPartitionExchanger::accept()     (thread T296)
  FREED : Chunk::append_column() <- Analytor::_output_result_chunk()        (thread T295)
```

**Root cause:** `OrderedPartitionExchanger::accept()` hands a chunk to the downstream sources (`add_chunk`) and then retains references into that same chunk — `_previous_chunk` and `_previous_partition_columns` (which alias the chunk's partition-key columns for `SlotRef` keys). On the next `accept()`, it reads `_previous_chunk->num_rows()` and `compare_at()` on those columns to test the partition join between consecutive chunks. But the chunk has already been consumed by the downstream `AnalyticSinkOperator`, whose `_output_result_chunk()` reuses the input chunk as its output and mutates it on another thread:

- `append_column()` reallocates the chunk's `_columns` vector → the reported UAF on `num_rows()`.
- On the LIMIT path, `set_num_rows()` → `as_mutable_raw_ptr()->resize()` resizes every column in place (bypassing COW) → races with `compare_at()` and can index out of bounds.

The exchanger violates the pipeline contract that a chunk handed downstream is owned by the consumer. The bug has existed since `OrderedPartitionExchanger` was introduced (#35486); the analytic operator already reused and mutated the input chunk by then (#34312). It only triggers with a window skew hint + `PARTITION BY` + DOP>1, which is why it escaped routine testing.

## What I'm doing

Stop retaining anything that aliases a chunk handed downstream. `accept()` only needs the previous chunk's last-row partition key to compare against the next chunk's first row, so:

- Replace `ChunkPtr _previous_chunk` / `Columns _previous_partition_columns` (aliasing the chunk) with an owned single-row copy of the boundary key, plus a `bool _has_previous` sentinel.
- Add `_clone_partition_key_row()` which deep-copies just the last row of each partition-key column.
- Clone the boundary row before the chunk is published via `add_chunk()` — i.e. while it is still exclusively owned by the current driver thread — so the clone itself is race-free without locks. After publishing, the exchanger only ever reads its own copy.

The clone is one row × a few key columns per chunk (negligible vs. the sort+window work), and is robust against any downstream in-place chunk mutation, not just the two known today.

author: shawndaprawn
body:
## Problem

Clients receive article links by email. On devices where the installed PWA captures in-scope links (notably Android with "open supported links" enabled), tapping the link launched the **portal-only PWA** instead of the browser. The PWA's `StandaloneRedirect` then treated `/resources/article/:slug` as a marketing route and bounced the client to the sign-in screen — so they could **never reach the article**.

## Fix

Article routes are now handled as a special case so a shared article link always lands on the public website:

- **`isArticleRoute` helper** (`src/utils/pwa/articleRoute.ts`) — centralises detection of `/resources/article/:slug`.
- **`StandaloneRedirect`** no longer bounces article routes into the portal (it explicitly excludes them, even though they live under `/resources`).
- **`ArticleBrowserRedirect`** (new) — when the installed PWA lands on an article route in standalone mode, it renders a focused, branded interstitial that:
  - fires a single best-effort `window.open(...)` so capable browsers jump straight to the website, and
  - shows a guaranteed tap-to-open **"Read article in browser"** button (works even when auto-open is blocked because there's no user gesture on launch), plus a **"Continue to the app instead"** escape hatch.
- Mounted in `MainLayout` alongside `StandaloneRedirect`.

The canonical website host (`SITE_ORIGIN`) is used so the link opens on `www.navigatewealth.co` regardless of the PWA's origin.

**Normal browser tabs are completely unaffected** — the component renders nothing and the article page renders as usual. The behaviour only triggers in genuine standalone (installed PWA) mode.

## Tests

- `articleRoute.test.ts` — route matching (slug required, listing/other routes excluded).
- `StandaloneRedirect.test.tsx` — marketing routes still bounce; article routes do **not**; no-op in a normal tab.
- `ArticleBrowserRedirect.test.tsx` — renders nothing in browser / non-article routes; shows interstitial + auto-opens the canonical website URL when standalone; "continue to app" navigates to the portal.

All new tests pass; `typecheck` and `eslint` are clean on the changed files.

author: hoangsonww
body:
## Problem

When a user opens an input modal (text / voice / face) on the Home page and submits to the backend, the full-screen **loading overlay renders *below* the modal** instead of covering it. The overlay has `position: fixed; z-index: 2000` and the MUI modal default z-index is `1300`, so a naive read says the overlay should win — but it doesn't.

## Root cause — stacking-context trap, not a z-index value

The route wrapper `.page-anim` (wraps every routed page) carried a **persistent** `will-change: transform, opacity`.

`will-change: transform` establishes a **stacking context even when no transform is applied at rest**. That confines every `position: fixed` descendant — including the loading overlay — to `.page-anim`'s body-level stacking level (effectively `z-index: auto` / ~0).

MUI `Modal` portals to `<body>` with `z-index: 1300`. Since `.page-anim`'s context sits at ~0 at the body level, the modal and all its contents paint **above the entire `.page-anim` subtree**, overlay included — no matter that the overlay's internal value is `2000`.

The CSS already had a comment ("No transform at rest so position:fixed descendants behave normally") and zeroed out the resting `transform`, but missed that `will-change` alone is enough to create the trap.

## Fix

Scope `will-change` to only the active `enter` / `appear` / `exit` transition phases instead of the resting `.page-anim`. At rest, `.page-anim` no longer creates a stacking context, so the fixed overlay competes at the document level (`2000 > 1300`) and correctly covers the modal.

- ✅ Overlay now covers the text / voice / face modals during inference.
- ✅ Page-transition animation unchanged — `will-change` perf hint is still present during the frames that actually animate.
- ✅ Root-cause fix: un-traps fixed descendants on **every** route, not just this modal.
- ✅ No JS changes, no z-index escalation, no `!important`.

## Testing

- `npx prettier --write` clean (no diff).
- Manual: open Home → pick a mode → submit → overlay sits on top of the modal and backdrop.

CRM Plus風に「配信中のメニュー」と「配信終了したメニュー」を分けて表示してほしいという河原さん要望。LINE Messaging APIには「アーカイブ」概念がないので、ハーネス側で**動的に判定**して画面を分ける実装。

|---|---|
| **使用中** | デフォルトメニュー OR aliasから参照されているメニュー |

author: unnfazzed
body:
Lands the P0/P1 findings from the first-principles gstack eng review of the merged mobile Phase 1 (two independent passes + a self-pass). Both passes **independently converged on the same P0** — a concurrent refresh-token race that would log customers out constantly.

## P0 — auth (`src/api/client.ts`, `src/auth/auth-context.tsx`)
- **Single-flight, rotation-aware refresh.** The backend *rotates* refresh tokens and the order screen runs two 4s pollers, so when the access token expires both requests 401, both refresh with the same token, and the second hits a just-revoked session → false sign-out. Now one in-flight refresh is shared; if another request already rotated, the current session is reused instead of signing out.
- **Rotated token persisted before retry.** `onTokens` is now async and `await`ed inside the refresh path, so a crash mid-rotation can't lose the single-use refresh token (previously fire-and-forget `void saveSession`).

## P1
- **Delivery code survives remount/relaunch** (`app/order/[id].tsx`, `src/auth/session.ts`). It was held only in component state and lost forever on navigation — the customer could never relay the handover code. Now persisted per-order in SecureStore (loaded on mount) **plus a "Re-issue delivery code" button** that calls the existing `rotate` endpoint.
- **Input safety** (`app/home.tsx`, `src/util.ts`). Locale-safe `parseNum` (comma decimals → `.`, a real Zimbabwe-keyboard risk), and the form now gates on **all four coordinates** being finite — an empty longitude was passing as `0` → a Gulf-of-Guinea pickup. Submit is disabled until valid.
- **Socket robustness** (`src/realtime/use-order-socket.ts`). Keyed on the access token (no reconnect storm on every session change), recovers the **first GPS fix** when the snapshot rider is still null, drops the redundant optimistic write, and refetches on `connect_error`. The order screen also **polls at 10s during active statuses** so tracking self-heals if the WS drops.
- **Keyboard avoidance** on the tall create-order form.

## P2 — hardening
- `config.ts` **fails loudly** instead of shipping a `localhost` API URL in a release; `app.json` drops the localhost default and adds the `expo-location` iOS usage string; `getCurrentPositionAsync` wrapped in try/catch with `accuracy`.
- `CUSTOMER_CANCELLABLE_STATUSES` promoted to `@lynia/shared` so the mobile cancel affordance and the server rule (`order-lifecycle.service.ts`) can't drift.

## Verification-corrected
The adversarial pass called missing `react-native-reanimated` a P0 "won't boot." **Verified false** — no unmet-peer warning, and Expo Router's default native `<Stack>` doesn't need it. Deferred to Phase 2, noted in `docs/BACKLOG.md` (along with HTTPS-for-device, native map, a11y).

## Verification
- `pnpm --filter @lynia/mobile typecheck` clean (CI gate); **102 API tests pass** (the shared-enum change keeps the lifecycle cancel tests green). Runtime exercise of the refresh fix / code re-issue needs a device — flagged.

author: oobabooga
body:
On a 24 GB desktop card, loading a 27B GGUF would pin `-ngl -1`, then silently offload layers back to CPU at runtime and run at roughly half speed. Reported in #6682 (Qwen3.6-27B-MTP, ~14 tok/s instead of 30-35).

Closes #6682

## Problem

The GGUF auto-fit (#6312) reserves a flat 5% of total VRAM before sizing context. On a 24 GB card that is only ~1.2 GB, too thin to absorb what the byte estimate can't capture exactly: the CUDA context and compute buffers, and the gap between nvidia-smi's reported free and the VRAM CUDA actually exposes. So auto-fit sizes the context right up against the card's real usable limit. At that edge part of the load ends up on host RAM and generation roughly halves, even with nothing else on the card.

Clean-card context sweep for `Qwen3.6-27B-MTP` UD-Q4_K_XL, q8 KV, on an idle RTX 3090 (24 GB):

| context | tok/s |
|---|---|
| 32k-92k | 60 (full speed) |
| 102k | 47 |
| 113k (what #6312 picks) | ~35 |
| 131k | 27 |

At the ~113k that 5% advertises, the 27B is already down to ~35 of 60 tok/s with the GPU sitting ~1 GB short of full and host RAM climbing (the load is not staying fully on the device). Backing the context off restores full speed. A desktop or browser sharing the GPU makes it worse: at `-c 112128` with a 3.5 GB desktop held, it ran at 14.6 tok/s (reporter: 14.3).

## Fix

Floor the reserve: `min(max(0.05*total, 3072 MiB), 0.125*total)`. So the reserve is 5% base, floored at 3 GiB, capped at 12.5%:

- <= 24 GB: 12.5% (3 GiB on a 24 GB card)
- 24-60 GB: flat 3 GiB (a shrinking fraction)
- \>= 60 GB: 5% (datacenter cards unchanged)

The floor is a per-pool cushion. The desktop drift and the one-lump layer-split compute buffer it covers are not per-device, so it is applied once across the pool, not per GPU. It lives in one helper (`_pooled_usable_mib`) at the single place the auto-context budget is computed. Ranking and the tensor-parallel paths are untouched.

## Speed (RTX 3090, 24 GB)

Same model and card, measured idle and with a 1 GB desktop sharing the GPU:

| reserve | context | tok/s (idle) | tok/s (1 GB desktop) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5% (#6312) | 113408 | ~35 (spilling) | ~23 |
| floored (this PR) | 66560 | 60 | 60 |

The fix holds full speed through a ~1 GB desktop. It is a fixed cushion, not a guarantee. A 27B with a ~3 GB desktop on 24 GB is at the card's edge (the fix gives 21.9 vs 14.6 there), and a steady desktop gets sized down to a smaller full-speed context instead.

Generalizes across architecture and cache type:
- `gemma-3-27b` (SWA): #6312 picks 122880 at 23 tok/s; fix picks 78592 at 40 tok/s (full speed).
- f16, q8, q4 KV all land at ~21 GB footprint and full speed (fix picks 33k, 66k, 98k for the same safe footprint).

## No context regression for models that already fit

Base (#6312) vs fix, same hardware. Only the two 27Bs that were spilling get reduced. Everything else is byte-identical:

| model | #6312 ctx | fix ctx |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-1.7B | 40960 | 40960 |
| gemma-4-12b | 262144 | 262144 |
| gemma-3-27b | 122880 (spilled) | 78592 |
| Qwen3.6-27B | 113408 (spilled) | 66560 |
| Qwen3.6-27B on a 49 GB card | 262144 | 262144 |

## Multi-GPU

The per-pool floor matters here. On a constrained 49+24 GB pool (neither card fits the model alone), a naive per-device floor would reserve 3 GiB per card and drop to the 4096 fallback with `--fit`. The per-pool floor pins both GPUs at 36352, 74 tok/s, no spill.

## Verification

- 6 new unit tests on the reserve helpers: floor, cap, and datacenter regimes, single-GPU pool, floor-applied-once-across-pool (the multi-GPU case), and the unknown-total (MIG/vGPU) carve-out.
- VRAM, fit, MTP, tensor-parallel, and datacenter suites green (666 passed).
- End-to-end through Studio on real hardware (RTX 3090 and RTX 6000 Ada): the loads in the tables above, plus the loaded 27B serves 102/102 spec-compliance tests at 67 tok/s with no spill.

Code change is ~50 lines (two helpers and one call-site swap). The rest is tests.

author: fw-bot
body:
Steps to reproduce the bug:
- Create a Purchase Order with 2 products and confirm it
- Note the receipt's deadline (= date_planned of both lines)
- Set the quantity of one PO line to 0
- Update the scheduled date (date_planned) of the purchase order

Problem:
the receipt deadline does not update.
The receipt kept the old deadline from the cancelled move. When a PO line qty is set to 0, `_merge_moves` cancels the corresponding stock move via `_action_cancel`. Then `_update_move_date_deadline` correctly skips cancelled moves (filtered by `state not in ('done', 'cancel')`), so the cancelled move retains its original `date_deadline`. However, `_compute_date_deadline` on `stock.picking` used
`move_ids.filtered('date_deadline')`, which not checks move state, so the stale deadline of the cancelled move was included in the min/max computation.

## Summary

**What:** An interactive explorer for the Australian Government's BITRE Domestic Airline On Time Performance data — 22 years (118,000 rows) of on-time, delay and cancellation figures for every competitive domestic route and airline, turned into a fast consumer tool.
**Audience:** Australian travellers comparing airlines/routes before booking, nervous flyers, frequent flyers and aviation watchers.
**Data:** BITRE Domestic Airline On Time Performance (data.gov.au), refreshed monthly via a GitHub Actions pipeline.
**Stack:** Vanilla TypeScript + Vite + Vitest (51 tests). Leaflet for the map; every other chart hand-rolled in SVG.

🔗 **GitHub Pages:** https://ben-gy.github.io/au-flights/
🔗 **Custom domain:** https://au-flights.benrichardson.dev *(live after DNS + cert — see REVIEW.md)*

## Features

- Airline punctuality leaderboard with year-on-year trend arrows and sparklines, plus per-airline 22-year history
- Sortable/filterable route table with a deep-linkable slide-in drill-down (airline breakdown + trend) per route
- Leaflet map of 44 airports and the routes between them, coloured by on-time rate
- Hand-rolled force-directed network graph, filterable by airline
- 22-year national trend with the COVID-19 collapse marked
- Airline × airport on-time matrix heatmap, plus a month-of-year and year×month seasonality heatmap
- Auto-generated insights (worst/best routes, cancellation spikes, most improved/worsened airlines)
- Plain-language glossary tooltips on all jargon + an About panel

## Data Sources

| Source | URL | Update Frequency |
|--------|-----|-----------------|
| BITRE Domestic Airline On Time Performance | https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/domestic-airline-on-time-performance | Monthly |

## Value Proposition

BITRE publishes authoritative on-time data but only as a 9.6 MB CSV no traveller can use. This makes it instantly answerable: which airline and route is most reliable, what to avoid, and when delays peak — with a route map, network graph and 22-year trend no other consumer site offers.

- **Scrollback opt-in (#4)** — on-disk scrollback is **off by default**, opt-in via `halo-persist-scrollback = true` (daemon reads it from config). Terminal output can hold secrets, so it no longer persists by default.
- **Plugin trust (#5)** — `SECURITY.md` documents the trust model (arbitrary code from git URLs, keystroke injection), scrollback, IPC perms, sandbox stance; install notice mentions plugins run their own code.
- **Hygiene (#7)** — `install.sh` copies halo+halod+halo-attach to PATH (with `mkdir -p`/sudo hint) instead of symlinking into `.build`; documented `halo-persist-scrollback` in README + live docs.

Separately staged (not in this PR): the macOS-only GhosttyKit framework is published as release `ghostkit-1` and a URL+checksum `binaryTarget` is ready — it activates when the repo is public (SwiftPM can't fetch a private repo's asset).

author: mekenthompson
body:
## Summary

`src/auth/account-refresh.ts` presented the wrong `client_id` (`9d1cd16e-…`) on the OAuth refresh exchange, so Anthropic rejected every refresh with `400 invalid_request: Client with id … not found`. Corrected to the real Claude Code OAuth client `9d1c250a-…` (the one the `claude` CLI's own login/setup-token flow uses).

## Why it went unnoticed

The wrong id had been here since the primitive landed (#621/#1254), but the bug was **latent**: every historical switchroom account was a long-lived `setup-token` (`user:inference`, ~1y expiry) that **never hits the refresh path**. The first full Claude-Code **session token** (broad scopes, ~8h expiry) added to the broker exercised the dead code — refresh `400`'d every ~8h and the account silently expired.

**Real incident:** `ken@autograb.com.au` (2026-06-26) — active account, token expired, manual `switchroom auth refresh` reproduced the 400. Swapping to `9d1c250a-…` made the refresh succeed immediately (verified live).

## Changes

- `src/auth/account-refresh.ts` — `DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID` → `9d1c250a-…`, exported, with a header doc explaining the latent-bug history. `SWITCHROOM_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` env override preserved.
- `src/auth/account-refresh.test.ts` (new) — pins the value, asserts the refresh **request body** carries it (hermetic tmp-home + capturing fetcher), and verifies the env/opts override.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest run src/auth/account-refresh.test.ts` — 3 pass
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `check-no-pii-secrets`, `check-bun-test-imports` clean
- [x] Live: refresh on the real broker now succeeds with the corrected id

## Risk

Low. `client_id` is a public identifier, not a secret. The other accounts never refresh (long-lived setup-tokens), so the only behavioral change is that short-lived session tokens can now actually refresh. No invariant touched (still the subscription OAuth, no API/SDK).
