author: alami-amine
body:
#### Summary

##### Problem

- `chip::Callback::Cancelable` (`src/lib/core/CHIPCallback.h`) deletes its copy constructor but not its copy-assignment operator. Its data members are intrusive cancelable-list links (`mNext`/`mPrev`), so it is non-copy-constructible yet **still copy-assignable** via a defaulted, shallow `operator=` that copies those links.
- That asymmetry propagates to every class holding a `Callback` by value: such a class is non-copy-constructible (its implicit copy-ctor is deleted) but **still copy-assignable** — its implicit copy-assignment shallow-copies the `Callback` member's list links, and any self-referential buffer view the class owns. Examples: `DefaultOTARequestor`, `CommissioningWindowOpener`, `AndroidLogDownloadFromNode`.

##### Impact

- A copy-assignment of such an object would corrupt the intrusive cancelable lists (two nodes sharing `mNext`/`mPrev`) and shallow-copy any self-referential span. No code does this today, but nothing prevents it, and the deleted copy-constructor gives a false impression that these types are non-copyable.

##### Solution

- Delete `Cancelable::operator=` as well, completing the rule-of-three (copy construction is already deleted). `Cancelable` becomes fully non-copyable, and every `Callback`-holding class becomes non-copy-assignable automatically — one root fix rather than per-class `= delete`s, and it also covers future `Callback` holders.

##### Caveats

- Hardening only; no behavior change. Nothing in the tree currently copy-assigns a `Callback`/`Cancelable`.

#### Testing

- Rebuilt the device-side tree under AddressSanitizer with the change — `examples/energy-gateway-app/linux` plus the `src/` unit tests and `src/controller` controller wheels it pulls in (~2250 targets): everything compiles, confirming nothing copy-assigns a `Callback` today. A repo-wide grep for `Callback` copy-assignment also found none.
- Confirmed with a `static_assert(!std::is_copy_assignable<...>)` probe that a representative holder (`DefaultOTARequestor`) changes from copy-assignable to non-copy-assignable with this change.

author: jamesmarkeyuk
body:
## Problem

The daily discussion topic appeared **twice** in the General feed — two "Today's topic" cards with identical text but separate reply threads (1 reply vs 3 replies in the report).

## Root cause

The rotation in `maybePostDailyTopic()` decided whether a topic already existed by reading `postsByTab.general`, which comes from the per-tab feed listener:

```js
.where('tab', '==', tab).limit(60)   // no orderBy
```

With no `orderBy`, Firestore returns docs ordered by **document id**. Topic ids are `topic-YYYY-MM-DD`, which sort late lexicographically, so once the General feed held more than ~60 posts the live topic silently dropped out of the snapshot.

`decideDailyTopic` then saw no current topic, took the **bootstrap** branch, and posted a fresh index-0 topic under a new day's doc id (`topic-<newday>`) with `replacePostId: null` — so the original topic was **never deleted**. That produced two identical index-0 topics with independent threads. `cleanOldPosts()` also explicitly skips `isTopic`, so the orphan lingered indefinitely.

## Fix (`js/anonymous.js`)

- **Authoritative read** — the rotation now fetches topics with a direct `where('isTopic','==',true)` query (immune to the 60-doc cap) and merges them over the snapshot before deciding, so it never re-bootstraps over a hidden topic. Falls back to the snapshot if the read fails.
- **Sweep to one** — keeps only the newest topic doc and deletes the rest, healing any existing duplicates even when no new topic is due.
- **Render-side guard** — new `dedupeTopics()` ensures the feed only ever surfaces the newest topic, so the UI can't show two threads regardless of the underlying Firestore state.

Also bumps `service-worker.js` `CACHE_NAME` to `bipolarbear-v106` so existing clients pick up the change.

## Testing

- `node --check` passes on both changed files.
- No automated test suite exists for this module; the logic was verified by tracing the snapshot/rotation interaction against the reported screenshot.

author: jthrilly
body:
Closes complexdatacollective/network-canvas-monorepo#701

Controls in a field's prefix/suffix slot (Generate buttons, clear, the number steppers) are part of the field *conceptually* but were not *mechanically*: `useField`/`InputField` validate-on-blur keyed off the inner `<input>`'s blur, so moving focus to an in-field control was treated as "leaving the field" and left a **stale error** (e.g. *"Identifier cannot be empty"* on a field that was just populated). This makes the **field container the unit of focus** for both validation and styling, and gives slots a first-class way to set the value.

## Changes

- **Container-scoped validation** (`useField`): a `handleContainerBlur` on the field container skips validation when focus moves to a descendant control (`e.currentTarget.contains(e.relatedTarget)`); `onBlur` moved from `fieldProps` to `containerProps`. Single-control fields behave identically; multi-control fields (RadioGroup, Combobox, DatePicker…) get strictly better behaviour (intra-widget focus moves no longer mis-fire validation).
- **Slot field controller** (`InputField`): `prefixComponent`/`suffixComponent` now also accept a render function `(field) => ReactNode` receiving a `FieldSlotController` (`{ name, value, setValue, validate, focusInput }`), so a slot control can set + validate the value without importing the form store. Delivered via the new `useFieldController` hook / `FieldController` context. The plain `ReactNode` form is unchanged (additive, opt-in). Because `setValue` routes through the change handler, a generated value clears a pre-existing error.
- **Focus indication**: slot controls stay real tab stops with native button semantics and render their own design-system focus ring (`Button`/`IconButton` already do) — one ring per focused element, no double-ring. The `InputField` wrapper un-clips (`overflow-visible`) while a slot control is focus-visible so its offset ring isn't clipped by the rounded container.
- **Escape hatch**: `validateOnControlBlur` on `Field` restores validation when focus moves to an in-field control.
- **Audit**: removed now-dead injected `onBlur` forwarding from `TextArea`, `ToggleField`, `DatePicker`, `RelativeDatePicker`, `RichTextEditor`, and `SegmentedCodeField`'s hand-rolled blur containment (the container now owns it). `RichTextEditor` keeps tiptap's own value-commit `onBlur`.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`InputFieldContainerValidation.test.tsx`): touch-then-empty → focus a slot button → no stale error; `setValue` populates without a stale error; leaving the whole field validates; `setValue` clears a pre-existing error once blurred.
- **Storybook** (`Field.stories.tsx`): keyboard regression (Tab input→Generate→no error flash→activate→Tab out) and number-stepper keyboard; documents the keyboard model.

## Verification

`pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm knip`, lint/format, and the fresco-ui unit suite (671 passing) are green. The focus-ring clipping fix was verified in Storybook: simulating the ring under `overflow: hidden` shows it clipped top/bottom; `overflow: visible` shows it wrapping the button fully.

author: nexus-cw
body:
## Summary

First step toward bringing **cairn-server to convergence-core parity**, heading for the chosen destination — the **privacy/embargo enforcement point**.

**Architecture reality** (from a full survey, recorded in `docs/cairn/specs/2026-06-26-cairn-server-parity.md`): the running server is the older git-hosting model (`internal/repo`); `internal/change` (the whole convergence engine) is imported by **zero** server paths. The server is a faithful but **blind git locker** — it stores `refs/cairn/*` opaquely (so cairn↔cairn fidelity already works *by accident*) but can't read the change-graph it hosts. The dead `ChangeService` gRPC facade was never registered.

**Slice 0 makes the server convergence-AWARE, read-only** (zero behavior change, off the hot path):
- `change.OpenBare(bareDir)` — opens an engine whose git store **is** an existing bare repo (the server's layout, vs the CLI's nested `dir/objects.git`), with an **in-memory** catalogue reconstructed from the pushed `refs/cairn/meta` via `LoadFromMeta`. No server-side `.cairn/cairn.db` — the meta ref is the single source of truth (nothing extra to keep coherent under concurrent pushes).
- `change.Engine.OpenConflictCount()` — cheap health read.
- `repo.Service.OpenChangeEngine` / `ChangeGraph` — open the engine for a hosted repo, summarize its line tree + open-conflict count.

This de-risks the one real unknown (can the engine open + read the server's bare store) before any feature rides on it.

## Latent bug fixed along the way

The single-connection in-memory engine surfaced an anti-pattern in `GetLineTree`: it issued nested queries (`sealedTip → OpenChangeForLine`) **while iterating the line-rows cursor**, which deadlocks a 1-connection engine and worked on the on-disk engine only by luck of multiple connections. Now it materializes the rows before the per-line ahead computation — correct regardless of connection model.

## Roadmap (in the spec)

Slice 0 (this) → 1 introspection API → 2 convergence-correct protection → **4 private store + redacted serve → 5 per-identity gating → 6 embargo/Disclose** → (7 multi-agent hub, later).

## Test Plan
- [x] `OpenBare` + `LoadFromMeta` reconstruct the line tree from a pushed meta (+ the empty/no-meta case).
- [x] `repo.ChangeGraph` wiring end-to-end on a real hosted bare.
- [x] `GetLineTree` tests still pass (the materialize-rows fix).
- [x] Full `go test ./...` green with git identity stripped.

author: meawoppl
body:
## What

Hardens the gameplay protocol validation shared by HTTP and WebSocket clients:

- Adds shared validators/constants for commit hashes, reveal secrets, chat text, and strategy summaries.
- Requires commits to use canonical 64-char lowercase SHA-256 hex before entering session/engine state.
- Requires reveal secrets to parse as `<throw>:<hex nonce>` and fit a 256-byte cap before forwarding/verifying.
- Applies the same chat and strategy-summary caps on the WebSocket path that HTTP already had.
- Keeps malformed WS commit/reveal/chat payloads retryable with `Error` + continue instead of persisting/forwarding them.

## Why

This addresses part of the security-audit lane: malformed or oversized protocol payloads could previously reach unbounded WS/session queues, DB transcript writes, or SHA-256 verification work. It does not implement global rate limiting or turn deadlines; those are separate throttle work.

author: greg-flux
body:
## Summary

Make turbo-surf **look like a real Chrome** across every layer, rotate that identity across a fleet, and plug in (or debug) anti-bot challenge solving. Reported by a Meta user: surf fused a stock reqwest+rustls client with a bare `turbo-surf/0.1` UA — an instant WAF tell.

## What's in it

**1. Chrome HTTP headers** (default, rustls, zero new deps) — real Chrome 149 UA + full nav header set (`sec-ch-ua`, `sec-fetch-*`, …), verified against a live real-Chrome capture.

**2. `impersonate` feature** (opt-in, BoringSSL via `wreq` 6-rc) — real Chrome **149** JA3/JA4 + Akamai HTTP-2 fingerprint. One `http_backend` alias swaps the backend; off by default (needs cmake/nasm). Live fingerprint e2e passes.

**3. Render-tier `navigator`** — `ENV_BOOTSTRAP` installs a coherent Chrome 149 macOS `navigator` (`platform`/`vendor`/`webdriver:false`/plugins/`window.chrome`) + masks `Function.prototype.toString` so polyfills report `[native code]`. Killed the `turbo-surf`/`turbo-test` tell.

**4. Fingerprint seed pool** (`turbo-surf-core::fingerprint`) — ~4000 internally-coherent real-Chrome identities, deterministic by client key (FNV-1a): stable per host, spread across the fleet. Opt-in via `FetchOptions.profile`; default reproduces prior wire bytes.

**5. Challenge solver** (`turbo-surf-core::challenge`) — detect a JS/PoW wall (Akamai/DataDome/Kasada/Cloudflare) → hand to a server-side solver (`ScrapflySolver`/`HyperSolver`) → replay cleared cookies. Configured via env / `.env` (`.env.example`), inert until a key is set. `SolveContext.proxy` for IP/JA3 token pinning.

**6. Wired into the product** — MCP session (per-host profile + auto detect/solve/replay through `fetch_into`) and `TurboNavigator` (the crawl seam, opt-in solver).

**7. Debug/probe mode** (`probe_globals` + MCP `probe` tool) — run a page's JS with `navigator`/`screen`/`window.chrome`/canvas instrumented; report what fingerprinting code touched + which reads returned `undefined` (the shim to-do list). Recon for getting past consistency gates.

## Gate
- **Default:** `cargo test --workspace`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets` (0 warnings), `fmt` — all clean.
- **Impersonate:** core clippy clean + lib tests + live fingerprint e2e green on Chrome 149; MCP binary builds with `--features impersonate`.

## Scope / honesty
- Self-solving the active canvas/WebGL/PoW layer in-isolate is **not** included (no raster/GPU; the VMs re-obfuscate) — that's what the solver adapters + `probe` recon are for. Tier-3 analysis in the thread.
- `impersonate` pulls pre-release `wreq`/`wreq-util` (only crate with Chrome 149); the default build never sees them.
- Not a release — no version bump / tag.

body:
## What

Reworks `README.md` to be KISS and approachable for non-technical users — focused on storytelling and the customer's perspective rather than implementation detail.

## Why

The old README led with mechanics (immutable sources, identity profiles, source traceability, an ASCII pipeline). A newcomer couldn't tell *why* they'd want this. The rewrite answers "why does this exist?" before "how does it work?"

## The new arc

1. **The problem** — you read a lot, you forget it, note apps become a graveyard because the upkeep is tedious.
2. **The idea** — let the AI do the boring part, and make it personal: it filters by *who you are* and gets sharper over time. (Distills the Karpathy + Baljanak gists into plain English.)
3. **Install** — one copy-paste line you hand to your AI; no manual clone/cd/edit-yaml steps surfaced.
4. **The four commands that matter** — `add`, `ingest`, `lint`, `filter evolve` — each one plain sentence + one example, framed as a simple loop.

- `Bash 4+`, `symlinks`, `seeds your config`, and other developer jargon

author: oomkapwn
body:
## Test-infra [release-blocker, recursion of rc.20]
rc.20 converted the 6 wall-clock timing tests' NEGATIVE controls to `quad / linear > 8` ("ratio, robust to runner speed"). But a `coverage` job flaked: **`quad/linear = 7.50 < 8`**. Root cause: the **`linear` denominator is a sub-millisecond op whose wall-clock is noise-dominated on a contended CI runner** (~43 ms there vs ~2.5 ms locally), compressing the ratio — the rc.20 fix moved the flake from the POSITIVE budget to the ratio's noisy denominator.

Re-fixed durably: the 3 NEGATIVE controls (`wikilink-scan` ×2 + `write` ×1) now assert an **absolute FLOOR on the OLD catastrophic time** (`expect(quad).toBeGreaterThan(50)`) and drop the `linear` baseline. Calibrated empirically — the old functions are ~325 ms / ~430 ms / ~830 ms on a dev laptop; **CI is only SLOWER, so a 50 ms floor can only fail if the runner ran the quadratic 6–16× FASTER than a laptop (impossible)**, and load pushes the quad's time *up*, never below the floor. The POSITIVE `< 2000 ms` ceilings (already robust) are unchanged.

## Docs — comparison-ready external-audit brief
Ships `docs/audits/AUDIT-REQUEST-FULL-FROM-SCRATCH-v3.11.0-rc.21-2026-06-26.md` (targets the `v3.11.0-rc.21` tag) for the v3.11.0 → `@latest` promotion gate. Redesigned from the rc.17 brief after a 3-report Workflow analysis: obligation-gating sink-trace + prior-finding re-probe (cap the score if unfilled), named worst-case shapes (dense-CLOSED `[[a]]`, not unclosed), wrong-probe 3-point complexity-curve self-check, evidence-or-downgrade, outcome-anchored severity rubric, anti-anchoring novel-class tier, and a fix to the rc.17 brief's own `40 src/*.ts` count drift.

No `src/` behavior change (only `VERSION`); **1416 tests unchanged**.

author: houseme
body:
## Related Issues
Refs https://github.com/rustfs/backlog/issues/721
Refs https://github.com/rustfs/backlog/issues/715

## Summary of Changes
- Add a `RustfsCodecDecodeEngine` adapter backed by `rustfs-erasure-codec` for the GET codec streaming decode path.
- Add a boxed `CodecStreamingDecodeEngine` enum so the GET reader can select either the existing legacy engine or the new RustFS codec engine without changing the `ErasureDecodeReader` type shape.
- Add `RUSTFS_GET_CODEC_STREAMING_ENGINE` with allowed values `legacy` and `rustfs`; the default remains `legacy`, and the engine selector is only used after codec streaming is enabled.
- Cover byte-for-byte legacy/rustfs equality, missing data shard recovery, parity-only missing behavior, insufficient shards, empty object handling, and zero-length shard recovery.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo check -p rustfs --lib`
- `cargo test -p rustfs-ecstore erasure_codec --lib`
- `cargo test -p rustfs-ecstore erasure_decode_reader --lib`
- `cargo test -p rustfs-ecstore codec_streaming --lib`
- `RUSTFS_GET_CODEC_STREAMING_ENGINE=legacy bash scripts/run_get_codec_streaming_smoke.sh --skip-build --mode codec --sizes 1MiB --concurrency 16 --duration 15s --rounds 1 --python-bin <python3.10+>`
- `RUSTFS_GET_CODEC_STREAMING_ENGINE=rustfs bash scripts/run_get_codec_streaming_smoke.sh --skip-build --mode codec --sizes 1MiB --concurrency 16 --duration 15s --rounds 1 --python-bin <python3.10+>`
- `make pre-pr`
- `make pre-commit`

## Impact
- Compatibility: default behavior remains the existing legacy engine; the new RustFS codec engine is opt-in and has no effect when `RUSTFS_GET_CODEC_STREAMING_ENABLE=false`.
- Configuration: adds `RUSTFS_GET_CODEC_STREAMING_ENGINE=legacy|rustfs` for codec streaming GET experiments.
- Performance: this PR adds the adapter and validation harness only. It does not make `rustfs` the default engine or claim a throughput win yet.
- Rollback: unset `RUSTFS_GET_CODEC_STREAMING_ENGINE`, set it to `legacy`, or disable codec streaming with `RUSTFS_GET_CODEC_STREAMING_ENABLE=false`.

## Additional Notes
The local smoke required a Python 3.10+ interpreter for the compatibility probe because the default macOS Python 3.9 cannot parse the probe's modern type annotation syntax.

author: debuggingfuture
body:
A Schedule-mode recipe that audits **the FlareDispatch deployment's own trust surface** — least-privilege of its API tokens, defense-in-depth of its controls, hygiene of its long-lived secrets — and opens one weekly draft PR with a posture scorecard. Distinct from [`security-scan`](../tree/main/recipes/security-scan), which scans a checked-out repo's dependencies; this one reviews the Dispatcher itself, scored against [`specs/07-trust-model.md`](../blob/main/specs/07-trust-model.md).

## Insight

A run executes inside a Workflow and **cannot introspect which Worker Secrets or bindings are set** — `io.env` is a deliberate no-op, and "the operator's Cloudflare account is sound" is an explicit trust assumption. So an honest self-audit can't pretend to read `VIEWER_ACCESS_MODE` or the CF token scope off the live deploy. The recipe splits its inputs into two planes accordingly:

- **Live (introspected):** `github.repositories()` — the one least-privilege signal a run *can* measure directly: the App key's real install blast-radius (repo count, distinct installations, archived repos still attached).
- **Declared (CONFIG_KV):** a `security-posture.manifest` the operator keeps current (token scopes, App permission set, which DiD controls are on). Every field defaults to its most-unknown value, so a partial manifest surfaces `unknown` findings, never a false `ok`.

## Rationale

- **Deterministic rules carry the high-confidence findings**, with the model only adding narrative + what the rules miss. An over-broad token, a missing Access layer, an unneeded `HMAC_SECRET` are rule-decidable; they shouldn't hinge on a model. Each rule maps to a control/known-gap in the trust model via a `reference` field.
- **The model pass is best-effort.** An unconfigured or failing backend degrades to a rules-only report rather than failing the run — a security control should fail toward "tell me less," never go dark. This is the one deliberate departure from the sibling `ci-triage-pr` / `spec-drift-pr` recipes (which fail hard on model error).
- **Reuses the `ai-code-review` engine** (`@flare-dispatch/review-agent`'s `completeStructured`, resolved under the `security-posture.*` namespace) — no new model plumbing, no model API key (the Workers AI binding is the auth).
- **Recipe-only, no core changes.** Built entirely on existing capabilities (`config`, `github.repositories`, `github.openDraftPullRequest`, `completeStructured`), so it's a self-contained copy-paste starter like `deploy-smoke` / `nightly-e2e`.

## Rubric (what it checks)

- **Least-privilege** — CF token has no account-wide/"god" scope; read-purpose token holds no edit scopes; deploy token includes `Containers` (the silent-freeze gotcha); App permissions stay within the minimal manifest baseline; a webhook-/schedule-only deploy isn't carrying an unused `HMAC_SECRET`.
- **Defense-in-depth** — viewer isn't `token-only`; `VIEWER_ACCESS_MODE=required` actually has a custom domain (Access can't front `*.workers.dev`); `/v1/admin/*` is Access-fronted on top of the bearer.
- **Secret hygiene** — required secrets for the trigger modes in use are set; `BROWSER_CDP_API_TOKEN` (a known gap) has a rotation plan; a declared ≤90-day rotation cadence.
- **Blast-radius** — App installed on selected repos, not org-wide "all"; live reachable-repo count is sane and carries no archived repos.

## Verification

- Typechecks as a real run (temp-copied into `runs/` and run through the package `tsc` — clean against the live `@flare-dispatch/core` + `review-agent` APIs).
- `oxlint` clean; `sync-recipes --check` still green (this is a custom recipe, not a sync-mirror).

## Key actions / todos for an operator adopting it

- [ ] Copy `security-posture.run.ts` into `runs/`, add `0 7 * * 1` to `wrangler.jsonc` `triggers.crons`, `wrangler deploy`.
- [ ] Set `security-posture.report-repo` and populate `security-posture.manifest` (shape in the recipe README).
- [ ] Pick a backend model (`security-posture.opencode.model` / `.reasonix.*`) for the narrative; absent → rules-only reports.

author: sajoluo
body:
## Summary

Fixes MaaFramework ADB control for emulator extras, especially MuMu:

- Translate MAA emulator extras config into the JSON schema expected by MaaFramework `MaaAdbControlUnit`.
- Report the fastest screencap method back to MAA when emulator extras are selected.
- Respect MaaFramework control-unit feature flags and synthesize input with `touch_down`/`touch_move`/`touch_up` or key down/up when required.

## Root Cause

`MaaFwAdbController` previously passed `{}` for non-AVD configs, so MuMu/LDPlayer extras configured by the GUI never reached MaaFramework. That made MuMu enhanced screenshot unavailable under `TouchMode = MaaFwAdb`.

After enabling MuMu emulator extras input, MaaFramework's MuMu extras control unit advertises that click should be performed with down/up events instead of `click()`. `MaaFwAdbController` did not handle that feature flag, so direct `click()` could fail even though the control unit was initialized.

## Validation

Validated locally on Windows with MuMu 12 and `TouchMode = MaaFwAdb`:

- Built `MaaCore` with CMake `RelWithDebInfo` successfully.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- GUI reported fastest screenshot as `MumuExtras` with 7ms cost.
- Core log showed `MaaFwAdbController` and `MaaAdbControlUnit`, not MaaTouch.
- Auto battle completed successfully with `MaaFwAdbController::click`/`swipe` calls.

## Summary by Sourcery

将 MaaFramework 的 ADB 模拟器附加配置和特性开关集成到 `MaaFwAdbController` 中，以改进模拟器截屏和输入行为。

New Features:
- 支持 MuMu 12 和 LDPlayer 模拟器附加配置：将 GUI 中的 ADB 配置转换为 `MaaAdbControlUnit` 所需的 JSON 模式，并传递合适的截屏和输入方法。
- 当使用模拟器附加配置时，将所选择的最快截屏方式及其性能开销回传给 GUI。

author: ericksoa
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD041 -->
## Summary

Adds native OpenShell-managed authenticated HTTPS Streamable HTTP MCP server lifecycle for OpenClaw, Hermes, and LangChain Deep Agents Code. It exposes `mcp add|list|status|restart|remove`, integrates crash-safe rebuild and destroy recovery, and keeps raw credentials out of sandbox files and NemoClaw registry state. Stable OpenShell `0.0.72` is the shipping dependency for NemoClaw `v0.0.74`.

## Related Issue

Closes #566.
Refs #6195.
Implements the [accepted native OpenShell design decision](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw/issues/566#issuecomment-4847534784).
Supersedes the closed host-proxy implementation in #565.

## Changes

- Support OpenClaw, Hermes, and LangChain Deep Agents Code with `mcp add|list|status|restart|remove`; normal sandbox rebuild and destroy participate in lifecycle reconciliation.
- Accept only authenticated canonical HTTPS Streamable HTTP endpoints with exactly one host-side `--env KEY` credential reference per server.
- Use native OpenShell `protocol: mcp` policy enforcement and provider-backed credential replacement. NemoClaw starts no MCP proxy, relay, listener, stdio adapter, or persistent secret-bearing host process.
- Persist only credential names and opaque ownership metadata. Agent configuration contains `Bearer openshell:resolve:env:KEY`; raw values are supplied only to the allowlisted OpenShell provider subprocess.
- Fail closed on private/local/special-use targets, unsupported host aliases, userinfo, query, fragment, percent characters, non-canonical paths, ambiguous provider/policy/adapter state, and ownership drift.
- Serialize supported per-sandbox writers with one cross-process mutation lock and exact-check policy/provider state before and after mutation.
- Preserve owned MCP intent across rebuild, recover interrupted add/remove/destroy transactions, and delete shared state only after exact ownership verification.
- Add stable and explicit dev-channel live lanes, artifact credential scanning, workflow boundary tests, operator documentation, and focused security/lifecycle regression coverage.

### Apurv review feedback addressed

- [x] [Use the checked-in Hermes `BASE_IMAGE` pin](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw/pull/5876#discussion_r3516487751): validation now reads the single immutable `ARG BASE_IMAGE=...@sha256:...` from the actual final Dockerfile, accepts only that official digest, and rejects a different digest. The obsolete `NEMOCLAW_STALE_OPENCLAW_BASE_DIGEST` guard is removed.
- [x] [Preserve falsey non-map YAML roots](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw/pull/5876#discussion_r3516487753): both Hermes transaction paths normalize only `None` to `{}`. `[]`, `false`, `0`, and `""` reach the object-root guard and fail without a write; tests prove byte preservation and zero writes.
- [x] [Block rebuild while MCP destroy is incomplete](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw/pull/5876#discussion_r3516487755): live rebuild and absent-sandbox onboarding reject both `destroyPreparedAt` and `destroyPendingAt` before policy, adapter, provider, gateway, pruning, or recreation work.
- [x] [Reject every percent character and retain legacy cleanup](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw/pull/5876#discussion_r3516487758): host and Hermes add validation reject `%`, `%GG`, `%2`, and valid percent escapes before side effects. Forced Hermes cleanup validates the action and server name, then removes the exact legacy key without re-rejecting its already-persisted URL.
- [x] [Recheck exact policy content and serialize supported writers](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw/pull/5876#discussion_r3516487761): the fresh policy read deep-compares the live key with the exact previously owned content and refuses changed or removed values before `policy set`; a post-set exact read gates ownership commit. Supported NemoClaw policy, channel, shields, inference, snapshot, onboarding, and config writers share the per-sandbox lock.
- [x] [Keep credential revision proof host-side](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw/pull/5876#discussion_r3516487763): the sandbox-writable revision snapshot is removed. Fresh OpenShell-mediated execs return only bounded `absent`, `canonical`, or `vN` observations; the host retains the prior value and requires a changed, non-absent revision after update.

The review fixes landed in signed commit `299efb5c1eaeec21f9b91d7d1ce9874b6768d8e8` and remain present on final exact head `f9283fe624a479796ee1dcba35e5e95fde182ab2`.

### Release boundary and residual-risk disposition

- Stable OpenShell `0.0.72` is the only supported and shipped OpenShell version for NemoClaw `v0.0.74`; installer, blueprint, workflow, and credential-boundary data are aligned to that version.
- OpenShell `0.0.72` attributes some script clients to Node/Python interpreters rather than immutable package entrypoints. Exact destination, literal path, MCP method profile, request-size bound, public-IP pins, provider ownership, and runtime checks narrow that grant. Remove interpreter grants when OpenShell exposes stable package-entrypoint attribution.
- Static provider credentials are sandbox-scoped rather than endpoint-exclusive. Every managed server requires a unique credential name and a least-privilege token; operators must not grant the same runtime a broader route capable of resolving that placeholder.
- Supported NemoClaw writers are serialized, and external drift visible before or after mutation is rejected by exact reads. A direct external `openshell policy set` does not participate in NemoClaw's lock, and OpenShell `0.0.72` exposes no policy compare-and-swap/version precondition. If an external set lands in the narrow interval after the fresh read and loses the final write race, it can be overwritten. Closing that arbitrary-client race requires an upstream OpenShell CAS primitive; this PR does not claim atomicity beyond supported NemoClaw writers.
- OpenShell policy does not bind URL scheme, HTTP `Host`, or query parameters. NemoClaw therefore accepts only canonical HTTPS URLs and rejects userinfo, query, fragment, percent characters, credential-shaped paths, and unsupported aliases.
- Stable OpenShell cannot safely parse bracketed IPv6 literals in HTTPS CONNECT targets. Direct IPv6 literals are rejected; DNS AAAA destinations remain supported through resolve/validate/connect and exact public-address pins.
- The explicit compatibility-only dev lane consumed mutable OpenShell `0.0.76-dev.3+g6461677c`. OpenClaw and Deep Agents passed, but Hermes rebuild exited during pre-delete MCP preservation. The same exact NemoClaw head passed the identical Hermes rebuild with supported stable `0.0.72`. Because the dev lane is non-default, unverified, outside the `v0.0.74` support range, and not a required PR check, this PR does not add speculative compatibility code for the moving artifact; compatibility should be re-evaluated with OpenShell before NemoClaw widens its supported range.

### Exact-head verification

- PR head `f9283fe624a479796ee1dcba35e5e95fde182ab2` is signed and GitHub-verified, labeled `v0.0.74`, [approved by Apurv](https://github.com/NVIDIA/NemoClaw/pull/5876#pullrequestreview-4628151574), and merged to `main` as `bddbb3e2418766015b931829571202f443a788f1`. Immediately before merge, `main` advanced by heading-only commit `cc532e5`; the overlap audit and `merge-tree` were clean.
- The final restack integrates current-main DCode `0.1.30` runtime hardening while preserving managed MCP in interactive and headless paths. The complete sandbox-writable MCP file is validated fail-closed as HTTPS-only registry-owned shape before launch; stdio commands, extra headers, raw credentials, mismatched placeholders, unsafe ownership/mode, and unrelated top-level configuration are rejected.
- Final local validation passed build, typecheck, all 44 config schemas, repository checks, commit/push hooks, 290/290 focused CLI tests, 192/192 MCP integration tests, 77/77 DCode image-contract tests, and the affected DCode

author: albertovasquez
body:
## What

\"what skills do we have?\" / \"what can you do?\" classify as `chat_question` and route to `ChatHandler` — which was a bare model call that never saw the catalog. So you got a model-guessed (or, in mock mode, a placeholder) answer that never enumerated the real skills, even though the **Router already holds the full `(name, description)` catalog** one step earlier when it classifies.

This passes that same catalog to `ChatHandler` and answers capability questions **deterministically from it** — a full name + description list, no model round-trip, works in mock mode too. Ordinary chat is unchanged.

## How

- `ChatHandler` gains an optional `catalog`. `is_capability_question()` detects meta-questions with a deliberately **narrow** regex (`\bskills?\b` or "what can you do") and yields a formatted catalog instead of calling the model — narrow by design, since a false positive would hijack legitimate chat while a false negative just falls through to the model.
- `Router` exposes a public `.catalog` property; both call sites (`acp_agent.py`, `run_traced.py`) pass `router.catalog` through.
- `_ScriptedRouter` test double mirrors the new `.catalog` attribute.

## Before / after

```
what skills do we have?
[classified: chat_question · conf: 0.98]
```

**Before:** model guesses, or `[mock mode] …` placeholder — never the real list.
**After (mock mode, no model call):**
> I have **4 skills** available:
> - **test-driven-development** — …
> - **systematic-debugging** — …
> - **verification-before-completion** — …
> - **receiving-code-review** — …

## Tests

- 9/9 `test_chat_handler.py` (6 new): detection precision (matches skill/ability questions, rejects "what is python?", "debug this skillfully"), catalog answering, **no-model guarantee** (litellm raises if called), empty-catalog message, and no-regression on ordinary chat.
- Full suite: **176 passed**. The one failure on this branch — `test_header_uses_brand_e_mark` — is **pre-existing on `main`** (an earlier change set the header `DON≡` → `≡` without updating its test) and is out of scope here.

## What

ADR-029 records the **C5 decision** (#612 Phase C) from an architecture session: introduce a Go command **`dotf secrets sync <target>`** that resolves a scoped secret set backend-agnostically (reusing the existing `Loader.EnvFor` resolver map) and pushes it to the target surface.

- **Slice one = `ci`**: select `ci:*`-consumer entries, resolve each value (age **or** bw, transparently), upload via `gh secret set`. Absorbs `scripts/github-secrets-manager.sh` (ADR-020 strangler-fig) and **retires the age-only `ls --pairs` leak**.
- **Why now:** once a `ci:*` secret flips to `backend: bw` (C4, #627), `ls --pairs` excludes it and it silently drops from the Actions upload. `sync` is backend-agnostic by construction, which unblocks migrating `ci:*` secrets.
- `container`/`agent` `.env` materialization is **designed but deferred**; the live `bw unlock` + `gh` smoke is Windows-empirical and deferred.

## Notes

- Docs-only (no production LOC; spec-gate N/A).
- Downstream: `/spec init` for the `sync ci` implementation; the script + `--pairs` retire behind a one-time parity check.

Decision context: ADR-028 (two-tier secrets) specifies the `sync` step; ADR-020 (CLI convergence) says `dotf` absorbs the shell twin.

author: paulorochagodoi
body:
## Resumo

Esta PR adiciona suporte a Português (Brasil), uma nova tela de histórico de eventos detectados e um script de atualização que preserva os dados existentes.

## Mudanças

### 🌐 Tradução PT-BR
- Arquivos de tradução completos em `site/public/lang/pt-br/` para todas as páginas (common, main, index, listen_settings, audiostream_settings, videostream_settings, network_settings, system_settings, debugging e a nova timeline).
- Português (BR) adicionado ao menu de idiomas na navbar, com a bandeira do Brasil.
- Migração automática da coluna `language.current` de `CHAR(2)` para `CHAR(5)` (necessária para o código `pt-br`), feita tanto em runtime (`language_config.php`) quanto pelo script de atualização.

### 🕑 Tela de histórico (timeline)
- Nova página `timeline.php`, acessível pelo link "Histórico" na navbar.
- `site/src/events.php` com as funções de criação/consulta/limpeza da tabela `events` (criada automaticamente, sob demanda).
- `listen.php` modificado para registrar cada notificação detectada (choro, balbucio, som) na tabela `events`.
- Endpoints `get_events.php` e `clear_events.php` para consulta e limpeza via AJAX.
- `js/timeline.js` renderiza a timeline agrupada por dia, com ícones por tipo, filtro por categoria, atualização automática e limpeza com confirmação.

### 📦 Atualizador zipado
- `update.sh` reescrito para funcionar como pacote de atualização (sem depender de git, já que a instalação no dispositivo não é um repositório git).
- Detecta a instalação existente (ou via `--target`), faz backup dos arquivos antes de substituí-los, aplica patch no `config.json` preservando credenciais/customizações, migra o banco (best-effort) e reinicia o Apache.
- Suporta `--dry-run` e `--help`.

### 📖 Documentação
- Nova seção "Updating" no README (atualização com e sem internet) e novas funcionalidades adicionadas à lista de features.

## Preservação de dados

A atualização preserva configurações, redes salvas, senhas e histórico de eventos. O `config.json` é alterado por *patch* (não sobrescrito) e um backup com timestamp de cada arquivo substituído é criado em `.update_backup_<data>/`.

## Testes

O fluxo do atualizador foi testado de ponta a ponta contra uma instalação simulada: cópia de arquivos, patch do config.json com preservação de senha customizada, criação de backup, idempotência (execução repetida) e degradação graciosa quando mysql/apache não estão disponíveis.

## Summary

Added comprehensive documentation explaining how the buyer matching system works, what manual inputs affect marketing sends, and how to troubleshoot matching issues.

## Changes

- **New file:** `docs/marketing/buyer-matching-field-guide.md` (239 lines)
  - Explains the three-layer matching architecture: hard filters (deterministic), tier scoring, and optional AI soft pass
  - Documents all GHL fields that affect buyer matching, including custom fields (`CF.TARGET_CITIES`, `CF.MAX_PRICE`, etc.) and contact fields
  - Clarifies the critical distinction between `contact.target_zips` (legacy notes field, not read by matcher) and `CF.TARGET_MARKETS` (structured field actually used by matcher)
  - Details how the `parsed_prefs` JSON field is generated and what it controls
  - Provides troubleshooting table for common matching problems
  - Explains the role of `contact.buy_box` as the highest-leverage manual input for both hard filters and AI parsing
  - Documents geographic matching logic including scope precedence (tags → `alert_area_scope` field → default behavior)
  - Lists fields that are stored but NOT used in matching (for clarity)

## Notable Details

- Emphasizes that AI soft pass (Layer 3) never overrides hard filters and is cost-gated behind `AI_MATCH_LIVE` env var
- Explains how HOA rejection is checked across three sources in priority order
- Documents the tier scoring system (Tier 1 = exact match, Tier 2 = softer, Tier 3 = state fallback)
- Clarifies that buyers with no explicit geographic targets set match everything by default
- Provides field reference tables organized by function (hard filters, tier scoring, AI parsing)
- Includes last-updated timestamp (2026-06-26) for maintenance tracking

This guide serves as the canonical reference for operators and developers understanding buyer matching behavior.

author: irichard00
body:
## Why
Install registers an app but doesn't capture the credential it needs to run. The Apps page (#291) shipped **install** and **activate** but no **connect** step — so apps like GitHub install yet stay unusable, and nothing prompts for auth. This adds that missing step.

## What
A **Connect** action adaptive to each app's auth type (the Hub embeds `auth` on every marketplace card and exposes `GET /auth/status`).

**API client (`lib/apis/apps/index.ts`)**
- `getAuthStatus(appId)`, `startOAuth(appId)`, `submitApiKey(appId, fields)`.
- Parse the card's `auth` block (`type`/`status`/`manualFields`/`setupUrl`) onto `MarketplaceApp`; `needsAuth()` helper; Hub error envelope (`{error.message}`/`{detail}`) surfaced to the user.

**UI (`pages/apps/Apps.svelte`)**
- Installed + needs-auth → **Connect** (or **Reconnect** when expired), gating **Activate** behind a live connection.
- **oauth2:** `startOAuth` → open the system browser (`openExternalUrl`) → poll `/auth/status` until connected. The provider redirects to the Hub callback (not back into the app), so the desktop completes by **polling** — no callback server needed.
- **api_key/basic:** inline credential form from the declared `manualFields` → `POST /auth/api-key`, with a "where do I get this?" setup link.
- Shows the connected account hint; cancels polling on unmount.

## Tests
`getAuthStatus`/`startOAuth`/`submitApiKey`, card `auth` normalization, `needsAuth`, and Hub-error surfacing (`apps.test.ts`). Existing apps + command tests stay green.

## Validation
Verified the workx→Hub wiring against the live test stack: `/auth/status` returns the expected shape and the UI renders **Connect**; `startOAuth` reaches the Hub. Hot-reloaded live in `tauri:dev` with no compile errors.

## Note (deployment)
Completing an **OAuth round trip** needs the Hub's provider OAuth client creds (`client_id`) configured per environment. Without them `startOAuth` returns "oauth config is incomplete" — surfaced cleanly in the UI. The **api_key** path needs no provider registration (no api_key apps in the current catalog, but the form + storage are covered by Hub tests).

author: adrian-niculescu
body:
## Summary

When a recursive command (`run`, `exec`, `publish`, `pack`, `rebuild`) is filtered to a subset of projects, the topological sort ran on the selected subgraph only and dropped edges that pass through unselected projects. Two selected projects related only transitively could then run concurrently or in the wrong order, so a dependency's script could start after its dependent's.

The sort now resolves edges through the full workspace graph: a project runs after the selected projects it transitively depends on, while projects with no real dependency relationship still run concurrently.

Prod-only filters (`--filter-prod`) prune dev dependencies from the graph they select against. The prod-only selected projects resolve order through that prod-pruned graph, so transitive prod dependencies are respected without pulling the dropped dev edges back. A selection that mixes `--filter` with `--filter-prod` resolves each project through the graph that matches how it was selected: regularly filtered projects through the full graph, prod-only ones through the prod-pruned graph. That keeps a regular filter's transitive ordering intact when a prod-only filter is also present, and stops a dev-only reverse edge from forming a cycle that would collapse a real prod dependency and its dependent into one chunk.

Note: the cyclic-workspace-dependency warning still inspects the selected subgraph only, so a cycle that runs through unselected projects affects ordering but is not warned about. Left as is to keep this change focused.

Fixes pnpm/pnpm#8335

## Squash Commit Body

```text
The recursive command runners sorted opts.selectedProjectsGraph, which keeps
only the selected projects as keys. Edges to unselected projects were dropped,
so a transitive dependency between two selected projects (a -> b -> c with only
a and c selected) was lost and the two ran out of order.

sortFilteredProjects resolves the order through the full workspace graph: for
each sorted project it walks dependencies, tunneling past unselected projects
and stopping at selected ones, so a transitive relationship becomes a direct
edge. Projects without a real dependency stay in the same chunk, preserving
concurrency.

Prod-only filters (--filter-prod) prune dev edges. Their selected projects are
sorted through the prod-pruned full graph, so transitive prod deps are honored
without reintroducing the dropped dev edges. In a mixed selection each project
is sorted through the graph that matches how it was selected: regularly filtered
projects through the full graph, prod-only ones through the prod-pruned graph.
Carrying prod-only projects on the full graph would let a dev-only reverse edge
form a cycle and collapse a real prod dependency and its dependent into one
chunk.

Fixes pnpm/pnpm#8335
```

## Checklist

- [x] Ported to pacquet, as the maintainer requested
  ([comment](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/12688#issuecomment-4827239056)):
  commit `dce50a7` applies the same `sort_filtered_projects` fix — resolving
  transitive order through the full / prod-pruned workspace graph — to pacquet's
  recursive `run`, `exec`, and `pack` runners, with matching tests. pacquet has
  no recursive `publish`/`rebuild` ordering, so nothing else needs porting.
- [x] Added a changeset.
- [x] Added or updated tests.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Improved recursive command ordering when selecting projects with filters, including mixed regular and production-only selections.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Fixed command execution, build, pack, publish, and rebuild order so dependencies selected through unselected intermediaries run first.
  * Corrected behavior for `--filter-prod` and combined `--filter` + `--filter-prod` use cases.
  * Recursive operations now handle production-only project selections consistently.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

author: askmethatfr
body:
## Problem

`File.WriteAllText` in `WriteMissingTranslations()` runs synchronously on every missing translation, blocking ASP.NET Core request threads. Under load, this causes thread pool starvation.

## Fix

Replaced sync `File.WriteAllText` with `Task.Run(() => WriteFileSynchronously(...))`:

- `Task.Run` offloads the file I/O to the thread pool — the calling thread returns immediately
- `WriteFileSynchronously` preserves exception handling with `Console.Error` logging
- API surface unchanged (no `async` ripple required; `IStringLocalizer` indexer is sync)

## Tests

- `MissingTranslation_WithCollectToJSON_WritesFileEventually` — verifies file is written eventually (async semantics preserved)
- `Should_Track_Colored_NotFound` — existing test still passes

Closes #19

This wires the workflow to build and mirror only the backend and sandbox images, install the chart-managed API/Celery/proxy/sandbox pods, disable the chart webserver with `webserver.replicaCount=0`, and shard discovered tests under `backend/tests/integration/tests/craft/k8s`. The workflow and CI values file match the corresponding files from `whuang/real-craft-integration-tests`, including the web build removal. ## How Has This Been Tested? ## Additional Options - [ ] [Optional] Please cherry-pick this PR to the latest release version. - [x] [Optional] Override Linear Check --- ## Summary by cubic Run Craft k8s integration tests against a Helm-installed Onyx in `kind`, replacing compose with chart-managed API/Celery/proxy/sandboxes and real backing services. Tests shard per file, pull prebuilt images, and include robust diagnostics for reliable CI. - **New Features** - Install `deployment/helm/charts/onyx` via `helm upgrade --install` with CI overlays; disable the webserver at install and run DB migrations once CNPG is ready. - Use chart-managed Postgres (CNPG), Redis (operator), OpenSearch, and MinIO; wait for readiness and port-forward Postgres/Redis/API/MinIO to the runner (no custom pod-network routes). - Build `backend` and `sandbox` images in a separate job, push to ECR cache, then mirror per shard into `localhost:5001` for unauthenticated pulls. - Discover `backend/tests/integration/tests/craft/k8s/test_*.py` and run one shard per file (no fail-fast), each on its own `kind` cluster. - Seed a dev license for EE-gated tests; set CI-safe flags like `DISABLE_MODEL_SERVER` and `INTEGRATION_TESTS_MODE`. - Resolve the sandbox-proxy Service IP for runner clients; stream sandbox pod logs and capture port-forward logs plus full cluster dumps on failure. - Gate with tighter path filters and a single aggregated required check that covers discovery, build, and test results. - Update `values-ci.yaml`: enable vector DB/OpenSearch; right-size CNPG/OpenSearch/MinIO/API/web/Celery; tune sandbox CPU/memory/storage and approval timeouts; disable ingress/bots/optional services; set `api.runStartupMigrations=false`; point `SANDBOX_API_SERVER_URL` to the chart API service. Written for commit 0fac037035fb8826fecf53af9de56be18c974a55. Summary will update on new commits.

author: kynoptic
body:
## Summary

- Close the loop from the roadmap objective: the `.goggle` files are now build artifacts of the reliability data instead of hand-maintained files.
- `core.build_goggle` maps each rated domain to a Goggle action (`gr`→`$boost=2`, `nc`→`$downrank=2`, `gu`/`d`→`$discard`, `m`→none), then merges a data-derived **base** layer (369 rules) with a curated **overlay** (`goggle_overlay.txt`, 3,676 rules) holding nuance the data can't yet derive. Overlay wins on conflict.
- Approach: overlay-merge keeps every hand-curated rule (verified superset, 0 dropped both variants) while surfacing what the generator adds and where it disagrees.

## What changed

- New `core/build_goggle.py` — generator, overlay merge, renderer, diff + gap reports, and a guard against re-seeding from an already-generated goggle.
- `goggle_overlay.txt` — seeded once from the hand goggle: 444 path-qualified + 3,210 manual + 23 conflict rules.
- Regenerated both goggle variants: deduped ~560 duplicate hand-maintained lines, lowercased resolved domains, added 74 new data-derived domains.
- Reports: `outputs/goggle_diff.md` (additions, conflicts, overlay-preserved remainder) and `outputs/goggle_gap_candidates.csv` (unrated domains for manual review, never auto-added).
- Docs: README "Generating the goggles" how-to; roadmap marks the loop closed and records the path-qualified-generation follow-up.

## Review focus

The **23 conflicts** in `outputs/goggle_diff.md` are where the data-driven status disagrees with the hand file (e.g. the most-cautious collapse rates `foxnews.com`/`cnet.com` as discard while the hand file boosts them). The curated value is kept and flagged — these are the granularity gap the follow-up targets.

The large diff on the `.goggle` files is the expected one-time hand→generated reorg; the superset test guarantees no rule was lost.

## Test plan

### Automated testing
- [x] 21 new unit tests for grammar round-trip, status mapping, merge precedence, diff buckets, overlay round-trip, variant rendering, and the seed guard
- [x] Full suite passes (100 tests)
- [x] markdownlint clean

### Manual testing
- [x] Superset guarantee verified against the committed goggle (0 keys dropped, both variants)
- [x] Build is deterministic; `-only` variant carries the catch-all `$discard` and the commented Google rules

## Breaking changes

None — the goggle URLs and rule semantics are unchanged; output is a superset of the prior rules.

## Documentation

- [x] Docstrings on public functions in `core/build_goggle.py`
- [x] README updated with the generation and bootstrap how-to

## Z+ markers

- **Z+ 15-row matrix** — N/A for a docs-only PR; the charter itself *defines* the evidence-table discipline (Executive-Summary status table per deliverable). No code matrix to fill; honestly marked N/A rather than fabricated.
- **Z+ 7-row resilience matrix** — N/A (no code path / failure surface added); the charter §5 *mandates* the resilience matrix for future code PRs. Not faked here.
- **Z+ 7-layer audit** — N/A (no material action / hash-chained event added by a docs change); the charter §8 codifies the audit-trail expectation.
- **4-agent hostile review** — proportionate review for a docs-only, zero-code-surface change; the documents were drafted against `CLAUDE.md` and the existing ledger (#899/#921/#932/#933) for factual accuracy. None introduced — no code, no data path, no behavioural change. The only "failure mode" is documentation drift, mitigated by tracing every claim to a real ledger entry / Golden Rule.

Docs-only — no run to prove. Factual claims (2dp snap, vendor ~5 r/s, verbatim-integrity status, the HELD 5× format) are cited from `CLAUDE.md` §6 and the MIGRATION ledger, not invented.

### Rollback plan
Revert the single commit; no migration, no data, no behavioural state to undo.

### Out of scope
Any `brutex/` code change; a new MIGRATION decision ID; the implementation of any roadmap item (each is a future, gated PR); Kubernetes/MQ/multi-service concerns (N/A for a single-process engine, stated in the charter).

author: rap1ds
body:
Before this change, the first argument to `vc-jj--process-lines` was `"log"`. This seems wrong.

The signature of the function is: `(defun vc-jj--process-lines (file-or-list &rest args))`

The docstring says:

> FILE-OR-LIST may be nil or non-nil.  When non-nil, it should be a file or a list of files.

"log" clearly is not a file or list of files. It's the jj subcommand we aim to run.

Running the following in my repository:

`(vc-jj--process-lines "log" "--no-graph" "-r" "@-" "-T" "change_id" "-n" "1")` returns `nil`

...whereas running the following:

`(vc-jj--process-lines nil "log" "--no-graph" "-r" "@-" "-T" "change_id" "-n" "1")` returns the actual revision

author: piersonmarks
body:
Two related Gemini/conversation robustness fixes. Bumps to **0.21.0** with a CHANGELOG entry.

---

## Fix 1 — Single-turn Gemini TTS 400 on terse input

**Problem:** `generateSpeech` / `streamSpeech` on `google/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` returned **HTTP 400 — "Model tried to generate text, but it should only be used for TTS."** for terse conversational input like `"Hello there."`. Longer declarative text worked.

**Root cause:** `generateContent` reads a bare short turn as a chat *prompt* and tries to answer it (`responseModalities: ["audio"]` was already set — the modality wasn't the issue; the framing was).

**Fix:** Prepend Google's documented read-aloud style-prompt directive to the single-turn text part so Gemini voices it verbatim. The instruction before the colon is delivery guidance and **isn't spoken**, so `text`, timestamps, and char-count/billing are untouched. Left the 3.1 `/interactions` streaming path alone (it synthesizes `input` literally and isn't subject to the 400 — a directive there would be voiced).

## Fix 2 — 500 on conversations with more voices than native dialogue supports

**Problem:** `POST /v1/audio/conversation/with-timestamps` returned **500** with:
```
DialogueConstraintError: google/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview native dialogue requires exactly 2 unique voices; got 3 unique voices.
```
A 3-voice conversation on a max-2-voice native provider threw instead of rendering.

**Root cause:** `chooseConversationPath` threw `DialogueConstraintError` when unique voices exceeded the provider's native `maxVoices` (deliberate in 0.19.0 — "no silent wrong-path fallback").

**Fix:** Route that case to the existing **per-turn stitch** path — each turn is a single-voice `generateSpeech` call, so stitch has no voice-count limit — and attach a warning that native multi-speaker dialogue was bypassed (so it's *warned*, not silent, addressing the original 0.19.0 concern). Honors `gapMs` / `volumeDbfs` / `speed` / `output` / timestamps. `DialogueConstraintError` stays exported but is no longer thrown by the conversation router. The ≤2-voice native path and the gateway path are unchanged. This supersedes the 0.19.0 over-`maxVoices` behavior, so the CHANGELOG documents it.

---

## Tests

- Single-turn: updated the body-shape assertion + one terse-input regression; `/interactions` literal-input guard.
- Conversation: converted the two "throws on too many voices" dispatch tests into a stitch-fallback assertion (net −1 test), plus one full-flow `generateConversation` regression proving 3 voices → 3 `generate()` calls + valid audio + warning (no throw).
- Full suite **1011/1011**; typecheck, build, lint clean.

## Notes

- Bumped `package.json` → `0.21.0` and added the matching CHANGELOG heading (the changelog CI gate requires it on version bump).
- Live-audio gap still stands for Fix 1 (confirming the directive is silent) — needs a real `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in CI, not chat.

author: psn-github
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the v2.4 Document-track rebrand (#2). That change removed the green/data accents but the suite still painted **Enoki (taupe) fills** behind every table header and down the **left column of the metadata block on page 1 of every document**.

Those bands carry no information: they read as light grey in B&W, and they only *cost* anything when colour-printed — exactly the "lot of colour for no real gain" concern. This PR removes them so the **logo is the only colour on the page**.

## Changes

- **Table headers** (metadata, change-history, signature, content tables, register): no fill → bold near-black labels with a hairline header rule.
- **Status chips**: outlined pills instead of filled (the status word + the page watermark carry the meaning).
- **Caution / critical-step callout**: a heavier Morel left rule, no panel fill.

The only non-text colour that remains is the **Morel logo** (the brand's single permitted colour and "common thread") and thin hairline rules.

## Result

- **Cost**: a colour printer now spends toner only on the logo, not on decorative bands. On a B&W printer the output is unchanged (the taupe was already just grey).
- **Design**: the classic regulated-document look — black on white, structure from weight, rules and whitespace.
- **Pagination**: unaffected — backgrounds don't alter layout. All 57 documents hold their exact page counts (**508 pages, identical** to the previous build), verified with a full before/after comparison.

## Note on the shared spec

`brand-assets/design/documents.md` lists Enoki as an *optional* table-header tint. This PR chooses to forgo it for cost/repro reasons; happy to also tighten that shared spec to "prefer no fill" so the two repos stay aligned — say the word.

author: jp-pino
body:
Fixes #16.

## Summary

Two coupled shared-memory layout defects in `seq_lock`:

1. **Padding miscalculation.** `padding[CACHELINE_BYTES - sizeof(seq) - sizeof(size)]` assumed `seq` (4B) and `size` (8B) pack back-to-back. On 64-bit targets the compiler inserts 4 bytes between them, so the header is 16B not 12B and `entry` no longer started on a cacheline boundary (offset 36/40 on aarch64, 68/72 on x86_64) — defeating the seqlock's false-sharing isolation and causing the `ipc_read` tool to read garbage.

2. **Wrong `CACHELINE_BYTES` on aarch64.** `smp.h` hardcoded `32` for the whole `__arm__ || __aarch64__` branch. That's right for armv7 (i.MX/Cortex-A9) but every aarch64 core uses **64**-byte lines — verified on the target (Orin / Cortex-A78AE) via `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache/index*/coherency_line_size = 64`. Without this, even the corrected padding only isolated to a 32-byte boundary on Jetson, so `seq`/`size` and `entry` still shared a real cacheline.

## Changes

- **`tyndall/ipc/seq_lock.h`** — replace `padding[]` with `alignas(CACHELINE_BYTES) STORAGE entry;` (entry always at `offsetof == CACHELINE_BYTES`, independent of STORAGE alignment) + a `static_assert` guarding over-aligned STORAGE.
- **`tyndall/ipc/smp.h`** — split the ARM branch so aarch64 gets `CACHELINE_BYTES = 64`, armv7 keeps `32`.
- **`tools/ipc_read.cpp`** — drop the now-redundant `format_char_align`/`storage_align` rounding; compute `entry_offset = offsetof(seq_lock<char>, entry)` directly.
- **`tests/ipc/seq_lock_layout.cpp`** (new) — `static_assert` + runtime check that `offsetof(entry) == CACHELINE_BYTES` for storage types across alignment classes. Fails to compile on the buggy layout, so the bug can't regress.

## Verification

Multi-arch containers (QEMU), post-fix `entry` offset now equals the real cacheline on every ABI:

| ABI | before | after | `CACHELINE_BYTES` |
|---|---|---|---|
| armv7 (i.MX) | 32 ✅ | 32 | 32 |
| aarch64 (Orin) | 36/40 ❌ | **64** ✅ | 64 |
| x86_64 | 68/72 ❌ | 64 ✅ | 64 |

- Layout test runs green on all three arches (incl. 8-byte-aligned `vec3`/`mixed` that previously broke).
- Cross-compiled for **i.MX** and **Jetson** via the Yocto SDK: `tests` (incl. the new layout test — `static_asserts` pass on the real aarch64 toolchain) and `tyndall_tool_ipc_read` build cleanly.

See issue #16 for the full investigation, the multi-arch reproduction, and the on-device cache-line confirmation.

author: tanvibhakta
body:
Builds on the merged sitemap work (#104). Moves the `/sitemap` blurbs out of the page itself and next to the content they describe, so `/sitemap` — and share cards, and anywhere else — just pulls them together.

## What changed

**Single source of truth for blurbs**
- **Sections** (`blog`, `poetry`, `weeknotes`, `digital-garden`) define `title` + `description` in `content.config.ts`, right next to their collection definitions. Each section's index page now reads its own metadata from there (no more duplicated `{ title: "Blog" }` literals).
- **Pages** (`care`, `now`) carry a `description` in their **own frontmatter** — auto-discovered, so adding a new markdown page surfaces on `/sitemap` with **zero edits elsewhere**.
- Hand-built standalone routes (`home`, `work`, `subscribe`, `tags`) live in a small `STANDALONE_PAGES` registry with a by-href lookup (`PAGE_META`).

**`/sitemap` page**
- Separates **Pages** from **Sections**.
- Shows a **child count** per section (e.g. Blog · 31, Weeknotes · 55), pulled live from the collections.

**Share-card reuse**
- `description` now threads through `ProseLayout` → `Layout`, which emits `<meta name="description">` plus Open Graph tags (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type`, `og:url`) from the same source. Previously there were **no description/OG tags at all**.
- _Dynamic OG images are a deliberate follow-up — this PR establishes the text source they'd consume._

**Incidental fix (was breaking `main`)**
- `posts/blog/notes-on-running.md` is tagged `health`, which wasn't in the `TAGS` enum (added via the CMS, which doesn't validate it). The production build on `main` is currently failing because of this. Added `health` to `TAGS` to unblock. **Flagging in case you'd prefer a different tag name or want to gate CMS tags some other way.**

## Verification
- `pnpm build` passes (was failing on `main` before the tag fix).

body:
## Summary

Two-part fix for the no-wallet playtest still showing the wallet login screen after picking a faction.

**Root cause**: Players visiting `frontierprotocol.app` (Cloudflare static, `DEV_MODE=false`) hit "Enter Game" → land on `frontierprotocol.app/game` (no backend) → pick faction → `DEV_MODE=false` so quick-auth never fires → `GameLayout` shows wallet gate. Secondary issue: anyone who lands on `frontiernext.fly.dev/game` directly without the landing page auto-login (cleared session, direct bookmark) also hits the wallet gate.

### Fix 1 — `gameUrl.ts` (Cloudflare routing)
`GAME_URL` now resolves at runtime: on any host that isn't `localhost` or `*.fly.dev`, it returns `https://frontiernext.fly.dev/game` instead of `/game`. "Enter Game" on `frontierprotocol.app` now crosses to the Fly backend without any Cloudflare dashboard change. `VITE_GAME_URL` still overrides if set.

### Fix 2 — `GameLayout.tsx` (direct `/game` access)
In `DEV_MODE` builds, if no dev session is active and no real wallet is connected, the game page redirects to `/` (landing page) instead of showing the wallet gate. The landing page auto-login (`VITE_DEV_AUTOLOGIN=true`) fires and brings the player back to `/game` as the test commander. This is compile-dead on mainnet (`DEV_MODE=false`).

**User journey after this fix:**
- `frontierprotocol.app` → Enter Game → `frontiernext.fly.dev/game` → faction gate → picks faction → quick-auth → game ✓
- Direct to `frontiernext.fly.dev/game` → no session → redirect to `/` → auto-login → `/game` → game ✓
- `frontiernext.fly.dev` landing → auto-login → `/game` → game ✓ (unchanged)

## Test plan

- [ ] typecheck: `pnpm run check` — **PASS**
- [ ] server tests: `pnpm run test:server` — **411/425 PASS**
- [ ] client tests: `pnpm run test` — **189 PASS**

author: joemooney
body:
## Summary

SPIKE-67 slice 3 — the **real-time** complement to the slice-1/2 git-log sensor (`field_study.rs`). During a real `aida queue work --auto-complete` drain, record one structured event when the orchestrator catches a **stated-rule violation that no programmatic gate stopped** — CI red on fmt/clippy/provenance (the `///` SPEC-ID doc-comment leak), a reviewer flag, or a punt citing a rule.

This is the field evidence the controlled ablations (STORY-655) could not reach: a confident agent breaks a rule *stated* in CLAUDE.md / a brief, caught only after the fact in CI. The thesis it serves: a stated rule is unreliable against a confident LLM — you need a programmatic **gate** (substrate-as-bouncer). This counts which stated rules keep needing one.

## What shipped

- **New module `aida-cli/src/rule_violation.rs`** — event schema (`~/.aida/rule-violations.jsonl`) + pure `detect()` classifier + JSONL append/read + `by_rule`/`headless_split` aggregators. Observe-only; never blocks or delays the drain.
- **Detectors** (3): CI-red on a stated rule (`fmt`/`clippy`/`provenance-leak`/`commit-format`), reviewer RequestChanges citing a rule, punt citing a rule. A genuine test failure is deliberately *not* a violation (no false events).
- **Hook**: fed from `record_auto_complete_run` (the existing TASK-266 telemetry path) — reuses the already-classified `OrchestrationResult`; a cheap `detect().is_empty()` pre-check skips the repo-size git call on a clean drain.
- **Opt-in** via the existing `AIDA_FIELD_STUDY` switch; honors `AIDA_TELEMETRY=0`. Default OFF (plant-sensor-now, harvest-over-weeks).
- **Privacy floor**: identifiers + categories only. The failure message text is parsed for a rule signature *then discarded* — never logged (asserted by a test). No paths, no diff content, no requirement content.
- **Query**: `aida field-study violations [--json]` (hidden, like `scan`/`report`).
- **Docs**: findings note `docs/plans/2026-06-26-spike-67-gate-vs-rule-evidence.md` (incl. the concrete early gate-vs-rule cases this repo already produced — the recurring `///` leak that needed BUG-624's gate, the advisor-code-gate STORY-684, agents `--no-verify`'ing) + `AIDA_FIELD_STUDY` env-var row updated.

## Test plan

- `aida-cli/src/rule_violation.rs` unit tests (12): each detector, no-false-positive on a real test failure, dedup across CI+punt, clean-run-yields-nothing, the privacy-floor leak guard (a secret path in the failure message must not appear in the event), JSON round-trip, `by_rule`/`headless_split`.
- Full `env -u AIDA_SESSION_ROLE cargo test -p aida-cli`: 3005 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p aida-cli -- -D clippy::correctness`, `bash scripts/glyph-lint.sh --block`: all green.

This pull request introduces support for image and document attachments in the account-provider runner, especially for GitHub Copilot, and improves the device login flow for GitHub authentication. It also refactors how attachments are handled and validated, and makes the login process more user-friendly by copying device codes and displaying clear instructions. Additionally, it adds configuration flexibility and better error handling for attachments.

**GitHub Device Login Improvements**
- The GitHub device login flow now displays the device code in the UI, offers a one-click copy button, and provides clearer instructions for users, including whether the code was copied automatically. (`components/ApiKeyForm.tsx` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-325f75030431bb6701e03340b9cd7018baa4a1bd5aab466c1c727c6abd7ebc96R84-R97) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-325f75030431bb6701e03340b9cd7018baa4a1bd5aab466c1c727c6abd7ebc96R115) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-325f75030431bb6701e03340b9cd7018baa4a1bd5aab466c1c727c6abd7ebc96L201-R238) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-325f75030431bb6701e03340b9cd7018baa4a1bd5aab466c1c727c6abd7ebc96R251-R261) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-325f75030431bb6701e03340b9cd7018baa4a1bd5aab466c1c727c6abd7ebc96R396-R410)
- The backend now returns additional fields (`verificationUrl`, `deviceCode`, `userCode`, `expiresIn`) to support this improved UI. (`lib/account-provider-runner.mjs` [lib/account-provider-runner.mjsL156-R171](diffhunk://#diff-fd48fdc3ae47b5011bbea14ee09928125235bbcd36580118f0896eedcefec038L156-R171))

**Attachment Handling and Validation**
- The account-provider runner now supports image and document attachments, including validation to ensure images have base64 data and documents are text-readable. Unsupported attachments produce descriptive error messages. (`lib/account-provider-runner.mjs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fd48fdc3ae47b5011bbea14ee09928125235bbcd36580118f0896eedcefec038L188-R269) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-6e3db1dde79f1973d58b20578649a43c863e7594de95e8f2357984a7881ea077L38-R57) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6e3db1dde79f1973d58b20578649a43c863e7594de95e8f2357984a7881ea077L75-R97)
- The provider definition exposes a new `ACCOUNT_RUNNER_TEXT_AND_IMAGE_ATTACHMENTS` constant to declare support for image and document attachments. (`lib/providers/account-runner.ts` [lib/providers/account-runner.tsR10-R16](diffhunk://#diff-6e3db1dde79f1973d58b20578649a43c863e7594de95e8f2357984a7881ea077R10-R16))
- Attachments are now passed through to the runner and included in the chat payloads for both ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot, with appropriate formatting for each API. (`lib/account-provider-runner.mjs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fd48fdc3ae47b5011bbea14ee09928125235bbcd36580118f0896eedcefec038L233-R310) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fd48fdc3ae47b5011bbea14ee09928125235bbcd36580118f0896eedcefec038R321-R338) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-6e3db1dde79f1973d58b20578649a43c863e7594de95e8f2357984a7881ea077L99-R118)

**Configuration and Limits**
- The runner now supports environment variable and flag overrides for GitHub API endpoints, and increases the request body size limit to 25MB. (`lib/account-provider-runner.mjs` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-fd48fdc3ae47b5011bbea14ee09928125235bbcd36580118f0896eedcefec038L8-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-fd48fdc3ae47b5011bbea14ee09928125235bbcd36580118f0896eedcefec038L30-R35) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fd48fdc3ae47b5011bbea14ee09928125235bbcd36580118f0896eedcefec038L73-R76)

**Prompt and Attachment Formatting**
- Attachment prompt text generation is simplified to always include text content if present, regardless of category. (`lib/attachments/prompt-text.ts` [lib/attachments/prompt-text.tsL7-R7](diffhunk://#diff-c2750666bc70584cca481b6fc791e2adedb1dee3b74e3f769e0e0f423b3e43a6L7-R7))
- The message-to-payload logic for both ChatGPT and Copilot now appends attachment text and images to the last user message, ensuring context is preserved. (`lib/account-provider-runner.mjs` [lib/account-provider-runner.mjsL188-R269](diffhunk://#diff-fd48fdc3ae47b5011bbea14ee09928125235bbcd36580118f0896eedcefec038L188-R269))

author: tracyjohnsonux
body:
Frontend-only preview of how the dashboard adapts when a user lacks workspace-create ability anywhere. The framing is intentionally not “this is a different kind of user” — all users are the same; some just can’t make workspaces, and when that is true the dashboard shifts into the Gateway Account experience.

Detection is a single signal, `useCanCreateWorkspace()`. When it returns `false`, the following adapt:

- `/` redirects to `/settings/account` instead of `/workspaces`.
- Workspaces, Templates, Tasks, and Agents nav items render disabled with a per-section tooltip in the form of “{Section} aren’t available on AI Gateway accounts. Contact your admin to upgrade your account.”
- The latency (proxy) menu and Admin settings (deployment) dropdown are hidden in the navbar.
- Schedule, SSH Keys, and OAuth2 Applications are hidden from the user settings sidebar.
- Workspace Events and Task Events groups are hidden on the user notifications page.
- The Name field helper on the account form drops the `data.coder_workspace_owner.me.full_name` template reference, which isn’t relevant when workspaces aren’t reachable.
- A first-run welcome dialog on the Account page explains what these users can do, links to token creation, and persists dismissal per user id in `localStorage`.

Unconditional change for everyone: the **Update account** button is disabled until the form is dirty.

The `minimum-implicit-member` experiment is no longer part of the UX gate. It is an admin-side config gate on the API that lets a deployment configure orgs to produce users without `organization-workspace-access`. Once such a user exists, the dashboard adapts based on their ability, regardless of which feature flag enabled the configuration.

`useCanCreateWorkspace` is still a frontend approximation today. It infers ability from `user.roles` plus each org’s `default_org_member_roles`, so it doesn’t see explicit per-org role grants on `OrganizationMember`. The accurate path is a backend-provided boolean exposed through `site/permissions.json` (e.g. `permissions.createWorkspace`) computed from the same rbac decision the workspace-create endpoint enforces. When that lands the hook collapses to `!permissions.createWorkspace` and the gap closes; called out inline in the hook.

<details>
<summary>Decision log</summary>

- Built the gating off existing client-side data so this can ship without a server change.
- Detection lives behind `useCanCreateWorkspace` so swapping in a backend permission is a one-file change.
- Kept the disabled nav items reachable as URLs; the API still enforces. Route-level guards can be added later for a friendlier landing screen than the existing empty/error states.
- Welcome dialog dismissal is per `user.id` in `localStorage`. If we want strictly once-ever-per-user across devices, switching to user preferences (the same API used for `task_notification_alert_dismissed`) is straightforward as a follow-up.
- `MobileMenu` duplicates the desktop nav and isn’t gated here. Wiring the same boolean through it is a small follow-up if mobile demos matter.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Local-only files used to demo this (intentionally not in the PR)</summary>

The Gateway Account flow requires the `minimum-implicit-member` experiment plus the Premium `multiple_organizations` entitlement (the org PATCH that empties `default_org_member_roles` is gated on it). To preview without a real license, three files were created locally in the demo workspace and left out of this PR:

- `enterprise/coderd/licenses_dev.go` — reads `CODER_DEV_LICENSE_PUBKEY` (base64 ed25519 public key) and registers it as `Keys["dev-local"]` so a license signed by the matching private key validates. Local-only by intent; should not ship.
- `enterprise/scripts/dev-license/main.go` — one-shot generator. Mints an ed25519 keypair, signs a Premium tier license JWT, prints `PUBKEY=...` and `LICENSE=...`. Lives under `enterprise/` because `scripts/` is AGPL and can’t import `enterprise/coderd/license`.
- `GATEWAY_ACCOUNT_PREVIEW.md` — a workspace cheatsheet (URLs, demo users, restart command, verification snippets).

If we want a sanctioned dogfood-mode mechanism in-tree instead of these unsigned local files, the cleanest follow-up is a `//go:build devlicense`-gated key registration shim plus a small env-var workflow.

</details>

body:
A single-file, mobile-first **POS calculator** for *Boris' Questionably Legal Elixirs* — a prop for the tabletop RPG puzzle. No real transactions; it just runs the over-engineered order math the DM tracks while players work the puzzle for some health potions.

## How to use
Open **`index.html`** in any browser — no build step, no server, no dependencies. On a phone, "Add to Home Screen" to run it full-screen (PWA manifest included).

## Features
- **Full menu** parsed from the price sheet — 3 sections, 34 items. Tap `+`/`–` to ring up an order.
- **Regular / Bulk** pricing toggle (base price shown struck-through next to the marked-up price).
- **20% markup** applied to every item.
- **$15 flat-rate shipping** added once per order.
- **Processing fee** selector: **$5**, **$10**, or **CashApp est.** — the last estimates the on-chain (gas) cost CashApp passes through on a BTC withdrawal, from live mempool fees.
- **Bitcoin conversion** at CashApp-style rates: live BTC spot (Coinbase, CoinGecko fallback) × an adjustable **spread %** (default 1.75%).
- **Breakdown** panel: base → markup → shipping → fee, spot rate, effective rate, refresh button. Live search bar.

## Order math
```
items            = Σ (base_price × qty)        # base = Regular or Bulk
+ 20% markup     = items × 0.20
+ shipping       = $15 flat (per order)
+ processing fee = $5 | $10 | CashApp on-chain estimate
─────────────────────────────────────────────
total (USD)
≈ Bitcoin        = total ÷ (spot × (1 + spread%))
```

## Verification
Smoke-tested headless (Chromium/Playwright): 2× Mega Mushroom + 1× Revive Ravioli →
regular **$212.00**, bulk **$194.00**, $10-fee variant **$199.00** (all match hand calc); search, tier/fee toggles, and breakdown panel all work with no JS runtime errors. Rates fetch live on the device when online and fall back gracefully to manual entry + fixed fees offline.

Hopefully your tests will pass and you can merge this pull request without too much risk. This should give you an idea how Depfu works in general.
