body:
## Problem (#106, #111)
`anova_test()` results — grouped and ungrouped — and `get_anova_table()` output put `rstatix_test` **after** `data.frame` in the class vector (e.g. grouped: `grouped_anova_test, tbl_df, tbl, data.frame, rstatix_test`). Recent `vctrs`/`dplyr` reject this ("the subclass must come before `<data.frame>`"), so `filter()` / `mutate()` / `add_xy_position()` on an anova_test result errored with *"must be a vector, not a `<…>` object."*

## Fix
Reorder all four class assignments in `R/anova_test.R` so the subclasses (including `rstatix_test`) come **before** `data.frame`:
`c(prefix, class(x), "rstatix_test")` → `c(prefix, "rstatix_test", class(x))`
(`.append_anova_class()`, the grouped result, and both `get_anova_table_from_simple_test()` branches). Same classes — only the order changes — matching the rest of the package's convention.

## No regression
- Class membership is unchanged, so all dispatch still works: `print.anova_test`, `plot.anova_test`, `get_anova_table()`/`is_grouped_anova_test()` (which keys off the `anova` column, not class order), and `get_test_label()`.
- ANOVA **values are unchanged** (the existing exact-value assertions, incl. GG/HF corrections, stay green).
- `filter()`/`mutate()` now work on ungrouped, grouped, and `get_anova_table()` outputs (incl. repeated-measures with sphericity corrections).

## Note on #111 (`add_xy_position` on an anova_test)
The class error is gone, but `add_xy_position()` on an omnibus ANOVA table still (correctly) reports *"data should contain group1 and group2 columns"* — an ANOVA has no pairwise comparisons. To position p-values on a plot, use a pairwise post-hoc that returns `group1`/`group2` (e.g. `tukey_hsd()`, `emmeans_test()`, or `pairwise_t_test()`).

## Tests
`test-anova_test.R`: class order (`rstatix_test` before `data.frame`); `filter()`/`mutate()` succeed on grouped, ungrouped, and `get_anova_table()` (incl. RM/GG); dispatch preserved; `add_xy_position()` gives the informative pairwise-columns message.

## Verification
`Rscript --vanilla -e 'devtools::test()'` → FAIL 0 | PASS 179.

Fixes #106
Refs #111

author: dylb0t
body:
Closes #111.

## Problem
The Genie 4 `#statusbar` / `#status` script command had **no implementation** in Genie 5. Scripts that wrote progress to it (e.g. `#statusbar Hunting: 3/10`) silently no-op'd — the command parser had no `status`/`statusbar` case, so the text had nowhere to go. This is especially noticeable in MDI mode where the bottom status bar isn't present.

## Fix
Per the issue's suggestion, route the text to a strip on the **right of the Script Bar**, which is already visible while scripts run. Wired through the existing `ICommandHost` → `GenieCore` event → App pattern (same shape as `#layout`, `#plugin`, `#goto`):

- **`ICommandHost.SetStatusBar(text, index)`** seam; **`GenieCore`** raises `StatusBarRequested`. Console/headless builds with no subscriber drop it silently (Genie 4 parity — a status write with no bar is a no-op, not an error).
- **`CommandEngine`** parses `#statusbar [N] {text}` — `N` = 1–10 (default 1), `#status` accepted as a synonym. `$variable` expansion already happens upstream in `ProcessInput`, so `#statusbar HP: $health` works.
- **`ScriptBarViewModel`** stores Genie 4's ten slots, composes the non-empty ones into `StatusText`, and clears them when the last script finishes so the strip keeps its zero-height-when-idle behaviour.
- **`MainWindowViewModel`** marshals the engine-thread event to the UI thread.
- **`MainWindow.axaml`** renders the status text docked right of the running-script chips (ellipsis-trimmed).
- Documented in `wiki/Scripting-Reference.md`.

## Test plan
- **Done/verified:** `dotnet build -c Release` clean (0 warnings, 0 errors). Logic mirrors the already-tested `#echo`/`#put` command path; confirmed `ExpandVariables` runs before command dispatch.
- **Worth a live check:** `#statusbar 1 hello` shows to the right of the bar; multi-slot (`#statusbar 2 ...`) composes left-to-right; the strip collapses when scripts end; long text ellipsizes.
- **Possible regressions:** the Script Bar's inner container changed from `StackPanel` → `DockPanel` (chips remain left-aligned); scoped to that one strip.

author: elhan-salaji
body:
## What

Restricts the room write endpoints to the Keycloak `admin` realm role (#219):

- `POST /api/rooms`, `PUT /api/rooms/{id}`, `DELETE /api/rooms/{id}` now require `admin`.
- `GET /api/rooms` and `GET /api/rooms/{id}` stay open to any authenticated user.

## How

- `@EnableMethodSecurity` on `SecurityConfig` and `@PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')")` on the three write methods in `RoomController`.
- The existing URL rules in `SecurityConfig` (`requestMatchers(...).hasRole("ADMIN")`) are kept as a first layer — method security is added on top, in line with the issue ("this issue only adds authorization").

## Note on the role name

The issue text suggests `hasRole('admin')` (lowercase). `KeycloakRealmRoleConverter` maps each realm role to `ROLE_<UPPERCASE>`, so the Keycloak `admin` role becomes the authority `ROLE_ADMIN`. The check therefore uses `hasRole('ADMIN')` — consistent with the existing URL rules and the converter's own test. Lowercase `'admin'` would look for `ROLE_admin` and never match, locking admins out. (Task 3 verified: the converter is already correct, no change needed.)

## Tests

- `SecurityConfigTest` — extended with PUT and DELETE: non-admin → 403, admin → 200/204 (POST was already covered).
- `RoomControllerMethodSecurityTest` (new) — proves `@PreAuthorize` enforces admin-only in isolation: the imported filter chain permits every request at the URL level, so a 403 can only come from the method-level check. This test fails if the `@PreAuthorize` annotations are removed.
- Full backend suite green: 138 tests.

Closes #219

author: iakinyemi
body:
Next free-tier increment, building directly on the v0.6 container collector (#21). Detects **privileged containers** — the classic host-escape vector.

## What

The container collector now records each container's effective-capability bitmask (`cap_eff`, from `/proc/[pid]/status` of the representative process). The diff derives a bare-key `privileged_container` signal — mirroring the filesystem setuid signal — when a container **appears privileged or gains privilege**.

"Privileged" = the effective set includes **CAP_SYS_ADMIN** (bit 21). Docker's default cap set drops it, so its presence flags `--privileged` or `--cap-add=SYS_ADMIN` — the capability that enables mount/namespace/BPF operations and most container escapes.

- **R39_PRIVILEGED_CONTAINER** (high), free. Next free rule id is **R40**.
- The readable `<id>.cap_eff` change is emitted alongside the signal.

## Design

- **Store the fact, derive the signal.** The snapshot stores raw `cap_eff`; the privileged determination happens at diff time — same approach as file modes → setuid. The heuristic can evolve without rewriting history.
- **No schema bump.** `cap_eff` is `omitempty` on the existing `containers` section; `schema_version` stays `0.5`.

## Tests / checks

- Collector captures `CapEff` from the lowest-PID init process.
- Diff fires on a privileged add and on a default→privileged transition; stays silent for default caps and for an already-privileged container (no *new* privilege).
- R39 fires on the signal, not on a plain container add.
- `gofmt` clean · `go vet` clean · `go test -race ./...` green.

VERSION stays `0.5.1`. CHANGELOG under `[Unreleased]`.

author: ahmedelbanna80
body:
## What & why

The reference container image CMD bare-exec'd `node apps/file-manager/server.js`, which starts the Next.js standalone server **directly** and bypasses `@knext/core`'s `node-server` runtime entry. That entry is the only place that:

- installs the **SIGTERM handler** that *forwards* the signal so Next drains in-flight requests and runs `after()` callbacks on scale-down (security.md graceful-shutdown invariant), and
- serves the **Prometheus metrics sidecar** on `:9091`.

So in the shipped reference container, graceful shutdown + metrics were **not** in the entrypoint path — they were only unit-tested in the library. This makes the container actually run the knext runtime, matching how an operator-managed knext deploy runs.

## Change

- `apps/file-manager/Dockerfile` CMD now boots the runtime entry via its published package specifier — `node -e "import('@knext/core/internal/node-server')"` (traced into the standalone bundle's `node_modules`) — and points it at `server.js` via `STANDALONE_SERVER_PATH`. The entry then spawns `server.js` itself. `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` export (f100deb) preserved.
- **The adapter's shutdown logic itself is untouched** (already unit-tested) — this is purely the entrypoint + an e2e proof (AC3).

## TDD evidence (RED → GREEN)

- `dockerfile-runtime-entrypoint.test.ts` (new) — asserts the CMD invokes the runtime entry, not bare `server.js`, and wires `STANDALONE_SERVER_PATH`. **RED** against the old bare-exec CMD (3/4 failed); **GREEN** after the fix.
- `sigterm-drain-e2e.test.ts` (new) + `__fixtures__/slow-standalone-server.mjs` — process-level e2e: boots the **built** runtime entry against a fixture slow server, issues an in-flight request, sends SIGTERM, and asserts the request **completes (drained)** + the process **exits cleanly** + metrics are served. Proves the drain end-to-end, not just in a unit test.
- `dockerfile-cmd-cache.test.ts` — updated to track the new runtime entry form while preserving its `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE`-export regression.

Full `apps/` suite: 17 files / 69 passed / 4 skipped. `packages/kn-next` shutdown + adapter-migration: 21 passed. Biome clean.

## Scope note (AC4)

Full kind/pod-level e2e is too heavy to land cleanly in this PR; per AC4 this delivers the entrypoint fix + a **container/process-level** (`node`-spawned built runtime entry) SIGTERM-drain test that exercises the genuine signal-forwarding + drain code path. The e2e skips (does not fail) when the `@knext/core` dist build is absent, so it is non-blocking in a source-only checkout; CI builds `@knext/core` before running it. Closes the security.md graceful-shutdown gap for the reference container.

## Human follow-up

- A future PR could add a true kind/pod SIGTERM-drain check (kill a pod, assert in-flight requests drain through the operator-managed Deployment) once that infra is cheap.

author: jphein
body:
## Fixes #1166 — `EngineStreamingSourceGaplessTest` flake

### Root cause
The `producedAllSentences stays false when close races a partially-drained source` case pulled **one** chunk, called `close()`, and *assumed* the producer was still mid-stream. With the instant fake engine, that assumption is a race:

1. `close()` calls `queue.clear()`, which frees the bounded-queue (capacity 8) back-pressure slot the producer was blocked on.
2. In the window **before** the coroutine cancellation is actually delivered, the instant producer can either:
   - blast through the remaining sentences and hit the natural-end branch → `producedAll = true` (fails `assertFalse`), or
   - slip a stray chunk into the queue **ahead** of the `END_PILL` → the second `nextChunk()` returns non-null (fails `assertNull`).

Both are test races, not contract violations.

### Fix — deterministic gating
Gate the fake engine so the producer **cannot** reach natural end while `close()` is racing it:

- Sentence 0 synthesizes instantly and is drained by the first `nextChunk()`.
- Every later sentence parks inside `generateAudioPCM` on a `gate` latch.
- The test waits on a `reachedGate` latch, so the producer is **provably parked mid-synth on sentence 1** before `close()` is called — "mid-stream, not at natural end" is now a guarantee.
- `close()`'s `producerExecutor.shutdownNow()` interrupts the parked worker; the engine swallows the `InterruptedException` and returns normally, so the producer exits via its existing `if (!running.get()) return@launch` check — no stray chunk enqueued, `producedAll` never set.

Added a pre-close `assertFalse` to pin the flag false at the exact moment the producer is parked, plus a 5s timeout on `reachedGate.await()` so a real regression fails fast instead of hanging.

### Notes
- Touches only the one test method + three `java.util.concurrent` imports; the shared `GaplessFakeVoiceEngine` helper signature is unchanged.
- Not a CI gate (unit tests aren't required) — pushed for CI on familiar to validate; not compiled locally per task instructions.

author: jbmertens
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in feature to track which config leaf items are actually read while a pipeline runs, and by which stage, plus the ability to **fail the run** when a config carries parameters no stage consumes. The `config/ci-tests` configs are cleaned of dead parameters and set to enforce this, so `run_tests.sh` rejects stale config going forward.

Set the top-level `log_config_usage`; at shutdown a summary lists the accessed items (with the requesting base paths, typically stage `unique_name`s) and the items never accessed. Off by default; no overhead unless enabled.

| value | behavior |
|---|---|
| `false` (default) | disabled |
| `true` / `info` | summary at INFO |
| `warn` / `error` | summary at that severity when any item went unused |
| `fatal_error` | **non-zero exit** when any item went unused (for CI) |

## Design

- **Single choke point.** All typed reads (`get<T>`, `get_default`, expression-variable lookups via `eval`) funnel through `Config::get_value(base_path, name)`, refactored to a single exit where accesses are recorded. Existing scope-walking resolution is unchanged (covered by the existing `test_config` cases).
- **Leaf, not branch**, attributed to the requesting `base_path`. A value resolved by walking up the tree is stored at its resolved leaf path.
- **Whole-block reads.** When `get_value` returns an *object* (e.g. `gpuProcess` reading its `in_buffers`/`out_buffers` map), every descendant leaf is recorded — the caller consumes the whole block.
- **Exclusions.** Framework dispatch markers (`kotekan_buffer`/`kotekan_stage`/`kotekan_metadata_pool`/`kotekan_update_endpoint`) and configUpdater-managed (`kotekan_update_endpoint`) blocks are excluded, since the factories and config updater consume those via a `get_full_config_json()` tree walk rather than `get()`.
- **Levels** parsed by `Config::parse_usage_report_level` (bool or string, case-insensitive; invalid value fails startup). The fatal path uses `exit_kotekan(FATAL_ERROR)` directly — `FATAL_ERROR_NON_OO` throws, and the summary runs from `~kotekanMode`, a `noexcept` destructor.

A `std::mutex` is intentionally not a `Config` member (would break the by-value `make_config` test helpers); the tracking map is guarded by a file-scope mutex.

## CI-test cleanup + enforcement

Removed parameters no stage reads in each pipeline — boilerplate `sizeof_*` constants, and genuinely-dead params verified against source: `retry_time` on `bufferSend`, `counts_max`/`counts_min` on `testN2kGen`, `input_order` on `hdf5FileWrite` writers, etc. (per-config: e.g. `frame_arrival_period` is dead in CPU configs but kept in GPU configs where `gpuProcess` reads it). Each config now sets `log_config_usage: fatal_error`.

## Testing

- `test_config` boost cases for access tracking and `parse_usage_report_level`.
- Ran all 21 `config/ci-tests/{cpu,gpu}_batch/*.yaml` on the real binary (2× A40): every config reports **N of N leaf items accessed** and exits 0. A negative test (injecting a bogus param) exits non-zero, and the level matrix behaves as specified (`info`/`warn`/`error`→exit 0, `fatal_error`→exit 1).

## Caveat

The summary reflects *runtime* accesses through `get()`. "Unused" means "not read in this execution" — a parameter read only on an untaken branch shows as unused. (This is the basis for the per-config cleanup above.)

## 무엇을

스킬 MP 비용이 정적 `mpCost` 리터럴(직업 무차별·풀 대비 과소)이라, MP 풀이 INT로 커지는데 비용은 고정이라 **전 직업에서 MP가 남아도는 죽은 자원**이었다. 이를 직업 계열·차수로 차등화한 **고정 절대값**으로 재설계한다.

비용 = `기준 풀(MP_REFERENCE_POOL=600) × 7%(MP_BASE_PCT) × 계열 배수 × 차수 배수`

- **계열**: 캐스터 ×1.3 / 병사 ×1.0 / 무인 ×0.85 / 도적 ×0.7 (tier1~4 전 직업 계보 매핑)
- **차수**: t1 1.0 / t2 1.4 / t3 1.8
- **무료**(mpCost 0 센티넬: 패시브·기본기·명상)·**몬스터**(monsterOnly) 스킬은 리터럴 유지
- 예시 고정값: 강타 42 · 화염구 55 · 파쇄 59 · 처단 41 · 마탄 76 · 원소마법 98

## 왜 고정 절대값(%아님)

%최대MP는 풀 따라 죄임이 일정하지만 **초반 스킬의 절대 비용이 풀 성장 따라 커져** 손해처럼 느껴지고, 지속형 MP 자원(전투 중 재생 없이 치료소/물약 리필)엔 예측 가능한 고정 숫자가 더 맞다. 트레이드오프: 엔드(풀↑)에선 약간 헐거워지고 초반엔 약간 빡셈 — `MP_REFERENCE_POOL` 단일 다이얼로 조정.

## 표시

`describeV2Skill`이 "MP 55" 절대값으로 표기 → 학습·로드아웃·전투패턴 화면 + 매뉴얼 일관. 매뉴얼 MP 섹션에 per-스킬 고정 비용·직업/차수 차등 설명 1줄 추가.

## 검증

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `npx vitest run` 2150 통과
- `npx next build` 성공
- Codex 리뷰 2회(%모델→고정모델) **LGTM**

## 후속(별도 PR)

- 고차 스킬 데미지 상향 (SP 비용 rubricSpCost 커플링 반영)

## Summary

Implements #16: Tool-call slice C: tool-result continuation and Cursor Agent validation

## User Stories

- US 1: As a Cursor Agent user, I want tool results returned by Cursor to be fed back into Codex, so that tool-driven tasks finish with a real assistant answer.
- US 2: As an API client, I want assistant `tool_calls` and `role:"tool"` messages to round-trip through OpenAI-compatible request parsing, so that continuation requests preserve tool-call context.
- US 3: As a maintainer, I want continuation behavior covered by fake-service tests, so that streaming and non-streaming regressions are caught.
- US 4: As a developer validating Cursor integration, I want documented Agent setup and known-good prompts, so that end-to-end tool-call behavior can be reproduced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC 1: Assistant `tool_calls` plus following `role:"tool"` results parse and are forwarded into a Codex continuation turn, covered by tests with fakes.
- [ ] AC 2: After tool results are supplied, the API returns a final assistant message in non-streaming mode.
- [ ] AC 3: After tool results are supplied, the API returns a final assistant message in streaming mode.
- [ ] AC 4: Cursor Agent can complete “list the files in this repo” through the tunnel using real tool activity, not hallucinated output.
- [ ] AC 5: Cursor Agent can complete “read go.mod and summarize the module + dependencies” through the tunnel using real tool activity, not hallucinated output.
- [ ] AC 6: Multi-step tool use with at least two sequential tool calls completes without the agent loop stalling.
- [ ] AC 7: Plain text Ask mode still works.
- [ ] AC 8: README documents Agent setup and validation prompts.
- [ ] AC 9: `go test ./...` passes.
- [ ] AC 10: `go vet ./...` passes.
- [ ] AC 11: `go build ./...` passes.
- [ ] AC 12: PR/manual validation documents cloudflared tunnel plus Cursor custom OpenAI API Agent prompts requiring file listing and `go.mod` reading, with final answers reflecting real repo data.

## Verification

The pipeline verified that branch `agent-codex-16-1782517637` was pushed before opening this draft PR. Review verification is posted in PR comments for each pipeline review iteration.

## Implementation Plan

1. Confirm the expected Codex Responses input shape for continuations in `internal/codex/builder.go`: preserve prior assistant function calls as Codex function/tool-call output items and map matching `role:"tool"` messages to function-call output items keyed by `tool_call_id`.
2. Extend `splitMessages` or replace it with a richer conversation builder in `internal/codex/builder.go` so it no longer skips `role:"tool"` messages. It should still extract system/developer text, preserve normal user/assistant text, include assistant `tool_calls` when content is null/empty, and attach tool results with their original `tool_call_id`.
3. Keep OpenAI parsing structs in `internal/openai/openai.go` mostly unchanged unless tests expose missing fields; current `ChatMessage.ToolCalls` and `ToolCallID` already support the issue’s request shape.
4. Add builder tests in `internal/codex/builder_test.go` for a continuation request containing user prompt, assistant `tool_calls`, and matching `role:"tool"` content. Assert the generated Codex payload includes both the prior call and the tool output, not a dropped tool message.
5. Add a multi-step builder test in `internal/codex/builder_test.go` with two assistant/tool-result pairs to prove ordering and call ID matching survive.
6. Add server non-streaming continuation coverage in `internal/server/server_test.go`: fake service receives messages including assistant `tool_calls` and `role:"tool"`, then returns final text with `finish_reason:"stop"` and no `tool_calls`.
7. Add server streaming continuation coverage in `internal/server/server_test.go`: fake stream returns text deltas after tool-result messages, final SSE chunk has `finish_reason:"stop"`, and no second `tool_calls` finish is emitted.
8. Add or adjust OpenAI parsing tests in `internal/openai/openai_test.go` only if needed to cover multiple tool calls, tool result content, and null assistant content.
9. Verify the default `faithful`/`prewarm` decision in `internal/server/server.go`: continuation requests from Cursor will likely include `tools`, so they use minimal mode by default. Ensure that mode is the one supporting continuation mapping.
10. Update `README.md` Cursor sections to describe Agent mode setup, HTTPS tunnel configuration, validation prompts, expected server log evidence, and known-good prompts for listing files, reading `go.mod`, and multi-step tool use.
11. Optionally update `docs/codex-tool-events.md` if continuation payload shape deserves separate documentation from outbound tool-call event parsing.
12. Run local validation: `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `go build ./...`.

## Branch

`agent-codex-16-1782517637`

## Review

This PR was generated by agent-pipeline-go (codex). The review loop runs against the acceptance criteria
above; each iteration's verdict is posted as a comment on this PR.

author: n-rodriguez
body:
The first three write operations the maintainer scoped into 1.0 (#6), built on the `OperationError` model (#12). Reviewed before opening — verdict **Ready: Yes**, no Critical/Important.

## New public surface

```crystal
client.add(dn, {"cn" => ["Alice"], "objectClass" => ["person", "top"]})   # §4.7
client.delete(dn)                                                          # §4.8
client.modify(dn, [                                                        # §4.6
  LDAP::Modification.replace("mail", "alice@example.com"),
  LDAP::Modification.delete("telephoneNumber"),   # whole attribute
  LDAP::Modification.add("objectClass", "person"),
])
```

- All three return `self` (chainable, like `authenticate`) on success.
- All three go through a new private `expect_result` helper: write → await the matching `*Response` → raise `OperationError` (carrying `result_code`/`matched_dn`/`error_message`) on a non-success code. Consistent with how `authenticate`/`search` already drive an operation.

## Modify input types

`LDAP::Modification` (a `struct`) + `LDAP::ModifyOperation` enum whose values **are** the wire ENUMERATED (`Add=0, Delete=1, Replace=2`, RFC 4511 §4.6). `delete`/`replace` accept zero values (RFC: removes the attribute — a typed splat needs ≥1 in Crystal, so they get an explicit zero-arg overload); `add` requires ≥1.

## Wire format (verified against RFC 4511 §4.6–4.8 / X.690)

- **DelRequest** is the RFC's **primitive** `[APPLICATION 10]` — the DN is the content itself, not a sequence (`set_string(dn, 10, Application)` → tag `0x4A`).
- **AddRequest** `{ entry, attributes SEQ OF { type, vals SET OF } }`.
- **ModifyRequest** `{ object, changes SEQ OF { operation ENUMERATED, { type, vals SET OF } } }`.

Builders compose only the existing `LDAP.app_sequence`/`LDAP.sequence`/`LDAP.set`/`BER#set_*` helpers — no hand-assembled tag/length bytes.

## Specs (TDD)

- **Byte-exact** `DelRequest` and a **byte-exact minimal `AddRequest`** (the latter computed by hand from the RFC, independent of the decoder — it pins the constructed `0x68` and SET `0x31` tags that decode-based checks can't isolate).
- Decode-based structure checks for the richer Add/Modify builders.
- Per op: success → `self`; failure → `OperationError` with the right `result_code`.
- `Modification` constructors + their enum mapping.

```
39 examples, 0 failures        # crystal spec
39 examples, 0 failures        # crystal spec -Dpreview_mt
```

Next: ModifyDN / Compare / Unbind. Refs #6.

author: erikfrey
body:
Update the Aloha cloth benchmark to use a diagonal dual-arm trajectory. The right arm now reaches across to grasp the opposite front-right corner while the left arm grabs the back-left corner, yanking and releasing the cloth to showcase self-collision and free-fall dynamics. Added checkerboard texture and material configurations to the cloth model.

Performance & Configuration Notes:
- Raised `nccdmax` from `1` to `256` in the benchmark configuration. The new diagonal yanking and dropping trajectory causes folding and self-collisions that generate significant CCD pairs. Setting it lower triggers CCD contact overflows during rollout.
- Baseline performance (with flat cloth and no control replay): 667.4 steps/second (solver iterations: 40.1 mean).
- New trajectory performance: 546.5 steps/second (solver iterations: 61.2 mean). The change is due to the increased complexity of solving the diagonal folding and self-collisions.
- Step time breakdown shows `flex_collision` remains the primary bottleneck (994.2ms out of 1829.2ms total step time, ~54.4%).

### Motivation

- Replace the prior service-secret authentication with using a Roblox account cookie so requests can be authenticated directly with Roblox credentials.
- Simplify CSRF handling when performing state-changing Roblox API calls to reduce fragile request replay logic.
- Provide usage docs and an environment example for easier local and hosted deployments.

### Description

- Removed `SERVICE_SECRET` and the `_require_secret` check and now read the Roblox account cookie from `X-Roblox-Cookie` or `ROBLOX_COOKIE` via a new `_cookie_from_request` helper.
- Updated `_headers` to accept the `request` and include the `.ROBLOSECURITY` cookie derived from the request or env and normalized to the raw cookie value.
- Rewrote `_request_with_csrf` to perform a single request, read the `X-CSRF-TOKEN` response header on failure, and retry with the token using `_request_json` instead of replaying raw requests and parsing headers manually.
- Removed secret requirement from `/ranks` and `/set-rank` handlers so they use the cookie-based auth, and left `health` returning the configured `GROUP_ID`.
- Added `README.md` with usage and API examples and a `.env.example` with `ROBLOX_COOKIE`, `ROBLOX_GROUP_ID`, and `PORT` settings.

### Testing

- No automated tests were added or run as part of this change.

author: mlcyclops
body:
## Feature

Adds **search and filter within folders** (roadmap increment #3).

- A debounced (~180ms) `<input type="search">` with a clear ("×") button in the sidebar header, styled to the dark violet theme.
- As you type, the folder tree and the unorganized-notebooks list filter **client-side, in memory** — no network, no persistence of the query.
- Matching is case-insensitive substring. A pure recursive predicate `nodeMatchesQuery(node, q, allFolders, notebooks)` returns true when the folder's own name matches, OR any notebook assigned to it matches, OR any descendant folder matches. It reuses the same `parentId` / `notebookIds` assignment logic the normal render uses.
- **Ancestor preservation:** because a folder renders whenever a descendant matches, the ancestors of a match stay visible (and expanded) so the match is reachable; non-matching siblings hide. A folder whose own name matches shows all its children.
- Empty/cleared query restores the full tree; a gentle **"No matches"** state appears when nothing matches.
- **Injection-safe highlighting:** matches are highlighted by escaping first (`escapeHtml`) and then wrapping the match in `<mark>` on the already escaped string — user text is never placed into innerHTML raw.
- **No data mutation:** filtering is purely visual and never mutates or re-persists stored folder data; drag-and-drop still operates on the real underlying data.

## ADR

`docs/adr/0005-search-and-filter-within-folders.md` (Accepted, 2026-06-26). Alternatives considered: server-side search (rejected — overkill, breaks offline-first) and fuzzy matching (deferred). ADR index and `PROGRESS.md` updated.

## Testing

- `node --check extension/content.js extension/background.js server.js` — all pass; `manifest.json` parses.
- Headless Chromium load via Playwright (persistent context, `--load-extension`): the MV3 service worker registers, no load errors.
- Node unit harness replicating the pure predicate + highlight logic — **16/16 assertions pass**: matches a folder by name, matches a nested notebook and keeps ancestors visible, hides non-matching branches, empty query returns everything, case-insensitive substring, and highlight output is escaped (fed a `<script>`-style name → no raw HTML, only `<mark>` wrappers).
- **Could not test (browser-gated):** live keystroke typing, debounce timing, and DOM rendering/drag-and-drop behaviour in a real NotebookLM page — these require an interactive browser session.

author: dhalperi
body:
A generic extended-community literal whose type octet has the high bit
set -- e.g. Junos "65000:672277L:36867" (type octet 0xFD) -- failed to
parse and was silently dropped. Two causes:

- parse() and of() assembled the type via signed-byte arithmetic, so a
  type or subtype octet >= 0x80 sign-extended to a negative int and was
  rejected. Mask each byte to its unsigned value.
- the constructor's VALID_TYPES allowlist rejected any type it did not
  specifically recognize. Extended communities observed on real devices
  may use experimental or vendor-specific types; model them as opaque
  values and let the type-specific predicates (isRouteTarget,
  isRouteOrigin, etc.) return false for unrecognized types. Only the
  single-byte type/subtype range is enforced now.

The Junos flatjuniper path previously fell back to a regex community
member for such literals, producing a FATAL convert warning on
"community add". It now parses as a literal extended community.

For batfish/batfish#10018.

author: robertwtucker
body:
Wave 2 PR-B of [v0.4 — make the silences loud](../blob/main/docs/design/2026-06-26-v0.4-scope-design.md). Both fixes live in `src/vault/projects.ts` and together make every Obsidian-canonical YAML shape for `area:` resolve to the same canonical form.

## What silences this PR ends

Before this PR, `find_project({area: 'Health'})` could return `[]` despite projects literally naming the area "Health" — because the `area:` value was written in a shape (unquoted wikilink, aliased wikilink) that the v0.3 normalization didn't anticipate. The project sat in the vault, invisible to the filter, with no signal that anything was wrong.

## Changes

**`a239b53` — #15: unquoted `area: [[Integration]]` is a YAML nested array, not a string.** Added `extractAreaString` helper that recognizes the single-element-nested-array shape js-yaml produces from unquoted `[[...]]` flow sequences and unwraps it. The strictness is deliberate — only the exact `[[Foo]]` shape unwraps, every other array shape still drops to `undefined`.

**`e1fb726` — #16: `normalizeArea` now collapses every wikilink shape to one canonical form.** Strip outer `[[ ]]`, prefer the alias when `[[Target|Alias]]` is present, fall back to the last path segment of the target when `[[Areas/Health]]` is used. Same normalization runs on both source values and query input, so the query side gets the same treatment.

Combined, the eight canonical shapes — Bare, Quoted, plus the four wikilink shapes in both unquoted and quoted form — all match a single canonical query.

## Test coverage

The parameterized area-shapes test (`test/vault/projects.test.ts`) now exercises all eight canonical shapes plus a dedicated alias-preference test. **93 tests pass** (was 92).

## Done criteria met

- [x] **#2 — Wikilink shapes verified.** All five shapes from the scope doc match `find_project({area: 'Health'})`.
- [x] **#3 — Unquoted-wikilink test added.** `area: [[Integration]]` bare unquoted is in the parameterized test fixture.

## Notes

- Both commits are atomic. #15's helper is independent of #16's normalizer rewrite — either could ship alone, but together they cover the full shape space.
- No public API change. `ProjectSummary.area` is still a `string | undefined`.
- The [[feedback-tools-vs-conventions|tools-vs-conventions]] principle is upheld — no new convention-encoding parameter shipped.

Closes #15, closes #16.

author: edweiss412
body:
## Problem

DXT-3 — the **final piece** of the untimed-Drive-read class (after export #128, files.get/list #132, asset byte-streams #136). Metadata reads off the onboarding scan path were unbounded (some also un-retried): a silent socket stall could hang an apply / cron pass.

## Fix

Each is now `withDriveRetry(() => client.X(params, { timeout: DRIVE_FILES_GET_TIMEOUT_MS, retry: false }))` — the DXT-1 gaxios-7 timeout pattern (a per-call timeout fires `AbortSignal.timeout` → `GaxiosError` `code: "TimeoutError"` → `driveErrorStatus` maps it to a transient 504 → `withDriveRetry` retries then throws typed; `retry: false` keeps `withDriveRetry` the single layer). The classifier is the one DXT-1 added — **client-agnostic**, so it works for the Sheets v4 client too.

**Sites bounded (5):** `verifyReelOnApply` `files.get` · cron `listSpreadsheetSheets` `spreadsheets.get` + `getSpreadsheetRevisionId` `revisions.list` · `applyStaged` `revisions.list` · **`sheetGids.ts` `fetchSheetTitleToGid` `spreadsheets.get`** (deep-link gid lookup, *on the onboarding scan path* — added by #134 after the initial enumeration and **caught in adversarial review**).

**Apply-path retry budget:** the two reads under the per-show advisory xact lock default to `maxRetries: 1` (≈16s worst/site) rather than the cron/scan default 3 (≈34s) — one retry covers a transient blip without holding the lock for the full budget.

**Testability:** `verifyReelOnApply.defaultDrive` + `applyStaged.defaultRetryEmbeddedRevisionAvailability` are now exported + injectable; cron + sheetGids tested via a googleapis-mock seam. 403/404/410 on `verifyReelOnApply` stay non-transient → propagate to drift handling.

## Contract updates (intent-preserving)

Wrapping `verifyReelOnApply`'s `.files.get` in a named `getFileMetadataCall` thunk shifted its `_scopeCheckContract` exemption key and the `_sharedDriveSupportContract` live-fixture self-test. The general `_sharedDriveSupportContract` arm still independently enforces `supportsAllDrives`.

## Review

4-lens workflow incl. a dedicated **contract-edit-integrity** skeptic. Found + fixed: the HIGH `sheetGids` miss, the MEDIUM apply-path retry budget, and per-site negative-test gaps. A class-sweep confirms the only remaining untimed Drive reads are `files.watch`/`channels.stop` in `lib/drive/watch.ts` (off all sync paths).

**This closes the entire untimed-Drive-read class.**

author: snacksin
body:
Fixes the pre-existing **Step 3** bug found during Step 4 testing (`task_85b3b3f5`) — it blocks ingest of any FicHub fic whose chapters carry per-chapter end-notes (common). Plan approved in plan mode. All in `epub.ts`, no migration/UI.

## Bug
`classifyByContent` (FicHub-gated) checked **"End Notes / Author's Notes → afterword" before "substantial prose → chapter."** So ~6000-word chapters that each end with an author's note were wholly demoted to `afterword`; every afterword takes `WRAPPER_NUMBER.afterword = -3`, so 2+ of them collide on `UNIQUE(work_id, number)` → the INSERT fails ("failed to record work") and the fic won't ingest. Reproducer `When_Harry_met_Wednesday_by_Jhotenko` had 3 chapters → `afterword(-3)` (`DUPLICATE numbers: [[-3, 3]]`).

## Fix
1. **Reorder `classifyByContent`** — the prose/heading chapter rule (`words >= 200 || "Chapter N" heading`) runs **before** the End-Notes rule, so a long chapter that merely ends with a note is a `chapter`; the afterword rule is left to genuinely note-only short items (reuses the existing 200-word threshold).
2. **Defense-in-depth** — in `parseEpub`'s finalize, before the chapter renumber, keep the first of each wrapper kind and **demote any later same-kind item to a chapter**, so a `UNIQUE(work_id, number)` collision is structurally impossible regardless of classification.

## Verification (trace harness + constructed EPUBs + the real reproducer)
- `pnpm check` → **0/0**; `pnpm build` clean (prod parity).
- **🔴 Reproducer ingests cleanly** via `/api/upload`: `status: created`, **30 chapters, 0 afterwords**, the 3 note-bearing items are real chapters; `npx tsx` trace shows **no duplicate numbers** (was `[[-3,3]]`).
- **Edge, both directions**: a long chapter ending in "Author's Notes" → `chapter`; a short standalone "End Notes" item → `afterword` (genuine end-notes still classify; the Step 3 8429-word "Sunday Kind of Love" stays a chapter via the same prose rule).
- **Defense-in-depth**: a FicHub fic with **two** end-notes items ingests cleanly — first stays `afterword`, second demoted to `chapter`, no UNIQUE failure.
- **No regression**: normal AO3 byte-identical (summary stays `summary`); Part A nav-skip and Part B title-split still work.
- DB backed up + restored around the upload tests; scratchpad harness cleaned up.

Not merging — Allie verifies (SHA on both refs). HANDOFF.md refreshed at closeout. After this: **MS Step 5** (verification + closeout).

author: robotsix-mill[bot]
body:
## Problem

The shared `docker-release.yml` reusable workflow (`.github/workflows/docker-release.yml`) is consumed by robotsix-chat, robotsix-cost-monitor, robotsix-calendar-agent, and robotsix-auto-mail to publish Docker images to GHCR. It builds and pushes images with SBOM/provenance attestation but performs **zero vulnerability scanning**.

Meanwhile, mill's own `docker-publish.yml` (which pushes to Docker Hub, not GHCR) includes comprehensive Trivy scanning:
- **Gate step**: Trivy table-format scan, `exit-code: 1`, `severity: CRITICAL`, `ignore-unfixed: true` — blocks the pipeline on critical fixable CVEs
- **SARIF step**: observability-only scan (all severities) with upload to GitHub Code Scanning

robotsix-auto-mail has worked around this gap by adding a separate `trivy` job in its own `release.yml` that scans the published image after `docker-release.yml` completes, plus a weekly `scan-container.yml` for rescans. robotsix-chat, robotsix-cost-monitor, and robotsix-calendar-agent have **no scanning at all** — they call `docker-release.yml` bare.

## Proposed fix

Add Trivy vulnerability scanning to `docker-release.yml` following the same pattern already proven in `docker-publish.yml`:

1. After the `docker/build-push-action` step, add a **gate scan**: Trivy table-format, `exit-code: 1`, `severity: CRITICAL`, `ignore-unfixed: true`
2. Add a **SARIF observability scan** (all severities, `if: always()`) with upload to Code Scanning via `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif`

This ensures every consumer gets automatic vulnerability scanning on every image publish, and makes auto-mail's post-publish workaround redundant.

## Consumer impact

- robotsix-auto-mail: can drop its separate `trivy` job from `release.yml` (the scan moves into the reusable workflow)
- robotsix-chat, robotsix-cost-monitor, robotsix-calendar-agent: gain vulnerability scanning automatically on next workflow reference update
- No workflow-call signature change needed (no new inputs) — the scan runs against the just-pushed image tag

author: alexmond
body:
Fourth slice of the **0.4.0 API freeze** (#500) — finishing **blocker 2** (after #513 removed the last `ApiException` leak).

## Why
The kubernetes-client `ApiClient` was exposed as a public `@Bean` and as a constructor param on `HelmKubeService` / `AsyncHelmKubeService` / `KubernetesClientProvider`, pinning the client major version into jhelm's public API.

## What (decided design: wrapper + customizer)
- New jhelm-owned **`KubeClient`** holder (`kube.service`) wraps the `ApiClient`; the client is reachable only via a **package-private** accessor — services in the package unwrap it, external code cannot.
- `JhelmKubeAutoConfiguration`: drop the public `ApiClient` `@Bean`; build the client in a private helper and expose a **`KubeClient` `@Bean`** instead. A consumer-supplied `ApiClient` is still honoured via an **`ObjectProvider<ApiClient>` override seam** (custom auth/transport keeps working), then wrapped.
- Service constructors take `KubeClient` instead of `ApiClient`.

`ApiClient` no longer appears in any public method/constructor/`@Bean` signature **except the single intentional override seam**.

## ⚠️ Breaking change
`HelmKubeService`/`AsyncHelmKubeService`/`KubernetesClientProvider` constructors take `KubeClient`, not `ApiClient`; the module exposes a `KubeClient` bean instead of an `ApiClient` bean. Supply a custom `ApiClient` `@Bean` to override.

## Verified
Full reactor green — **jhelm-kube 191, jhelm-cli 171, jhelm-rest 55** tests, 0 failures; PMD/Checkstyle clean.

## #500 status after this
Blocker 1 (throws Exception) ✅ · Blocker 2 (kube-client leak) ✅ · Blocker 3 (BouncyCastle) ✅ — **all three API-freeze blockers done.** Remaining #500 items are the High/Medium polish (immutable result models, typed `ReleaseContext`, `RepoManager` threading, enums).

author: jasonodoom
body:
Adds a static `ink` CLI verifier as the first increment of the Go second implementation (#186).

`go/cmd/ink` builds a single static binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, no Node or npm runtime) that verifies INK artifacts using the conformance-validated `go/ink` library. The command is layered so the verification logic is reusable by a later witness or inbound-verifier server:

- `cmd/ink/main.go` is a thin entry point.
- `go/internal/cli` parses arguments, reads the artifact JSON from `--file` or stdin under a 4 MiB cap, formats the result as JSON, and maps it to a process exit code.
- `go/internal/verify` holds the transport-neutral orchestration that calls the library verifiers.

Subcommands: `verify-card`, `verify-inclusion`, `verify-consistency`, `version`. The Merkle CLI inputs mirror the `merkle-inclusion` and `merkle-consistency` conformance vector shapes and are parsed strictly: pointer presence rejects a missing or null required field, unknown fields and duplicate keys and trailing data are rejected. The card path stays default-parse (ignore-unknown, last-wins) for parity with the TypeScript reference, which ignores unknown card keys.

Exit-code contract: `0` verified, `1` well-formed but rejected, `2` bad input or usage.

CI: the `go-conformance` job now builds the binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./cmd/ink`) and runs `gofmt -l` over the whole module.

Later increments (separate PRs): a `signature-verify` subcommand, then the witness HTTP server, then a server-side inbound verifier reusing `internal/verify`.

author: linyiru
body:
## What

`SourceMap::lookup_token` binary-searches a line's token slice for the
greatest token `<= (line, col)`. Every token in `lookup_table[line]` is built
to have `dst_line == line` (see `generate_lookup_table`), so searching the full
`(dst_line, dst_col)` tuple compares a component that is constant across the
slice on every probe. Searching `dst_col` alone is equivalent and avoids
building/comparing a tuple per step.

This is the per-token remapping hot path: bundlers call it once per token, per
chain link, when collapsing a sourcemap chain.

This PR:
- searches `dst_col` only in `lookup_token`;
- marks `lookup_token` `#[inline]` so it inlines into cross-crate callers;
- adds a `lookup_token` benchmark group — the existing `lookup_table` group only
  measured `generate_lookup_table` (table construction), not the lookups.

## Results

Microbench (`benches/simple.rs`, criterion, before → after):

| fixture | before | after | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lookup_token/real_small` | 21.67 ns | 14.00 ns | −35% |
| `lookup_token/real_medium` | 70.25 ns | 36.47 ns | −48% |
| `lookup_token/real_large` | 1.555 µs | 0.723 µs | −54% |
| `lookup_token/real_xlarge` | 54.06 µs | 25.68 µs | −52% |

End-to-end in rolldown (via a local `[patch.crates-io]`), `cargo bench -p bench`:

| bench | before | after | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sourcemap/collapse_codegen_chain` | 4.267 ms | 2.263 ms | **−47%** (p < 0.05) |
| `sourcemap/join_with_sourcemap` (control) | 571 µs | 582 µs | no change (p = 0.52) |
| `sourcemap/join_no_sourcemap` (control) | 43.5 µs | 43.4 µs | no change (p = 0.76) |

The two controls are untouched by this change, confirming the delta is isolated
to the lookup path.

## Correctness

`dst_line` is invariant within `lookup_table[line]`, so the tuple and
`dst_col`-only searches are equivalent (including the equal-key run handled by
`greatest_lower_bound`). All existing tests pass (`cargo test`), including
`lookup_token`, `lookup_with_duplicate_columns`, and `lookup_before_first_token`;
`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` is clean.

---

_Disclosure: this change was developed with AI assistance (Claude), and reviewed,
benchmarked, and verified by the author before submission._

author: srjadhikari
body:
Completes the Phase 3 backend (issue #5): the remaining course-domain services plus all HTTP endpoints (public catalog + admin CRUD), built TDD with a per-task review gate.

## What's included
- **Lesson service** — leaf CRUD; `createLesson` denormalizes `courseId` from its section; single `findByIdAndDelete` (no transaction).
- **Student service** — admin student management over `User`; list/get/update **scoped to `role:"student"`** (never resolves/modifies admins); password never exposed.
- **Public catalog** — `GET /api/courses` (published only, optional `?q=` text search), `GET /api/courses/:slug` (curriculum; never `videoKey`/`trailerKey`).
- **Admin routes** under `/api/admin` (router-level `authenticate` + `requireAdmin`):
  - Courses: `GET/POST /courses`, `GET/PATCH/DELETE /courses/:id` (incl. drafts; detail returns full curriculum)
  - Sections: `POST /courses/:courseId/sections`, `PATCH/DELETE /sections/:id`
  - Lessons: `POST /sections/:sectionId/lessons`, `PATCH/DELETE /lessons/:id`
  - Students: `GET /students`, `GET/PATCH /students/:id`
  - `DELETE /courses/:id` → **409** if enrollments exist; unauthenticated → **401**, non-admin → **403**.

## Architecture
- **Per-resource organization**: every resource has its own `*.service`, `*.controller`, and `*.routes`. `admin.routes` is a slim aggregator that applies the admin gate once, then composes the per-resource admin routers.
- **Controllers destructure `req.body` → explicit DTO** (never hand `req.body` to a service); params typed via `RequestHandler<{...}>`.
- REST nesting: nested on create (parent required to place the resource), flat on item ops (the resource's own id suffices).

## Testing
- **113 server tests pass** · `typecheck` · `lint` · `build` all green.
- Unit (service) + integration (Supertest route) coverage, incl. authz, the create flow + denormalization, validation 400, 409-if-enrolled, partial-update no-clobber, and student scoping.

## Deferred follow-ups (not blocking)
- `admin.routes.test.ts` sits at the 10/window `authLimiter` cap; next admin test that logs in should skip the limiter under test env (small, separate change).
- Phase-3 as-built docs back-fill rides the parked docs PR.

Part of #5.
